269.e: O Rama, scion of the Raghu dynasty  there at Pampa, by shooting an arrow at the choicest  fishes with a single bone, prawns and big fishes, crookedfaced fishes, fishes without scales and fins, baked on iron skewers and cooked will be offered to you by faithful Lakshmana.

269.sa: रोहितान्वक्रतुण्डांश्च नडमीनांश्च राघव।।3.73.14।। पम्पायामिषुभिर्मत्स्यांस्तत्र राम वरान्हतान्। निस्त्वक्पक्षानयस्तप्तानकृशानेककण्टकान्।।3.73.15।। तव भक्त्या समायुक्तो लक्ष्मणस्सम्प्रदास्यति।
269.e: O Rama, scion of the Raghu dynasty  there at Pampa, by shooting an arrow at the choicest  fishes with a single bone, prawns and big fishes, crookedfaced fishes, fishes without scales and fins, baked on iron skewers and cooked will be offered to you by faithful Lakshmana.

269.sa: भृशते खादतो मत्स्यान्पम्पायाः पुष्पसञ्चये।।3.73.16।। पद्मगन्धि शिवं वारि सुखशीतमनामयम्। उद्धृत्य सतताक्लिष्टं रौप्यस्फाटिकसन्निभम्।।3.73.17।। असौ पुष्करपर्णेन लक्ष्मणः पाययिष्यति।
269.e: While you delightedly eat the fishes, Lakshmana will fetch you water in a lotus leaf from the Pampa to drink. The waters of Pampa full of lotuses carry their scent, It  is enjoyable, cool, healthy and clear, resembling silver and crystal.

269.sa: भृशते खादतो मत्स्यान्पम्पायाः पुष्पसञ्चये।।3.73.16।। पद्मगन्धि शिवं वारि सुखशीतमनामयम्। उद्धृत्य सतताक्लिष्टं रौप्यस्फाटिकसन्निभम्।।3.73.17।। असौ पुष्करपर्णेन लक्ष्मणः पाययिष्यति।
269.e: While you delightedly eat the fishes, Lakshmana will fetch you water in a lotus leaf from the Pampa to drink. The waters of Pampa full of lotuses carry their scent, It  is enjoyable, cool, healthy and clear, resembling silver and crystal.

269.sa: स्थूलान्गिरिगुहाशय्यान्वराहान्वनचारिणः।।3.73.18।। अपां लोभादुपावृत्तान्वृषभानिव नर्दतः। रूपावनितांश्च पम्पायांद्रक्ष्यसि त्वं नरोत्तम।।3.73.19।।
269.e: O best of men you will see huge boars of delightful appearance that roar like bulls resting in mountain caves, roaming in the forest and coming to Pampa for its water.

269.sa: स्थूलान्गिरिगुहाशय्यान्वराहान्वनचारिणः।।3.73.18।। अपां लोभादुपावृत्तान्वृषभानिव नर्दतः। रूपावनितांश्च पम्पायांद्रक्ष्यसि त्वं नरोत्तम।।3.73.19।।
269.e: O best of men you will see huge boars of delightful appearance that roar like bulls resting in mountain caves, roaming in the forest and coming to Pampa for its water.

269.sa: सायाह्ने विचरन्राम विटपीन्माल्यधारिणः। शीतोदकं च पम्पाया दृष्ट्वा शोकं विहास्यसि।।3.73.20।।
269.e: When you stroll in the evening, you will see the trees laden with blossoms and lake Pampa full of cool water. You will forget your grief.

269.sa: सुमनोभिश्चितांस्तत्र तिलकान्नक्तमालकान्। उत्पलानि च फुल्लानि पङ्कजानि च राघव।।3.73.21।।
269.e: O son of the Raghus  there you will see tilaka trees, night jasmines full of flowers. You will also see blossoming water lilies and lotuses in Pampa.

269.sa: न तानि कश्चिन्माल्यानि तत्रारोपयिता नरः। न च वै म्लानतां यान्ति न च शीर्यन्ति राघव।।3.73.22।।
269.e: There is no one to wear those flowers. Those garlands do not wilt or wither O Rama

269.sa: मतङ्गशिष्यास्तत्राऽसन्नृषयस्सुसमाहिताः। तेषां भाराभितप्तानां वन्यमाहरतां गुरोः।।3.73.23।। ये प्रपेतुर्महीं तूर्णं शरीरात्स्वेदबिन्दवः। तानि जातानि माल्यानि मुनीनां तपसा तदा।।3.73.24।। स्वेदबिन्दुसमुत्थानि न विनश्यन्ति राघव।
269.e: While drops of sweat from the bodies of sage Matanga's disciples fell on earth under the heavy load of forest products they carried for their preceptor, they remained in a calm state. Those drops of sweat turned into flowers and those flowers do not wither due to the power of penance of the sages.

269.sa: मतङ्गशिष्यास्तत्राऽसन्नृषयस्सुसमाहिताः। तेषां भाराभितप्तानां वन्यमाहरतां गुरोः।।3.73.23।। ये प्रपेतुर्महीं तूर्णं शरीरात्स्वेदबिन्दवः। तानि जातानि माल्यानि मुनीनां तपसा तदा।।3.73.24।। स्वेदबिन्दुसमुत्थानि न विनश्यन्ति राघव।
269.e: While drops of sweat from the bodies of sage Matanga's disciples fell on earth under the heavy load of forest products they carried for their preceptor, they remained in a calm state. Those drops of sweat turned into flowers and those flowers do not wither due to the power of penance of the sages.

269.sa: तेषां गतानामद्यापि दृश्यते परिचारिणी।।3.73.25।। श्रमणी शबरी नाम काकुत्स्थ चिरजीविनी।
269.e: O Kakutstha  even now their attendant, named Sabari, an old ascetic is there even though they have left long ago.

269.sa: त्वां तु धर्मे स्थिता नित्यं सर्वभूतनमस्कृतम्।।3.73.26।। दृष्ट्वा देवोपमं राम स्वर्गलोकं गमिष्यति।
269.e: O Rama, she is established in righteousness, and you are godlike, and revered by all beings. When she sees you, she will attain heaven.

269.sa: ततस्तद्राम पम्पायास्तीरमासाद्य पश्चिमम्।।3.73.27।। आश्रमस्थानमतुलं गुह्यं काकुत्स्थ पश्यसि।
269.e: O Rama of the Kakutstha family, you will see on reaching the western bank of Pampa an incomparable site of hermitage concealed in a remote place.

269.sa: न तत्राक्रमितुं नागाश्शक्नुवन्ति तमाश्रमम्।।3.73.28।। विविधास्तत्र वै नागा वने तस्मिंश्च पर्वते। ऋषेस्तत्र मतङ्गस्य विधानात्तच्च काननम्।।3.73.29।।
269.e: The elephants of the forest and on the mountains do not attack the hermitage forbidden by sage Matanga.

269.sa: न तत्राक्रमितुं नागाश्शक्नुवन्ति तमाश्रमम्।।3.73.28।। विविधास्तत्र वै नागा वने तस्मिंश्च पर्वते। ऋषेस्तत्र मतङ्गस्य विधानात्तच्च काननम्।।3.73.29।।
269.e: The elephants of the forest and on the mountains do not attack the hermitage forbidden by sage Matanga.

269.sa: तस्मिन्नन्दनसङ्काशे देवारण्योपमे वने। नानाविहगसङ्कीर्णे रंस्यसे राम निर्वृतः।।3.73.30।।
269.e: O Rama, you will enjoy your stay in that forest which is like Nandana garden, the garden of the gods, full of various birds.

269.sa: ऋष्यमूकश्च पम्पायाः पुरस्तात्पुष्पितद्रुमः। सुदुःखारोहणो नाम शिशुनागाभिरक्षितः।।3.73.31।। उदारो ब्रह्मणा चैव पूर्वकाले विनिर्मितः।
269.e: Mount Rishyamuka situated on the bank of Pampa has trees filled with blossoms. It is difficult to climb and is protected by young elephants.This lofty mountain was created by Brahma in olden days.

269.sa: शयानः पुरुषो राम तस्य शैलस्य मूर्धनि।।3.73.32।। यत्स्वप्ने लभते वित्तं तत्प्रबुद्धोऽधिगच्छति।
269.e: Whatever wealth one dreams of in sleep on top of that mountain he will get on waking up, O Rama

269.sa: नत्वेनं विषमाचार पापकर्माऽधिरोहति।।3.73.33।। यस्तु तं विषमाचारः पापकर्माऽधिरोहति। तत्रैव प्रहऱन्त्येनं सुप्तमादाय राक्षसाः।।3.73.34।।
269.e: If an evildoer or a sinner ascends the (Rishyamuka) mountain, he, in his sleep, will be thrown down with asleep by the demons from there itself. A sinner does not climb this mountain of uneven terrain.

269.sa: नत्वेनं विषमाचार पापकर्माऽधिरोहति।।3.73.33।। यस्तु तं विषमाचारः पापकर्माऽधिरोहति। तत्रैव प्रहऱन्त्येनं सुप्तमादाय राक्षसाः।।3.73.34।।
269.e: If an evildoer or a sinner ascends the (Rishyamuka) mountain, he, in his sleep, will be thrown down with asleep by the demons from there itself. A sinner does not climb this mountain of uneven terrain.

269.sa: तत्रापि शिशुनागानामाक्रन्धश्श्रूयते महान्। क्रीडतां राम पम्पायां मतङ्गारण्यवासिनाम्।।3.73.35।।
269.e: O Rama, the trumpeting of the young playful elephants inhabiting sage Matanga's forest can be heard at Pampa.

269.sa: सिक्ता रुधिरधाराभिस्संहृत्य परमद्विपाः। प्रचरन्ति पृथक्कीर्णा मेघवर्णास्तरस्विनः।।3.73.36।।
269.e: The great, nimble elphants, dark like clouds, drenched with the flow of ichor come together and then separate and scatter.

269.sa: ते तत्र पीत्वा पानीयं विमलं शीतमव्ययम्। निर्वृतास्संविगाहन्ते वनानि वनगोचराः।।3.73.37।।
269.e: The wandering elephants of the forest drink plentiful water, pure and cool, from Pampa and contented, plunge into the forest.

269.sa: ऋक्षांश्च द्वीपिनश्चैव नीलकोमलकप्रभान्। रुरूनपेतापजयान् दृष्ट्वा शोकं जयिष्यसि।।3.73.38।।
269.e: When you see, shining like sapphires, the bears, tigers, antelopes who know no defeat, you will get over your grief.

269.sa: राम तस्य तु शैलस्य महती शोभते गुहा। शिलापिधाना काकुत्स्थ दुःखं चास्याः प्रवेशनम्।।3.73.39।।
269.e: O son of the Kakutstha family, there is a beautiful cave in that mountain covered with a slab of stone. It is difficult to enter.

269.sa: तस्या गुहायाः प्राग्द्वारे महान्शीतोदको ह्रदः। फलमूलान्वितो रम्यो नानामृगसमावृतः।।3.73.40।।
269.e: At the eastern entrance of the cave there is a cool watertank. On its bank teeming with various animals are delightful fruits and roots.

269.sa: तस्यां वसति सुग्रीवश्चतुर्भिस्सह वानरैः। कदाचिच्छिखरे तस्य पर्वतस्यावतिष्ठते।।3.73.41।।
269.e: Sugriva dwells in that cave with four other monkeys. At times he sits on the top of the mountain.

269.sa: कबन्धस्त्वनुशास्यैवं तावुभौ रामलक्ष्मणौ। स्रग्वी भास्करवर्णाभः खे व्यरोचत वीर्यवान्।।3.73.42।।
269.e: Having instructed both Rama and Lakshmana, courageous Kabandha, wearing a flowergarland, shone brightly like the Sun in the sky.

269.sa: तं तु खस्थं महाभागं कबन्धं रामलक्ष्मणौ। प्रस्थितौ त्वं व्रजस्वेति वाक्यमूचतुरन्तिके।।3.73.43।।
269.e: Both Rama and Lakshmana, ready to depart, went near the glorious Kabandha waiting in the sky and said, You may go now.

269.sa: गम्यतां कार्यसिद्ध्यर्थमिति तावब्रवीत्स च। सुप्रीतौ तावनुज्ञाप्य कबन्धः प्रस्थितस्तदा।।3.73.44।।
269.e: Then Kabandha said to the brothers satisfied, You may go now to accomplish your task. Then he took leave.

269.sa: स तत्कबन्धः प्रतिपद्य रूपं वृतश्श्रिया भास्करतुल्यदेहः। निदर्शयन्राममवेक्ष्य खस्थः सख्यं कुरुष्वेति तदाभ्युवाच।।3.73.45।।
269.e: Kabandha assumed his true form, his body shining like the radiance of the Sun. He stood in the sky showing his form and looking at Rama, said, Make friendship with Sugriva. इत्यार्ष श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये अरण्यकाण्डे त्रिसप्ततितमस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the seventythird sarga of Aranyakanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

270.sa: तौ कबन्धेन तं मार्गं पम्पाया दर्शितं वने। प्रतस्थतुर्दिशं गृह्य प्रतीचीं नृवरात्मजौ।।3.74.1।।
270.e: The two princes set forth in the western direction towards Pampa shown by Kabandha.

270.sa: तौ शैलेष्वाचितानेकान् क्षौद्रकल्पफलान्द्रुमान्। वीक्षन्तौ जग्मतुर्ध्रष्टुं सुग्रीवं रामलक्ष्मणौ।।3.74.2।।
270.e: Observing the trees loaded with honeysweet fruits on the mountain, Rama and Lakshmana   went to see Sugriva.

270.sa: कृत्वा च शैलपृष्ठे तु तौ वासं रामलक्ष्मणौ। पम्पायाः पश्चिमं तीरं राघवावुपतस्थतुः।।3.74.3।।
270.e: Rama and Lakshmana halted on the slope of the mountain and then departed for the western bank of Pampa.

270.sa: तौ पुष्करिण्याः पम्पायास्तीरमासाद्य पश्चिमम्। अपश्यतां ततस्तत्र शबर्या रम्यमाश्रमम्।।3.74.4।।
270.e: Both reached the west bank of lake Pampa and saw the delightful hermitage of Sabari.

270.sa: तौ तमाश्रममासाद्य द्रुमैर्बहुभीरावृतम्। सुरम्यमभिवीक्षन्तौ शबरीमभ्युपेयतुः।।3.74.5।।
270.e: Both reached the beautiful hermitage full of many kinds of trees. There they saw Sabari, and went towards her.

270.sa: तौ च दृष्ट्वा तदा सिद्धा समुत्थाय कृताञ्जलिः। रामस्य पादौ जग्राह लक्ष्मणस्य च धीमतः।।3.74.6।।
270.e: On seeing them both, Sabari, an accomplished ascetic, got up with folded hands and touched the feet of the sagacious Rama and Lakshmana.

270.sa: पाद्यमाचमनीयं च सर्वं प्रादाद्यथाविधि। तामुवाच ततो रामश्श्रमणीं संशितव्रताम्।।3.74.7।।
270.e: She offered them water to wash their feet and water to sip as per tradition. Then Rama spoke to Sabari who used to perform austere penance:

270.sa: कच्चित्ते निर्जिता विघ्नाः कच्चित्ते वर्धते तपः। कच्चित्ते नियतः क्रोध आहारश्च तपोधने।।3.74.8।।
270.e: O ascetic   hope you have overcome your obstacles to penance, you have controlled your anger and your desire for food. Is your austerity in progress.

270.sa: कच्चित्ते नियमाः प्राप्ताः कच्चित्ते मनसः सुखम्। कच्चित्ते गुरुशुश्रूषा सफला चारुभाषिणि।।3.74.9।।
270.e: O Sweettongued Sabari, have you achieved selfcontrol? Has your mind attained peace ? Have your services to the preceptor yielded results?

270.sa: रामेण तापसी पृष्टा सा सिद्धा सिद्धसम्मता। शशंस शबरी वृद्धा रामाय प्रत्युपस्थिता।।3.74.10।।
270.e: When Rama asked Sabari who was an old, accomplished ascetic adored by siddhas, she stood in front and replied :

270.sa: अद्य प्राप्ता तपस्सिद्धिस्तव संदर्शनान्मया। अद्य मे सफलं तप्तं गुरवश्च सुपूजिताः।।3.74.11।।
270.e: On seeing you now my penance has attained fulfilment, my services to my preceptors have borne fruit.

270.sa: अद्य मे सफलं जन्म स्वर्गश्चैव भविष्यति। त्वयि देववरे राम पूजिते पुरुषर्षभ।।3.74.12।।
270.e: O best of men, O highest of the gods my birth has become fruitful today with your worship, (you have made) even attainment of heaven quite certain.

270.sa: चक्षुषा तव सौम्येन पूतास्मि रघुनन्दन। गमिष्याम्यक्षयान्लोकांस्त्वत्प्रसादादरिन्दम।।3.74.13।।
270.e: O delight of the Raghus, your handsome look has sanctified me, O subduer of enemies, by your grace I will reach the inmperishable worlds.

270.sa: चित्रकूटं त्वयि प्राप्ते विमानैरतुलप्रभैः। इतस्ते दिवमारूढा यानहं पर्यचारिषम्।।3.74.14।।
270.e: The men I served have ascended heaven on aerial chariots of incomparable radiance the moment you touched Chitrakuta.

270.sa: तैश्चाहमुक्ता धर्मज्ञैर्महाभागैर्महर्षिभिः। आगमिष्यति ते रामस्सुपुण्यमिममाश्रमम्।।3.74.15।। स ते प्रतिग्रहीतव्यस्सौमित्रिसहितोतिथिः। तं च दृष्ट्वा वरान्लोकानक्षयांस्त्वं गमिष्यसि।।3.74.16।।
270.e: Those great honourable sages who knew the ways of dharma said: 'Rama would visit this sacred hermitage along with Lakshmana. He would be your guest. Receive him with due honour. And you would attain the great, inexhaustible worlds when you see him.'

270.sa: तैश्चाहमुक्ता धर्मज्ञैर्महाभागैर्महर्षिभिः। आगमिष्यति ते रामस्सुपुण्यमिममाश्रमम्।।3.74.15।। स ते प्रतिग्रहीतव्यस्सौमित्रिसहितोतिथिः। तं च दृष्ट्वा वरान्लोकानक्षयांस्त्वं गमिष्यसि।।3.74.16।।
270.e: Those great honourable sages who knew the ways of dharma said: 'Rama would visit this sacred hermitage along with Lakshmana. He would be your guest. Receive him with due honour. And you would attain the great, inexhaustible worlds when you see him.'

270.sa: मया तु विविधं वन्यं सञ्चितं पुरुषर्षभ। तवार्थे पुरुषव्याघ्र पम्पायास्तीरसम्भवम्।।3.74.17।।
270.e: O best among men I have collected and kept for your sake different kinds of forestfood grown on the bank of Pampa.

270.sa: एवमुक्तस्स धर्मात्मा शबर्या शबरीमिदम्। राघवः प्राह विज्ञाने तां नित्यमबहिष्कृताम्।।3.74.18।।
270.e: Entreated by her in that manner, the righteous Rama spoke to Sabari who was established in true knowledge:

270.sa: दनोस्सकाशात्तत्त्वेन प्रभावं ते महात्मनः। श्रुतं प्रत्यक्षमिच्छामि सन्द्रष्टुं यदि मन्यसे।।3.74.19।।
270.e: I have heard from great Danu about your power. If you agree, I would like to see this power in person.

270.sa: एतत्तु वचनं श्रुत्ता रामवक्त्राद्विनिस्सृतम्। शबरी दर्शयामास तावुभौ तद्वनं महत्।।3.74.20।।
270.e: At these words from the mouth of Rama, Sabari took them both round the great garden.

270.sa: पश्य मेघघनप्रख्यं मृगपक्षिसमाकुलम्। मतङ्गवनमित्येव विश्रुतं रघुनन्दन।।।3.74.21।।
270.e: O delight of the Raghus see this garden looking like the dense cloud. Full of animals and birds, it is popularly known as Matanga garden.

270.sa: इह ते भावितात्मानो गुरवो मे महावने। जुहवाञ्चक्रिरे तीर्थं मन्त्रवन्मन्त्रपूजितम्।।3.74.22।।
270.e: My precepters, who had perceived the Supreme Spirit made sacrificial offerings in this great garden, invoked gods through the power of mantras. They brought water and offered oblations to the sacrificial fire.

270.sa: इयं प्रत्यक्थ्सली वेदिर्यत्र ते मे सुसत्कृताः। पुष्पोपहारं कुर्वन्ति श्रमादुद्वेपिभिः करैः।।3.74.23।।
270.e: This is the altar named Pratyaksthali where the saints aged and exhausted( by performing chandrayana) whom I worshipped made offerings of flowers with trembling hands.

270.sa: तेषां तपःप्रभावेण पश्याद्यापि रघूद्वह। द्योतयन्ति दिशस्सर्वाश्श्रिया वेद्योऽतुलप्रभाः।।3.74.24।।
270.e: O Rama see, even now they illuminate the sacrificial altars with the power of their penance. They shed light in all directions with a matchless brilliance.

270.sa: अशक्नुवद्भिस्तैर्गन्तुमुपवासश्रमालसैः। चिन्तितेऽभ्यागतान्पश्य सहितान्सप्तसागरान्।।3.74.25।।
270.e: Look at the seven seas, which have reached here at their mere thought as they could not reach them due to fatigue from fasting.

270.sa: कृताभिषेकैस्तैर्न्यस्ता वल्कलाः पादपेष्विह। अद्यापि नावशुष्यन्ति प्रदेशे रघुनन्दन।।3.74.26।।
270.e: O delight of the Raghus  look at the bark robes spread on the trees to dry after their bathing which are still wet.

270.sa: देवकार्याणि कुर्वद्भिर्यानीमानि कृतानि वै। पुष्पैःकुवलयैस्सार्धं म्लानत्वं नोपयान्तिवै।।3.74.27।।
270.e: The flowers including lotuses offered by the sages while worshipping gods have not yet wilted.

270.sa: कृत्स्नं वनमिदं दृष्टं श्रोतव्यं च श्रुतं त्वया। तदिच्छाम्यभ्यनुज्ञाता त्यक्तुमेतत्कलेबरम्।।3.74.28।।
270.e: You have seen the entire garden and have listened what is to be heard. With your permission I would like to give up this body.

270.sa: तेषामिच्छाम्यहं गन्तुं समीपं भावितात्मनाम्। मुनीनामाश्रमो येषामहं च परिचारिणी।।3.74.29।।
270.e: I wish to reach those realisers of the Supreme Spirit whom I served and to whom this hermitage belonged.

270.sa: धर्मिष्ठं तु वचश्श्रुत्वा राघवस्सहलक्ष्मणः। प्रहर्षमतुलं लेभे आश्चर्यमिति तत्त्वतः।।3.74.30।।
270.e: Rama and Lakshmana on hearing the pious words of Savari joyfully exclaimed, This is really wonderful.

270.sa: तामुवाच ततो रामश्श्रमणीं संशितव्रताम्। अर्चितोऽहं त्वया भक्त्या गच्छकामं यथासुखम्।।3.74.31।।
270.e: Looking at Sabari who was steadfast in her vow, Rama said, O ascetic, you have worshipped me with devotion. You may go wherever you like (to the world you desire)

270.sa: इत्युक्ता जटिला वृद्धा चीरकृष्णाजिनाम्बरा। तस्मिन्मुहूर्ते शबरी देहं जीर्णं जिहासती।।3.74.32।। अनुज्ञाता तु रामेण हुत्वात्मानं हुताशने। ज्वलत्पावकसङ्काशा स्वर्गमेव जगाम सा।।3.74.33।।
270.e: With matted locks, tattered bark clothes and deer skin, Sabari consigned her old and emaciated body to the fire at that moment, with the permission of Rama and ascended to heaven, her body glowing like fire.

270.sa: इत्युक्ता जटिला वृद्धा चीरकृष्णाजिनाम्बरा। तस्मिन्मुहूर्ते शबरी देहं जीर्णं जिहासती।।3.74.32।। अनुज्ञाता तु रामेण हुत्वात्मानं हुताशने। ज्वलत्पावकसङ्काशा स्वर्गमेव जगाम सा।।3.74.33।।
270.e: With matted locks, tattered bark clothes and deer skin, Sabari consigned her old and emaciated body to the fire at that moment, with the permission of Rama and ascended to heaven, her body glowing like fire.

270.sa: दिव्याभरणसंयुक्ता दिव्यमाल्यानुलेपना। दिव्याम्बरधरा तत्र बभूव प्रियदर्शना।।3.74.34।। विराजयन्ती तं देशं विद्युत्सौदामिनी यथा।
270.e: Adorned with wonderful ornaments and beautiful garlands, anointed with fragrant unguents, robed in most beautiful clothes, she appeared like a streak of lightning, her body shining bright and her face contented.

270.sa: यत्र ते सुकृतात्मानो विहरन्ति महर्षयः।।3.74.35।। तत्पुण्यं शबरी स्थानं जगामात्मसमाधिना।
270.e: By virtue of her selfmeditation, Sabari went to that sacred world where the holy sages lived because of their good deeds. इत्यार्ष श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये अरण्यकाण्डे चतुस्सप्ततितमस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the seventyfourth sarga of Aranyakanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

271.sa: दिवं तु तस्यां यातायां शबर्यां स्वेन तेजसा। लक्ष्मणेन सह भ्रात्रा चिन्तयामास राघवः।।3.75.1।।
271.e: When Sabari departed for heaven with her brilliance, Rama  contemplated (about the power of sages)with Lakshmana.

271.sa: स चिन्तयित्वा धर्मात्मा प्रभावं तं महात्मनाम्। हितकारिणमेकाग्रं लक्ष्मणं राघवोऽब्रवीत्।।3.75.2।।
271.e: Thinking about the power of the great sages, righteous Rama said to Lakshmana,  his wellwisher with singleminded devotion:

271.sa: दृष्टोऽयमाश्रमस्सौम्य बह्वाश्चर्यो महात्मनाम्। विश्वस्तमृगशार्दूलो नानाविहगसेवितः।।3.75.3।।
271.e: O handsome one, we have seen this highly wonderful hermitage, where deer and tigers dwell together with mutual confidence, where birds of all kinds inhabit.

271.sa: सप्तानां च समुद्राणामेषु तीर्थेषु लक्ष्मण। उपस्पृष्टं च विधिवत्पितरश्चापि तर्पिताः।।3.75.4।।
271.e: O Lakshmana, having bathed in the waters of the seven seas (by taking ritualistic bath in these waters) the manes are offered oblations in accordance with tradition.

271.sa: प्रणष्टमशुभं तत्तत्कल्याणं समुपस्थितम्। तेन तत्त्वेन हृष्टं मे मनो लक्ष्मण सम्प्रति।।3.75.5।। हृदये हि नरव्याघ्र शुभमाविर्भविष्यति।
271.e: We have got rid of inauspicious time and good days have come. Therefore, I feel truly happy. Good fortune will appear (now), O Lakshmana, O tiger among men

271.sa: तदागच्छ गमिष्यामि पम्पां तां प्रियदर्शनाम्।।3.75.6।। ऋष्यमूको गिरिर्यत्र नातिदूरे प्रकाशते। यस्मिन्वसति धर्मात्मा सुग्रीवोंऽशुमतस्सुतः।।3.75.7।। नित्यं वालिभयात्त्रस्तश्चतुर्भिस्सह वानरैः।
271.e: Come, let us go to Pampa, which is pleasing to look at. Sugriva, the rigteous self, the son of the Sun has been staying for fear of Vali at the shining Rishyamuka, not far from here.

271.sa: तदागच्छ गमिष्यामि पम्पां तां प्रियदर्शनाम्।।3.75.6।। ऋष्यमूको गिरिर्यत्र नातिदूरे प्रकाशते। यस्मिन्वसति धर्मात्मा सुग्रीवोंऽशुमतस्सुतः।।3.75.7।। नित्यं वालिभयात्त्रस्तश्चतुर्भिस्सह वानरैः।
271.e: Come, let us go to Pampa, which is pleasing to look at. Sugriva, the rigteous self, the son of the Sun has been staying for fear of Vali at the shining Rishyamuka, not far from here.

271.sa: अभित्वरे च तं द्रष्टुं सुग्रीवं वानरर्षभम्।।3.75.8।। तदधीनं हि मे सौम्य सीतायाः परिमार्गणम्।
271.e: I am hastening to see that noble Sugriva the mighty monkey, as the search for Sita depends on him, O handsome one

271.sa: एवं ब्रुवाणं तं धीरं रामं सौमित्रिरब्रवीत्।।3.75.9।। गच्छावस्त्वरितं तत्र ममापि त्वरते मनः।
271.e: To the words of Rama who was of stable mind, Lakshmana replied : My mind too is hastening me. Let us get there quickly.

271.sa: आश्रमात्तु तत स्तस्मान्निष्क्रम्य स विशाम्पतिः।।3.75.10।। आजगाम ततः पम्पां लक्ष्मणेन सह प्रभुः।
271.e: Then Rama the lord of men along with Lakshmana departed from the hermitage and went to Pampa.

271.sa: स ददर्श ततः पुण्यामुदारजनसेविताम्।।3.75.11।। नानाद्रुमलताकीर्णां पम्पां पानीयवाहिनीम्। पद्मैस्सौगन्धिकैस्ताम्रां शुक्लां कुमुदमण्डलैः।।3.75.12।। नीलां कुवलयोद्घाटैर्बहुवर्णां कुथामिव।
271.e: He saw the sacred lake Pampa whose sweet flow of water was used by great seers. It abounded in trees and creepers. Its surface was red with lotuses at one place, white with clusters of lilies at another and with blue lotuses at other places. As such, it looked like a carpet with variegated colours.

271.sa: स तामासाद्य वै रामो दूरादुदकवाहिनीम्।।3.75.13।। मतङ्गसरसं नाम ह्रदं समवगाहत।
271.e: Rama reached the Matanga lake which he could see from  a distance and bathed in it.

271.sa: अरविन्दोत्पलवतीं पद्मसौगन्धिकायुताम्।।3.75.14।। पुष्पिताम्रवणोपेतां बर्हिणोद्घुष्टनादिताम्। तिलकैर्बीजपूरैश्च धवैश्शुक्लद्रुमैस्तथा।।3.75.15।। पुष्पितैः करवीरैश्च पुन्नागैश्च सुपुष्पितैः। मालतीकुन्दगुल्मैश्च भाण्डीरैर्निचुलैस्तथा।।3.75.16।। अशोकैस्सप्तपर्णैश्च केतकैरतिमुक्तकैः। अन्यैश्च विविधैर्वृक्षैः प्रमदामिव भूषिताम्।।3.75.17।। समीक्षमाणौ पुषपाढ्यं सर्वतो विपुलद्रुमम्। कोयष्टिकैश्चार्जुनकैश्शतपत्रैश्च कीरकैः।।3.75.18।। एतैश्चान्यैश्च विहगैर्नादितं तु वनं महत्। ततो जग्मतुरव्यग्रौ राघवौ सुसमाहितौ।।3.75.19।। तद्वनं चैव सरसः पश्यन्तै शकुनैर्युतम्।
271.e: Lake Pampa was filled with red lotuses and their fragrance.The bank was lined with blossoming mango trees and trees of several kinds like tilaka trees with fruits full of seeds like citron, dhava trees, white trees in bloom, karavira trees loaded with flowers, punnaga trees, clusters of jasmine and kunda shrubs, fig trees, so also reeds, ashoka trees, atimuktaka creepors and several other trees looking like women adorned all over. Rama and Lakshmana passed by, glancing at them. There were other trees full of flowers, huge trees, koyashtika trees with reed. Different kinds of birds such as peacocks, parrots, dwelling in the forest were screaming aloud. Looking at all these in that forest Rama and Lakshmana passed by undisturbed with a composed mind.

271.sa: स ददर्श ततः पम्पां शीतवारिनिधिं शुभाम्।।3.75.20।। तिलकाशोकपुन्नागवकुलोद्दालकाशिनीम्।
271.e: Rama saw lake Pampa with cool waters and the groves on the bank filled with tilaka, ashoka, punnaga, bakula and uddala trees.

271.sa: स रामो विविधान्वृक्षान्सरांसि विविधानि च।।3.75.21।। पश्यन्कामाभिसन्तप्तो जगाम परमं ह्रदम्।
271.e: On seeing different kinds of trees and tanks, the lovestriken Rama visited that great lake.

271.sa: पुष्पितोपवनोपेतां सालचम्पकशोभिताम्।।3.75.22।। षट्पदौघसमाविष्टां श्रीमतीमतुलप्रभाम्। स्फटिकोपमतोयाढ्यां श्लक्ष्णवालुकसन्तताम्।।3.75.23।। स तां दृष्ट्वा पुनः पम्पां पद्मसौगन्घिकैर्युताम्। इत्युवाच तदा वाक्यं लक्ष्मणं सत्यविक्रमः।।3.75.24।।
271.e: There were lovely pleasuregardens in full bloom  filled with sal and champk trees. Honeybees on flowers looked lovely and bright. The waters were crystalclear and fragrant with lotuses.The soft sands on the banks of Pampa gleamed. Rama saw them again and again and described them to Lakshmana.

271.sa: पुष्पितोपवनोपेतां सालचम्पकशोभिताम्।।3.75.22।। षट्पदौघसमाविष्टां श्रीमतीमतुलप्रभाम्। स्फटिकोपमतोयाढ्यां श्लक्ष्णवालुकसन्तताम्।।3.75.23।। स तां दृष्ट्वा पुनः पम्पां पद्मसौगन्घिकैर्युताम्। इत्युवाच तदा वाक्यं लक्ष्मणं सत्यविक्रमः।।3.75.24।।

271.sa: अस्यास्तीरे तु पूर्वोक्तः पर्वतो धातुमण्डितः। ऋष्यमूक इति ख्यातः पुण्यः पुष्पितपादपः।।3.75.25।।
271.e: The famous mount, sacred Rishyamuka is situated on the bank of Pampa full of blossoming trees.

271.sa: हरेः ऋक्षरजोनाम्नः पुत्रस्तस्य महात्मनः। अध्यास्ते तं महावीर्यस्सुग्रीव इति विश्रुतः।।3.75.26।।
271.e: The mighty son of Riksharaja, the great soul, the Sun whose son was the wellknown Sugriva, resides on this mountain.

271.sa: सुग्रीवमभिगच्छ त्वं वानरेन्द्रं नरर्षभ। इत्युवाच पुनर्वाक्यं लक्ष्मणं सत्यविक्रमम्।।3.75.27।।
271.e: Rama said to Lakshmana, the best of men, who had truth as his strength, Go to Sugriva, lord of the monkeys.

271.sa: राज्यभ्रष्टेन दीनेन तस्यामासक्तचेतसा। कथं मया विना शक्यं सीतां लक्ष्मण जीवितुम्।।3.75.28।।
271.e: O Lakshmana, deprived of the kingdom I have become a destitute. With my heart attached to Sita how can I live without her ?

271.sa: इत्येवमुक्त्वा मदनाभिपीडितः स लक्ष्मणं वाक्यमनन्यचेतसम्। विवेश पम्पां नलिनीं मनोरमां रघूत्तमश्शोकविषादयन्त्रितः।।3.75.29।।
271.e: Having said these words to Lakshmana who was listening to him with undivided attention, Rama, the best of the Raghus, oppressed by love and afflicted by tears of grief entered Pampa, the delightful lotuslake.

271.sa: ततो महद्वर्त्म सुदूरसङ्क्रमं क्रमेण गत्वा प्रविलोकयन्वनम्। ददर्श पम्पां शुभदर्शकाननामनेकनानाविधपक्षिजालकाम्।।3.75.30।।
271.e: Thereafter, going slowly to a distance, Rama and Lakshmana saw Pampa surrounded by beautiful forests full of many varieties of birds. इत्यार्ष श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये अरण्यकाण्डे पञ्चसप्ततिमस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the seventyfifth sarga of Aranyakanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

272.sa: स तां पुष्करिणीं गत्वा पद्मोत्पलझषाकुलाम्। रामस्सौमित्रि सहितो विललापाकुलेन्द्रियः।।4.1.1।।
272.e: Arriving with Laksmana at the lake filled with lotuses, lilies and fishes, Rama, his senses oppressed, burst into tears.

272.sa: तस्य दृष्ट्वैव तां हर्षादिन्द्रियाणि चकम्पिरे। स कामवशमापन्नस्सौमित्रिमिदमब्रवीत्।।4.1.2।।
272.e: He was glad to see it but sad at the thought of Sita. His passion stirred, his senses shaken, he said this to Saumitri:

272.sa: सौमित्रे शोभते पम्पा वैदूर्यविमलोदका। फुल्लपद्मोत्पलवती शोभिता विविधैर्द्रुमैः।।4.1.3।।
272.e: 'O Saumitri Pampa looks beautiful with its water clear as vaidurya, its lilies and lotuses in full bloom and its trees in all their variety.

272.sa: सौमित्रे पश्य पम्पायाः काननं शुभदर्शनम्। यत्र राजन्ति शैला वा द्रुमास्सशिखरा इव।।4.1.4।।
272.e: 'O Saumitri look at the pleasant forest around Pampa where trees stand splendid like mountainpeaks.

272.sa: मां तु शोकाभिसन्तप्तं माधवः पीडयन्ति वै। भरतस्य च दुःखेन वैदेह्या हरणेन च।।4.1.5।।
272.e: Already saddened due to the abduction of Sita and plight of Bharata, I am tormented by Spring.

272.sa: शोकार्तस्यापि मे पम्पा शोभते चित्रकानना। व्यवकीर्णा बहुविधैः पुष्पैश्शीतोदका शिवा।।4.1.6।।
272.e: Though stricken with grief, I feel so delighted to see the auspicious Pampa with its wonderful forest and cool water scattered with flowers.

272.sa: नलिनैरपि सञ्छन्ना ह्यत्यर्थशुभदर्शना। सर्पव्यालानुचरिता मृगद्विजसमाकुला।।4.1.7।।
272.e: Abounding in lotuses, birds and beasts and vicious serpents moving about, it looks splendid indeed.

272.sa: अधिकं प्रविभात्येतन्नीलपीतं तु शाद्वलम्। द्रुमाणां विविधैः पुष्पैः परिस्तोमैरिवार्पितम्।।4.1.8।।
272.e: The bluishyellow grass, dotted with different kinds of flowers fallen from the trees shines like a carpet spread.

272.sa: पुष्पभारसमृद्धानि शिखराणि समन्ततः। लताभिः पुष्पिताग्राभिरुपगूढानि सर्वशः।।4.1.9।।
272.e: Entwined with flowering creepers the treetops are covered all over with rich loads of flowers.

272.sa: सुखानिलोऽयं सौमित्रे कालः प्रचुरमन्मथः। गन्धवान्सुरभिर्मासो जातपुष्पफलद्रुमः।।4.1.10।।
272.e: 'O Saumitri it is the season of spring. The trees are laden with fruits and fragrant flowers. Ecstatic blows the gentle freeze.

272.sa: पश्य रूपाणि सौमित्रे वनानां पुष्पशालिनाम्। सृजतां पुष्पवर्षाणि तोयं तोयमुचामिव।।4.1.11।।
272.e: 'Look at the flowering trees sending showers of flowers like water dropping from the clouds, O Saumitri

272.sa: प्रस्तरेषु च रम्येषु विविधाः काननद्रुमाः। वायुवेगप्रचलिताः पुष्पैरवकिरन्ति गाम्।।4.1.12।।
272.e: Various forest trees shaken by the force of the wind scatter flowers on the beautiful rocky surface of earth.

272.sa: पतितैः पतमानैश्च पादपस्थैश्च मारुतः। कुसुमैः पश्य सौमित्रे क्रीडन्निव समन्ततः।।4.1.13।।
272.e: O Saumitri! look, the breeze appears to be playing with the flowers; that are fallen and that are still on the trees.

272.sa: विक्षिपन्विविधाश्शाखा नगानां कुसुमोत्कचाः। मारुतश्चलितस्थानैष्षट्पदैरनुगीयते।।4.1.14।।
272.e: "As the wind shakes the flowers off the branches of various trees the bees bumble in tune with the (whistling) wind.

272.sa: मत्तकोकिलसन्नादैर्नर्तयन्निव पादपान्। शैलकन्दरनिष्क्रान्तः प्रगीत इव चानिलः।।4.1.15।।
272.e: "As if the trees are dancing to the music of the cuckoos and to the sound of the wind coming out of the mountain-caves.

272.sa: तेन विक्षिपताऽत्यर्थं पवनेन समन्ततः। अमी संसक्तशाखाग्रा ग्रथिता इव पादपाः।।4.1.16।।
272.e: "Shaken by the strong wind all over, the tops of trees look as if they are knitted together.

272.sa: स एष सुखसंस्पर्शो वाति चन्दनशीतलः। गन्धमभ्यवहन्पुण्यं श्रमापनयनोऽनिलः।।4.1.17।।
272.e: 'The gentle touch of the breeze that blows, cool like sandalwood, full of pure fragrance, takes away the fatigue of the body.

272.sa: अमी पवनविक्षिप्ता विनदन्तीव पादपाः। षट्पदैरनुकूजन्तो वनेषु मधुगन्धिषु।।4.1.18।।
272.e: As if the trees are singing, swayed by the wind, while the bees in the forest, fragrant with honey, hum in tune.

272.sa: गिरिप्रस्थेषु रम्येषु पुष्पवद्भिर्मनोरमैः। संसक्तशिखराश्शैला विराजन्ते महाद्रुमैः।।4.1.19।।
272.e: 'The huge trees in the scenic mountainranges look delightful with their blossoms touching the peaks.

272.sa: पुष्पसञ्छन्नशिखरा मारुतोत्क्षेपचञ्चलाः। अमी मधुकरोत्तंसाः प्रगीता इव पादपाः।।4.1.20।।
272.e: With the tops of trees covered with flowers, the black bees hovering (humming) over them, the trees, shaken by the restless wind look like singers. (The trees with the top decked with flowers, the bees like black hair on the head swaying in the wind look like dancing and singing)

272.sa: सुपुष्पितांस्तु पश्येमान्कर्णिकारांत्समन्ततः। हाटकप्रतिसञ्छन्नान्नरान्पीताम्बरानिव।।4.1.21।।
272.e: 'See these Karnikaras in full bloom all over, looking like people clad in yellow silk adorned with golden ornaments.

272.sa: अयं वसन्तस्सौमित्रे नानाविहगनादितः। सीतया विप्रहीनस्य शोकसन्दीपनो मम।।4.1.22।।
272.e: 'O Saumitri this spring season resonating with the sounds of several kinds of birds, kindles my anguish as I am separated from Sita.

272.sa: मां हि शोकसमाक्रान्तं सन्तापयति मन्मथः। हृष्टः प्रवदमानश्च ममाह्वयति कोकिलः।।4.1.23।।
272.e: 'Kandarpa (Cupid) torments me while I am already griefstricken. The Cuckoo with his challenging cheerfulness mocks me.

272.sa: एष दात्यूहको हृष्टो रम्ये मां वननिर्झरे। प्रणदन्मन्मथाविष्टं शोचयिष्यति लक्ष्मण।।4.1.24।।
272.e: 'Lakshmana, while I am already lovestricken, the swamphen (gallinule, a marshbird) troubles me with its joyous cackles in the beautiful foreststream.

272.sa: श्रुत्वैतस्य पुरा शब्दमाश्रमस्था मम प्रिया। मामाहूय प्रमुदिताः परमं प्रत्यनन्दत।।4.1.25।।
272.e: 'While in the hermitage in the past, my beloved was very glad to hear such sounds, invite me to join her and rejoice again.

272.sa: एवं विचित्राः पतगा नानारावविराविणः। वृक्षगुल्मलताः पश्य सम्पतन्ति समन्ततः।।4.1.26।।
272.e: 'See, the different kinds of birds flying towards trees, shrubs and vines making wonderful sounds all over.

272.sa: विमिश्रा विहगाः पुम्भिरात्मव्यूहाभिनन्दिताः। भृङ्गराजप्रमुदितास्सौमित्रे मधुरस्वनाः।।4.1.27।।
272.e: 'O Lakshmana the female birds praised by their flocks, are united with their male partners. Enjoying the sweet sounds of large black bees, they are singing melodiously.

272.sa: दात्यूहरतिविक्रन्दैः पुंस्कोकिलरुतैरपि। स्वनन्ति पादपाश्चेमे ममानङ्गप्रदीपनाः।।4.1.28।।
272.e: These trees seem to enkindle my passion through all sorts of sounds like the loud cackle of swamphens and the sweet warble of the male cuckoos.

272.sa: अशोकस्तबकाङ्गारष्षट्पदस्वननिःस्वनः। मां हि पल्लवताम्रार्चिर्वसन्ताग्निः प्रधक्ष्यति।।4.1.29।।
272.e: 'The fire of spring with clusters of Asoka flowers as its charcoal, its coppercoloured tender leaves as flames, the buzz of bees as its crackle will, as if, consume me.

272.sa: न हि तां सूक्ष्मपक्ष्माक्षीं सुकेशीं मृदुभाषिणीम्। अपश्यतो मे सौमित्रे जीवितेऽस्ति प्रयोजनम्।।4.1.30।।
272.e: 'O Saumitri my life is meaningless if I cannot see my beloved Sita with her delicate eyelashes, beautiful locks of hair and her sweet voice.

272.sa: अयं हि दयितस्तस्याः कालो रुचिरकाननः। कोकिलाकुलसीमान्तो दयिताया ममानघ।।4.1.31।।
272.e: 'O sinless one, the spring season is dear to my beloved Sita when the outskirts of the forest are filled with voices of the cockoo.

272.sa: मन्मथाऽयाससम्भूतो वसन्तगुणवर्धितः। अयं मां धक्ष्यति क्षिप्रं शोकाग्निर्नचिरादिव।।4.1.32।।
272.e: 'The fire of grief ignited by Kandarpa (the god of love), enhanced by the effects of spring will certainly consume me soon.

272.sa: अपश्यतस्तां दयितां पश्यतो रुचिरद्रुमान्। ममायमात्मप्रभवो भूयस्त्वमुपयास्यति।।4.1.33।।
272.e: 'Unable to see my beloved wife, the very sight of these lovely trees intensifies my love for her who shines resplendent in me.

272.sa: अदृश्यमाना वैदेही शोकं वर्धयते मम। दृश्यमानो वसन्तश्च स्वेदसंसर्गदूषकः।।4.1.34।।
272.e: 'When in place of Vaidehi I see spring (with its cool breeze) that used to take away the sweat generated by sensual enjoyment, my sorrow is intensified.

272.sa: मां ह्यद्य मृगशाबाक्षी चिन्ताशोकबलात्कृतम्। सन्तापयति सौमित्रे क्रूरश्चैत्रवनानिलः।।4.1.35।।
272.e: 'O Saumitri the cruel breeze of the spring forest torments me as I am now immersed in grief in the absence of my fawneyed beloved.

272.sa: अमी मयूराश्शोभन्ते प्रनृत्यन्तस्ततस्ततः। स्वैः पक्षैः पवनोद्धूतैर्गवाक्षैः स्फाटिकैरिव।।4.1.36।।
272.e: 'Delightful are the peacocks dancing here and there, their feathers looking like crystal windows flung open by the wind.

272.sa: शिखिनीभिः परिवृतास्ते एते मदमूर्छिताः। मन्मथाभिपरीतस्य मम मन्मथवर्धनाः।।4.1.37।।
272.e: 'The peacocks intoxicated with passion for the peahens surround them intensifying my longing (for Vaidehi).

272.sa: पश्य लक्ष्मण नृत्यन्तं मयूरमुपनृत्यति। शिखिनी मन्मथार्तैषा भर्तारं गिरिसानुनि।।4.1.38।।
272.e: 'Look at the lovelorn peahen, excited by love, dancing on the moutain slope, O Lakshmana  Engrossed in love, she dances for wooing the peacock.

272.sa: तामेव मन्मथाविष्टो मयूरोऽप्युपधावति। वितत्य रुचिरौ पक्षौ रुतैरुपहसन्निव।।4.1.39।।
272.e: 'Overwhelmed with love, the enchanted peacock, spreading his wings is running after her, making sounds, as though mocking her.

272.sa: मयूरस्य वने नूनं रक्षसा न हृता प्रिया। तस्मान्नृत्यति रम्येषु वनेषु सह कान्तया।।4.1.40।।
272.e: 'The peacock's beloved, for sure, has not been abducted by the demon. Therefore, he is dancing in delight in the forest in the company of his beloved.

272.sa: मम त्वयं विना वासः पुष्पमासे सुदुस्सहः। पश्य लक्ष्मण संरागः तिर्यग्योनिगतेष्वपि। यदेषा शिखिनी कामाद्भर्तारं रमतेऽन्तिके।।4.1.41।।
272.e: 'It is extremely unbearable for me to stay in the forest during this season of flowers (Spring). Look at the passion even among beasts and birds, O Lakshmana And craving for love, the peahen sports near her mate.

272.sa: मामप्येवं विशालाक्षी जानकी जातसम्भ्रमा। मदनेनाभिवर्तेत यदि नाऽपहृता भवेत्।।4.1.42।।
272.e: 'Had the largeeyed Janaki not been stolen, she would have also paid advances to me in this manner with all her love and excitement.

272.sa: पश्य लक्ष्मण पुष्पाणि निष्फलानि भवन्ति मे। पुष्पभारसमृद्धानां वनानां शिशिरात्यये।।4.1.43।।
रुचिराण्यपि पुष्पाणि पादपानामतिश्रिया। निष्फलानि महीं यान्ति समं मधुकरोत्करैः।।4.1.44।।
272.e: 'The trees look enchanting with flowers in full bloom, with bees hovering over them. But the flowers fruitlessly drop down on the ground.

272.sa: नदन्ति कामं शकुना मुदितास्सङ्घशः कलम्। आह्वयन्त इवान्योन्यं कामोन्मादकरा मम।।4.1.45।।
वसन्तो यदि तत्रापि यत्र मे वसति प्रिया। नूनं परवशा सीता सापि शोचत्यहं यथा।।4.1.46।।
272.e: 'If spring reigns wherever my beloved Sita is, she must have been overwhelmed with similar sad feelings like me.

272.sa: नूनं न तु वसन्तोऽतं देशं स्पृशति यत्र सा। कथं ह्यसितपद्माक्षी वर्तयेत्सा मया विना।।4.1.47।।
272.e: 'Spring must not have touched the place where she is now staying. Otherwise how could my Sita with eyes like blue lotus live without me?

272.sa: अथवा वर्तते तत्र वसन्तो यत्र मे प्रिया। किं करिष्यति सुश्रोणी सा तु निर्भर्त्सिता परैः।।4.1.48।।
272.e: 'Or, if there is spring where my beloved lives, what can that lady of beautiful hips do, threatened by enemies.

272.sa: श्यामा पद्मपलाशाक्षी मृदुपूर्वाभिभाषिणी। नूनं वसन्तमासाद्य परित्यक्ष्यति जीवितम्।।4.1.49।।
272.e: 'Eager to speak with her gentle voice, my young beloved, blessed with eyes like lotus petals, will certainly give up her life, unable to enjoy the spring.

272.sa: दृढं हि हृदये बुद्धिर्मम सम्परिवर्तते। नालं वर्तयितुं सीता साध्वी मद्विरहं गता।।4.1.50।।
272.e: 'My mind makes me feel certain that Sita with her chastity might not be able to live separated from me.

272.sa: मयि भावस्तु वैदेह्यास्तत्त्वतो विनिवेशितः। ममापि भावस्सीतायां सर्वथा विनिवेशितः।।4.1.51।।
272.e: 'Sita has her love truly fixed in me. My love for her is equally steadfast.

272.sa: एष पुष्पवहो वायुस्सुखस्पर्शो हिमावहः। तां विचिन्तयतः कान्तां पावकप्रतिमो मम।।4.1.52।।
272.e: 'This cool breeze that carries the fragrance of flowers, that is gentle in its touch feels like fire when I think about my beautiful beloved.

272.sa: सदा सुखमहं मन्ये यं पुरा सह सीतया। मारुतस्स विना सीतां शोकं वर्धयते मम।।4.1.53।।
272.e: 'The pleasant touch of the wind, which made me happy in the company of Sita intensifies my grief now in her absence.

272.sa: तां विना विहङ्गो यः पक्षी प्रणदितस्तदा। वायसः पादपगतः प्रहृष्टमभिनर्दति।।4.1.54।।
272.e: 'The crow that cried unhappily flying in the sky as if to foretell my separation from Sita, is now on the tree, singing joyfully (suggesting my possible union with Sita).

272.sa: एष वै तत्र वैदेह्या विहगः प्रतिहारकः। पक्षी मां तु विशालाक्ष्यास्समीपमुपनेष्यति।।4.1.55।।
272.e: 'The same crow attendant on Vaidehi there will take me to my largeeyed beloved.

272.sa: शृणु लक्ष्मण सन्नादं वने मद्विवर्धनम्। पुष्पिताग्रेषु वृक्षेषु द्विजानामुपकूजताम्।।4.1.56।।
272.e: 'Losten, O Lakshmana to the sweet warblings of the birds on the blossoming treetops of the forest. My love for her (Sita) enhances with their sweet voices.

272.sa: विक्षिप्तां पवनेनैतामसौ तिलकमञ्जरीम्। षट्पदस्सहसाऽभ्येति मदोद्धूतामिव प्रियाम्।।4.1.57।।
272.e: 'This honeybee is eager to approach the bunch of tilaka flowers in bloom scattered by the wind like a lover advancing towards his passionate beloved.

272.sa: कामिनामयमत्यन्तमशोकश्शोकवर्धनः। स्तबकैः पवनोत्क्षिप्तैस्तर्जयन्निव मां स्थितः।।4.1.58।।
272.e: 'This asoka tree increases (by nature) the sorrow of lovers. Perhaps it make its presence felt in order to intimidate me with the clusters of its flowers scattered by the wind.

272.sa: अमी लक्ष्मण दृश्यन्ते चूताः कुसुमशालिनः। विभ्रमोत्सिक्तमनसः साङ्गरागा नरा इव।।4.1.59।।
272.e: 'O Lakshmana these mangotrees full of blossoms appear like sexited men who have applied fragrant unguents to their bodies.

272.sa: सौमित्रे पश्य पम्पायाश्चित्रासु वनराजिषु। किन्नरा नरशार्दूल विचरन्ति ततस्ततः।।4.1.60।।
272.e: 'O Saumitri O' tiger among men look at the kinnaras wandering here and there, in the wonderful forest around the Pampa lake.

272.sa: इमानि शुभगन्धीनि पश्य लक्ष्मण सर्वशः। नलिनानि प्रकाशन्ते जले तरुणसूर्यवत्।।4.1.61।।
272.e: 'O Lakshmana look at these lotuses with fine fragrance all over the water glowing like the rising Sun.

272.sa: एषा प्रसन्नसलिला पद्मनीलोत्पलायुता। हंसकारण्डवाकीर्णा पम्पा सौगन्धिकान्विता।।4.1.62।।
272.e: 'This Pampa with its water clear and fragrant with red and blue lotuses is filled with swans and geese.

272.sa: जले तरुणसूर्याभैष्षट्पदाहतकेसरैः। पङ्कजैश्शोभते पम्पा समन्तादभिसंवृता।।4.1.63।।
272.e: 'Lake Pampa shines with lotuses with bees on their filaments like the rising sun.

272.sa: चक्रवाकयुता नित्यं चित्रप्रस्तवनान्तरा। मातङ्गमृगयूथैश्च शोभते सलिलार्थिभिः।।4.1.64।।
272.e: 'Frequented by the Chakravakas and surrounded by the wonderful forest with thirsty elephants and deer this Pampa looks beautiful.

272.sa: पवनाहतवेगाभिरूर्मिभिर्विमलेऽम्भसि। पङ्कजानि विराजन्ते ताड्यमानानि लक्ष्मण।।4.1.65।।
272.e: 'O Lakshmana look at the lotuses in clear water dashing against one another due to waves caused by the force of the wind.

272.sa: पद्मपत्रविशालाक्षीं सततं पङ्कजप्रियाम्। अपश्यतो मे वैदेहीं जीवितं नाभिरोचते।।4.1.66।।
272.e: 'Unable to see my beloved with eyes large like totus petals and an ardent lover of lotuses, I have no desire to live.

272.sa: अहो कामस्य वामत्वं यो गतामपि दुर्लभाम्। स्मारयिष्यति कल्याणीं कल्याणतरवादिनीम्।।4.1.67।।
272.e: 'Oh how adversly disposed is the god of love He makes me remember that auspicious lady with a pleasing voice when she is lost and difficult to reach.

272.sa: शक्यो धारयितुं कामो भवेदभ्यागतो मया। यदि भूयो वसन्तो मां न हन्यात्पुष्पितद्रुमः।।4.1.68।।
272.e: 'If the spring that has set in, with the trees in bloom does not kill me, I have once again to endure the agony of love.

272.sa: यानि स्म रमणीयानि तया सह भवन्ति मे। तान्येवारमणीयानि जायन्ते मे तया विना।।4.1.69।।
272.e: 'Whatever was endearing to me earlier in the company of Sita, has turned out to be disenchanting without her.

272.sa: पद्मकोशपलाशानि द्रष्टुं दृष्टिर्हि मन्यते। सीताया नेत्रकोशाभ्यां सदृशानीति लक्ष्मण।।4.1.70।।
272.e: 'Seeing the delicate petals around the lotus buds that look like beautiful eyelids of Sita, my eyes crave for them O Lakshmana

272.sa: पद्मकेसरसंसृष्टो वृक्षान्तरविनिस्सृतः। निश्श्वास इव सीताया वाति वायुर्मनोहरः।।4.1.71।।
272.e: 'The bleeze that blows through the trees carrying the fragrance of the filaments of lotuses feels pleasant like Sita's breath.

272.sa: सौमित्रे पश्य पम्पाया दक्षिणे गिरिसानुनि। पुष्पितां कर्णिकारस्य यष्टिं परमशोभनाम्।।4.1.72।।
272.e: 'Look at the very spectacular karnikara tree with its blossmed branches on the mountain slope towards the southern side of Pampa, O Saumitri

272.sa: अधिकं शैलराजोऽयं धातुभिः सुविभूषितः। विचित्रं सृजते रेणुं वायुवेगविघट्टितम्।।4.1.73।।
272.e: 'This king of mountains is rich with plenty of minerals and, therefore, generates multicoloured dust particles splattered by the speed of the wind.

272.sa: गिरिप्रस्थास्तु सौमित्रे सर्वतस्सम्प्रपुष्पितैः। निष्पत्रैस्सर्वतो रम्यैः प्रदीप्ता इव किंशुकैः।।4.1.74।।
272.e: 'O Saumitri With leafless kimsuka trees in full bloom all over the mountain ranges they appear beautiful like blazing mountains.

272.sa: पम्पातीररुहाश्चेमे संसक्ता मधुगन्धिनः। मालतीमल्लिकाषण्डाः करवीराश्च पुष्पिताः।।4.1.75।।
272.e: 'Very closely grown on the banks of Pampa, stand malati, mallika and karavira trees with their clusters of fragrant blossoms.

272.sa: केतक्यस्सिन्दुवाराश्च वासन्त्यश्च सुपुष्पिताः। माधव्यो गन्धपूर्णाश्च कुन्दगुल्माश्च सर्वशः।।4.1.76।।
272.e: 'Fully blossmed ketaka, sinduvara, madhavi and kunda bushes in spring scatter their fragrance everywhere.

272.sa: चिरिबिल्वा मधूकाश्च वञ्जुला वकुलास्तथा। चम्पकास्तिलकाश्चैव नागवृक्षास्सुपुष्पिताः।।4.1.77।। नीपाश्च वरणाश्चैव खर्जूराश्च सुपुष्पिता।
272.e: 'Chiribilva, madhuka, vanjula, bakula, champaka, tilaka and naga varana and kharjura trees are in full bloom.

272.sa: पद्मकाश्चैव शोभन्ते नीलाशोकाश्च पुष्पिताः। लोध्राश्च गिरिपृष्ठेषु सिंहकेसरपिञ्जराः।।4.1.78।।
272.e: 'Lotuses and blue asokas are also in bloom. Lodhra trees on the mountainslopes look golden like the lion's mane.

272.sa: अङ्कोलाश्च कुरण्टाश्च चूर्णकाः पारिभद्रकाः। चूताः पाटलयश्चैव कोविदाराश्च पुष्पिताः।।4.1.79।। मुचुकुन्दार्जुनाश्चैव दृश्यन्ते गिरिसानुषु। केतकोद्दालकाश्चैव शिरीषाः शिंशुपा धवाः।।4.1.80।।
272.e: 'There are trees like ankola, kuranta, churnaka, paribhadraka, mango, patali, kovidara, muchukunda, arjuna, ketaka, uddalaka, shirisha, shimshupa and shava, all in full bloom on the mountain peaks.

272.sa: अङ्कोलाश्च कुरण्टाश्च चूर्णकाः पारिभद्रकाः। चूताः पाटलयश्चैव कोविदाराश्च पुष्पिताः।।4.1.79।। मुचुकुन्दार्जुनाश्चैव दृश्यन्ते गिरिसानुषु। केतकोद्दालकाश्चैव शिरीषाः शिंशुपा धवाः।।4.1.80।।
272.e: 'There are trees like ankola, kuranta, churnaka, paribhadraka, mango, patali, kovidara, muchukunda, arjuna, ketaka, uddalaka, shirisha, shimshupa and shava, all in full bloom on the mountain peaks.

272.sa: शाल्मल्यः किंशुकाश्चैव रक्ताः कुरवकास्तथा।।4.1.81।। त्रिनिशा नक्तमालाश्च चन्दनास्स्यन्दनास्तथा।
पुष्पितान्पुष्पिताग्राभिर्लताभिः परिवेष्टितान्। द्रुमान्पश्येह सौमित्रे पम्पाया रुचिरान्बहून्।।4.1.8283।।
272.e: 'O Saumitri look at the beauty of these numerous flowering trees on the banks of Pampa, entwining creepers with blooming tops.

272.sa: पुष्पितान्पुष्पिताग्राभिर्लताभिः परिवेष्टितान्। द्रुमान्पश्येह सौमित्रे पम्पाया रुचिरान्बहून्।।4.1.8283।।
272.e: 'O Saumitri look at the beauty of these numerous flowering trees on the banks of Pampa, entwining creepers with blooming tops.

272.sa: वातविक्षिप्तविटपान्यथाऽसन्नान्द्रुमानिमान्। लतास्समनुवर्तन्ते मत्ता इव वरस्त्रियः।।4.1.84।।
272.e: 'While the branches of trees swayed by the wind draw close, the creepers follow the trees like lovely women in a drunken state.

272.sa: पादपात्पादपं गच्छन् शैलाच्छैलं वनाद्वनम्। वाति नैकरसास्वादस्सम्मोदित इवानिलः।।4.1.85।।
272.e: 'The wind blows from tree to tree, mountain to mountain, and forest to forest as though content to enjoy all the fragrance.

272.sa: केचित्पर्याप्तकुसुमाः पादपा मधुगन्धिनः। केचिन्मुकुलसंवीताः श्यामवर्णा इवाबभुः।।4.1.86।।
272.e: 'Some trees stood fragrant with profuse flowers and some with buds shining blue.

272.sa: इदं मृष्टमिदं स्वादु प्रफुल्लमिदमित्यपि। रागयुक्तो मधुकरः कुसुमेष्वेव लीयते।।4.1.87।।
272.e: 'Fascinated by the flowers, the honeybees cling to one or the other, humming, 'this is soft, this is sweet, and this is fullyblossomed.'

272.sa: निलीय पुनरुत्पत्य सहसाऽन्यत्र गच्छति। मधुलुब्धो मधुकरः पम्पातीरद्रुमेष्वसौ।।4.1.88।।
272.e: 'The bees greedy for honey move among the trees on the banks of Pampa. Resting for a while, at one place they fly soon to another.

272.sa: इयं कुसुमसङ्घातैरुपस्तीर्णा सुखाकृता। स्वयं निपतितैर्भूमिश्शयनप्रस्तरैरिव।।4.1.89।।
272.e: 'With countless flowers fallen on their own from trees and scattered like a bed of flowers on stone the ground is rendered comfortable enough to relax on.

272.sa: विविधा विविधैः पुष्पैस्तैरेव नगसानुषु। विकीर्णै पीतरक्ताहि सौमित्रे प्रस्तराः कृताः।।4.1.90।।
272.e: 'O Saumitri varieties of colourful flowers, some red and some yellow, are spread out on the mountain slopes.

272.sa: हिमान्ते पश्य सौमित्रे वृक्षाणां पुष्पसम्भवम्। पुष्पमासे हि तरवस्सङ्घर्षादिव पुष्पिताः।।4.1.91।।
272.e: 'Winter has ended and the season of flowers has set in, O Saumitri The trees are full of flowers as if competing with one another.

272.sa: आह्वयन्त इवान्योन्यं नगाष्षट्पदनादिताः। कुसुमोत्तंसविटपाश्शोभन्ते बहु लक्ष्मण।।4.1.92।।
272.e: 'The trees, crowned with flowers filled with humming bees, look splendid. It appears they are calling one another, O Lakshmana

272.sa: एष कारण्डवः पक्षी विगाह्य सलिलं शुभम्। रमते कान्तया सार्धं काममुद्दीपयन्मम।।4.1.93।।
272.e: 'This duck, entering into auspicious water, sports with its beloved and incites my love.

272.sa: मन्दाकिन्यास्तु यदिदं रूपमेवं मनोहरम्। स्थाने जगति विख्याता गुणास्तस्या मनोरमाः।।4.1.94।।
272.e: 'Only Ganga, like Pampa, has such captivating charm. Its beauty and virtues are famous in the world.

272.sa: यदि दृश्येत सा साध्वी यदि चेह वसेमहि। स्पृहयेयं न शक्राय नायोध्यायै रघूत्तम।।4.1.95।।
272.e: 'O Lakshmna, the best of the Raghu race, if only that chaste Sita appears, we will stay here. I will not wish for the position of Indra or for Ayodhya.

272.sa: नह्येवं रमणीयेषु शाद्वलेषु तया सह। रमतो मे भवेच्चिन्ता न स्पृहाऽन्येषु वा भवेत्।।4.1.96।।
272.e: 'If I can sport with Sita in this beautiful green grassy land, I will not have any worry, I would not desire for any other pleasure.

272.sa: अमी हि विविधैः पुष्पैस्तरवो रुचिरच्छदाः। काननेऽऽस्मिन्विना कान्तां चिन्तामुत्पादयन्ति मे।।4.1.97।।
272.e: 'These trees with their beautiful leaves and varieties of flowers bring me agony as I live in this forest separated from my beloved.

272.sa: पश्य शीतजलां चेमां सौमित्रे पुष्करायुताम्। चक्रवाकानुचरितां कारण्डव निषेविताम्।।4.1.98।।
272.e: 'O Saumitri look at this lake of cool water filled with, lotuses, chakravakas flying about and ducks floating.

272.sa: प्लवैः क्रौञ्चैश्च सम्पूर्णां महामृगनिषेविताम्। अधिकं शोभते पम्पा विकूजद्भिःर्विहङ्गमैः।।4.1.99।। दीपयन्तीव मे कामं विविधा मुदिता द्विजाः। श्यामां चन्द्रमुखीं स्मृत्वा प्रियां पद्मनिभेक्षणाम्।।4.1.100।।
272.e: Pampa, filled with swimming, kraunchas and frequented by big animals looks splendid. The joyous warbling of a variety of birds is highly exciting. They kindle my passion for my young, Moonfaced, lotus eyed beloved.

272.sa: प्लवैः क्रौञ्चैश्च सम्पूर्णां महामृगनिषेविताम्। अधिकं शोभते पम्पा विकूजद्भिःर्विहङ्गमैः।।4.1.99।। दीपयन्तीव मे कामं विविधा मुदिता द्विजाः। श्यामां चन्द्रमुखीं स्मृत्वा प्रियां पद्मनिभेक्षणाम्।।4.1.100।।
272.e: Pampa, filled with swimming, kraunchas and frequented by big animals looks splendid. The joyous warbling of a variety of birds is highly exciting. They kindle my passion for my young, Moonfaced, lotus eyed beloved.

272.sa: पश्य सानुषु चित्रेषु मृगीभिस्सहितान्मृगान्। मां पुनर्मृगशाबाक्ष्या वैदेह्या विरहीकृतम्।।4.1.101।। व्यथयन्तीव मे चित्तं सञ्चरन्तस्ततस्ततः।
272.e: Look at the (male) deer happily roaming here and there together with the female deer on the colourful mountain slopes. Separated from the fawneyed Vaidehi, this sight fills my heart with agony.

272.sa: अस्मिन्सानुनि रम्ये हि मत्तद्विजगणायुते। पश्येयं यदि तां कान्तां ततस्स्वस्ति भवेन्मम।।4.1.102।।
272.e: 'If I find my dear beloved here on these mountain slopes full of passionate birds how happy will I not feel

272.sa: जीवेयं खलु सौमित्रे मया सह सुमध्यमा। सेवते यदि वैदेही पम्पायाः पवनं सुखम्।।4.1.103।।
272.e: 'O Saumitri I can be alive and happy if Sita of slender waist enjoys here with me the sweet breeze of Pampa.

272.sa: पद्मसौगन्धिकवहं शिवं शोकविनाशनम्। धन्या लक्ष्मण सेवन्ते पम्पोपवनमारुतम्।।4.1.104।।
272.e: 'O Lakshmana blessed are those who enjoy the breeze filled with fragrance of lotuses of the surrounding forests of Pampa. The gentle and auspicious breeze indeed takes away the sorrow of the mind.

272.sa: श्यामा पद्मपलाशाक्षी प्रिया विरहिता मया। कथं धारयति प्राणान्विवशा जनकात्मजा।।4.1.105।।
272.e: 'How can Janaka's daughter with eyes like lotus petals, so young and loving, sustain her life? Away from me, she must be feeling quite dejected.

272.sa: किन्नु वक्ष्यामि राजानं धर्मज्ञं सत्यवादिनम्। सीताया जनकं पृष्टः कुशलं जनसंसदि।।4.1.106।।
272.e: 'If righteous and truthful Janaka enquires about Sita's wellbeing in the assembly of people, what am I to speak ?

272.sa: या मामनुगता मन्दं पित्रा प्रव्राजितं वनम्। सीता सत्पथमास्थाय क्व नु सा वर्तते प्रिया।।4.1.107।।
तया विहीनः कृपणः कथं लक्ष्मण धारये। या मामनुगता राज्याद्भ्रष्टं विगतचेतसम्।।4.1.108।।
272.e: 'She followed me, O Lakshmana  as I was deposed from the kingdom and distraught. Now helpless, how can I live without her?

272.sa: तच्चार्वञ्चितपद्माक्षं सुगन्धि शुभमव्रणम्। अपश्यतो मुखं तस्यास्सीदतीव मनो मम।।4.1.109।।
272.e: 'Unable to see her beautiful, face with auspicious eyes like fragrant lotuses, I feel (so) depressed.

272.sa: स्मितहास्यान्तरयुतं गुणवन्मधुरं हितम्। वैदेह्या वाक्यमतुलं कदा श्रोष्यामि लक्ष्मण।।4.1.110।।
272.e: 'When can I listen to Sita's sweet, wholesome and virtuous, incomparable words interlaced with her gentle smile, O Lakshmana?

272.sa: प्राप्य दुखं वने श्यामा मां मन्मथविकर्शितम्। नष्टदुःखेव हृष्टेव साध्वी साध्वभ्यभाषत।।4.1.111।।
272.e: My young and faithful beloved used to put up a brave face and speak to me in all propriety to cheer me up in the midst of suffering in the forest whenever I felt tormented by passion.

272.sa: किं नु वक्ष्यामि कौसल्यामयोध्यायां नृपात्मज। क्व सा स्नुषेति पृच्छन्तीं कथं चापि तु मनस्विनीम्।।4.1.112।।
272.e: 'O Prince, what can I tell the highminded Kausalya at Ayodhya when she asks the whereabouts of her daughterinlaw'?

272.sa: गच्छ लक्ष्मण पश्य त्वं भरतं भ्रातृवत्सलम्। न ह्यहं जीवितु शक्तस्तामृते जनकात्मजाम्।।4.1.113।।
272.e: 'You may go to Ayodhya, O Lakshmana, to see our loving brother, Bharata. It is not possible for me to survive without the daughter of Janaka'.

272.sa: इति रामं महात्मानं विलपन्तमनाथवत्। उवाच लक्ष्मणो भ्राता वचनं युक्तमव्ययम्।।4.1.114।।
272.e: Thus spoke Lakshmana these befitting, unforgettable words to his hissouled brother, Rama wailing like an orphan:

272.sa: संस्तम्भ राम भद्रं ते मा शुचः पुरुषोत्तम। नेदृशानां मतिर्मन्दा भवत्यकलुषात्मनाम्।।4.1.115।।
272.e: 'O Rama, the foremost of men, control yourself. Be blessed. People who are pure at heart do not feel depressed at heart.

272.sa: स्मृत्वा वियोगजं दुःखं त्यज स्नेहं प्रिये जने। अतिस्नेहपरिष्वङ्गाद्वर्तिरार्द्रापि दह्यते।।4.1.116।।
272.e: 'Remembrance of loved ones causes sorrow. Even a wet cotton wick gets burnt by embracing excessive oil. Hence abandon grief.

272.sa: यदि गच्छति पातालं ततोऽभ्यधिकमेव वा। सर्वथा रावणस्तावन्न भविष्यति राघव।।4.1.117।।
272.e: 'Even if Ravana escapes into the nether world or into a world still lower, he cannot save himself by any means, O Rama

272.sa: प्रवृत्तिर्लभ्यतां तावत्तस्य पापस्य रक्षसः। ततो हास्यति वा सीतां निधनं वा गमिष्यति।।4.1.118।।
272.e: 'Once the whereabouts of that sinful demon are known he will either deliver Sita or die.

272.sa: यदि यातिदितेर्गर्भं रावणस्सह सीतया। तत्राप्येनं हनिष्यामि न चेद्दास्यति मैथिलीम्।।4.1.119।।
272.e: 'Even if Ravana enters into the womb of Diti (mother of demons) along with Sita, I will slay him there if he does not return the daughter of Mithila.

272.sa: स्वास्थ्यं भद्रं भजस्वार्य त्यज्यतां कृपणा मतिः। अर्थो हि नष्टकार्यार्थैर्नायत्नेनाधिगम्यते।।4.1.120।।
272.e: 'O noble prince be blessed. maintain composure. Without making any effort it is not possible to achieve the objective and recoup loss.

272.sa: उत्साहो बलवानार्य नास्त्युत्साहात्परं बलम्। सोत्साहस्यास्ति लोकेऽस्मिन् न किञ्चिदपि दुर्लभम्।।4.1.121।।
272.e: 'O revered Sire, enterprise is supreme strength. Nothing is difficult in this world for one who is up and doing.

272.sa: उत्साहवन्तः पुरुषा नावसीदन्ति कर्मसु। उत्साहमात्रमाश्रित्य सीतां प्रतिलभेमहि।।4.1.122।।
272.e: 'Enterprising men will never be disappointed in their mission. It is possible to get Sita through effort alone.

272.sa: त्यज्यतां कामवृत्तत्वं शोकं सन्न्यस्य पृष्ठतः। महात्मानं कृतात्मानमात्मानं नावबुध्यसे।।4.1.123।।
272.e: 'Bardon grief. Give up emotion. You are a great soul. You are not aware of your great accomplishments. (The temporary sorrow has relegated Rama's nobility to the background. Lakshmana is trying to restore the same)'.

272.sa: एवं सम्बोधितस्तत्र शोकोपहतचेतनः। त्यज्य शोकञ्च मोहञ्च ततो धैर्यमुपागमत्।।4.1.124।।
272.e: Thus persuaded by Lakshmana, Rama who was hitherto besieged by grief and delusion, could set them aside and regain patience.

272.sa: सोऽभ्यतिक्रामदव्यग्रस्तामचिन्त्यपराक्रमः। रामः पम्पां सुरुचिरां रम्यपारिप्लवद्रुमाम्।।4.1.125।।
272.e: No more disturbed by delusion, Rama of unimaginable valour, crossed the very brilliant Pampa with beautiful plants floating on its surface.

272.sa: निरीक्षमाणस्सहसा महात्मा सर्वं वनं निर्झरकन्दराश्च। उद्विग्नचेतास्सह लक्ष्मणेन विचार्य दुःखोपहतः प्रतस्थे।।4.1.126।।
272.e: The great Rama was overcome with grief while scanning the entire forest with its streams and caves. Engrossed in her thoughts, dejected at heart and inflicted with pain, he set both, accompanied by Lakshmana.

272.sa: तं मत्तमातङ्गविलासगामी गच्छन्तमव्यग्रमना महात्मा। स लक्ष्मणो राघवमप्रमत्तो ररक्ष धर्मेण बलेन चैव।।4.1.127।।
272.e: The great soul, Lakshmana, striding like a mighty elephant, with a steady mind, followed Rama dutifully, protecting him with his strength.

272.sa: तावृष्यमूकस्य समीपचारी चरन्ददर्शाद्भुतदर्शनीयौ। शाखामृगाणामधिपस्तरस्वी वितत्रसे नैव चिचेष्ट किञ्चित्।।4.1.128।।
272.e: The swiftfooted, mighty king of monkeys saw those two men of wonderful appearance as they were wandering at Rishyamuka. He neither got scared nor showed signs of nervousness.

272.sa: स तौ महात्मा गजमन्दगामी शाखामृगस्तत्र चरञ्चरन्तौ। दृष्ट्वा विषादं परमं जगाम चिन्तापरीतो भयभारमग्नः।।4.1.129।।
272.e: The great soul, Sugriva, walking slowly like an elephant saw both of them and became despondent, worried and immersed in fear.

272.sa: तमाश्रमं पुण्यसुखं शरण्यं सदैव शाखामृगसेवितान्तम्। त्रस्ताश्च दृष्ट्वा हरयोऽभिजग्मुर्महौजसौ राघवलक्ष्मणौ तौ।।4.1.130।।
272.e: Having seen the mighty Rama and Lakshmana, all other monkeys got frightened and ran into a sacred and safe hermitage. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये किष्किन्धाकाण्डे प्रथमस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the first sarga of Kishkindakanda of the Holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

273.sa: तौ तु दृष्ट्वा महात्मानौ भ्रातरौ रामलक्ष्मणौ। वरायुधधरौ वीरौ सुग्रीवश्शङ्कितोऽभवत्4.2.1।।
273.e: On seeing the two great souls, heroic Rama and Lakshmana wielding the best of weapons, Sugriva was alarmed.

273.sa: उद्विग्नहृदयस्सर्वा दिशस्समवलोकयन्। न व्यतिष्ठत कस्मिंश्चिद्देशे वानरपुङ्गवः। 4.2.2।।
273.e: Agitated at heart, the best of vanaras started in all directions and could not settle down at one spot.

273.sa: नैव चक्रे मनः स्थातुं वीक्षमाणो महाबलौ। कपेः परमभीतस्य चित्तं व्यवससाद ह4.2.3।।
273.e: Beholding the two strong heroes, the monkey (Sugriva) was very much frightened. His heart sank.

273.sa: चिन्तयित्वा स धर्मात्मा विमृश्य गुरुलाघवम्। सुग्रीवः परमोद्विग्नस्सर्वैरनुचरैस्सह4.2.4।।
273.e: Righteous Sugriva, became highly agitated, deliberated with all his followers on the pros and cons of the situation.

273.sa: ततस्स सचिवेभ्यस्तु सुग्रीवः प्लवगाधिपः। शशंस परमोद्विग्नः पश्यंस्तौ रामलक्ष्मणौ4.2.5।।
273.e: Sugriva, lord of monkeys, extremely agitated at the sight of both Rama and Lakshmana, spoke to his minister:

273.sa: एतौ वनमिदं दुर्गं वालिप्रणिहितौ ध्रुवम्। छद्मना चीरवसनौ प्रचरन्ताविहागतौ4.2.6।।
ततस्सुग्रीवसचिवा दृष्ट्वा परमधन्विनौ। जग्मुर्गिरितटात्तस्मादन्यच्छिखरमुत्तमम्4.2.7।।
273.e: On seeing these supreme bowmen, Sugriva's counsellers left for the peak of another mountain.

273.sa: ते क्षिप्रमधिगम्याथ यूथपा यूथपर्षभम्। हरयो वानरश्रेष्ठं परिवार्योपतस्थिरे4.2.8।।
273.e: The leaders of the monkey troops  reached Sugriva, the lord of monkeys, in no time  and stood surrounding him.

273.sa: एकमेकायनगताः प्लवमाना गिरेर्गिरिम्। प्रकम्पयन्तो वेगेन गिरीणां शिखराण्यपि4.2.9।।
273.e: Jumping  from one mountain to another swiftly and shaking the mountain tops, the monkeys reached one spot.

273.sa: ततश्शाखामृगास्सर्वे प्लवमाना महाबलाः। बभञ्जुश्च नगांस्तत्र पुष्पितान्दुर्गसंश्रितान्4.2.10।।
273.e: Then the mighty monkeys jumping on the trees in full bloom shook them.

273.sa: आप्लवन्तो हरिवरास्सर्वतस्तं महागिरिम्। मृगमार्जारशार्दूलांस्त्रासयन्तो ययुस्तदा4.2.11।।
273.e: The great monkeys went on leaping all over the great (Rishyamuka) mountain,   scaring the deer, wildcats and tigers.

273.sa: ततस्सुग्रीवसचिवाः पर्वतेन्द्रं समाश्रिताः। सङ्गम्य कपिमुख्येन सर्वे प्राञ्जलय स्थिताः।।4.2.12।।
273.e: Thereafter, all the ministers of Sugriva assembled together on the king of mountains and stood (in front of Sugriva), with folded hands.

273.sa: ततस्तं भयसंविग्नं वालिकिल्बिषशङ्कितम्। उवाच हनुमान्वाक्यं सुग्रीवं वाक्यकोविदः4.2.13।।
273.e: Suspecting that Vali might have sent them (Rama and Lakshmana), Hanuman, skilful in communication, said to Sugriva who was trembling in fear:

273.sa: सम्भ्रमस्त्यज्यतामेष सर्वैर्वालिकृते महान्। मलयोऽयं गिरिवरो भयं नेहास्ति वालिनः4.2.14।।
273.e: 'This is a great mountain range of Malaya and there is no fear for Vali here. Give up this fear.

273.sa: यस्मादुद्विग्नचेतास्त्वं प्रद्रुतो हरिपुङ्गव। तं क्रूरदर्शनं क्रूरं नेह पश्यामि वालिनम्4.2.15।।
273.e: 'O chief of monkeys I do not see here any sign of the cruel Vali, of whom you are afraid.

273.sa: यस्मात्तव भयं सौम्य पूर्वजात्पापकर्मणः। स नेह वाली दुष्टात्मा न ते पश्याम्यहं भयम्4.2.16।।
273.e: 'O goodnatured Sugriva you are afraid of your elder brother Vali as he is evilminded and sinful. (But) I do not see any reason for you to be frightened as he is not found anywhere here.

273.sa: अहो शाखामृगत्वं ते व्यक्तमेव प्लवङ्गम। लघुचित्ततयाऽत्मानं न स्थापयसि यो मतौ4.2.17।।
273.e: 'Oh monkey, whoever is lilylivered cannot be steady. It is evident that your very nature as a monkey makes you restless.

273.sa: बुद्धिविज्ञानसम्पन्न इङ्गितैस्सर्वमाचर। न ह्यबुद्धिं गतो राजा सर्वभूतानि शास्ति हि4.2.18।।
सुग्रीवस्तु शुभं वाक्यं श्रुत्वा सर्वं हनूमतः। ततश्शुभतरं वाक्यं हनूमन्तमुवाच ह4.2.19।।
273.e: Having heard the wise words of Hanuman, Sugriva addressed him with words more auspicious.

273.sa: दीर्घबाहू विशालाक्षौ शरचापासिधारिणौ। कस्य न स्याद्भयं दृष्ट्वा ह्येतौ सुरसुतोपमौ4.2.20।।
273.e: 'Who would not be apprehensive of these two longarmed and largeeyed individuals     comparable to sons of gods wielding arrows, bows and swords.

273.sa: वालिप्रणिहितावेतौ शङ्केऽहं पुरुषोत्तमौ। राजानो बहुमित्राश्च विश्वासो नात्र हि क्षमः4.2.21।।
273.e: 'I support these two excellent men might have been sent by Vali. Kings have many friends and so it may not be appropriate to trust any king.

273.sa: अरयश्च मनुष्येण विज्ञेयाश्छद्मचारिणः। विश्वस्तानामविश्वस्तारन्ध्रेषु प्रहरन्ति हि4.2.22।।
273.e: 'One has to identify these men roaming in disguise. These are not trustworthy and could even be our enemies, making us believe them so as to attack us when we are not vigilant.

273.sa: कृत्येषु वाली मेधावी राजानो बहुदर्शिनः। भवन्ति परहन्तारस्ते ज्ञेयाः प्राकृतैर्नरैः4.2.23।।
273.e: 'Vali is wise in his actions. Kings employ many strategies to annihilate their enemies. Our gullible individuals should be able to detect them.

273.sa: तौ त्वया प्राकृतेनैव गत्वा ज्ञेयौ प्लवङ्गम। इङ्गितानां प्रकारैश्च रूपव्याभाषणेन च4.2.24।।
273.e: 'O Hanuman assume an ordinary form and approach them. Try to read them through their gestures, traits, forms and conversations.

273.sa: लक्षयस्व तयोर्भावं प्रहृष्टमनसौ यदि। विश्वासयन्प्रशंसाभिरिङ्गितैश्च पुनः पुनः4.2.25।। ममैवाभिमुखं स्थित्वा पृच्छ त्वं हरिपुङ्गव । प्रयोजनं प्रवेशस्य वनस्यास्य धनुर्धरौ4.2.26।।
273.e: 'O best of monkeys ascertain their purpose by praising them and studying their honest intentions. Gain the confidence of the wielders of bows and if you find them agreeable, enquire the purpose of their entering this forest.

273.sa: लक्षयस्व तयोर्भावं प्रहृष्टमनसौ यदि। विश्वासयन्प्रशंसाभिरिङ्गितैश्च पुनः पुनः4.2.25।। ममैवाभिमुखं स्थित्वा पृच्छ त्वं हरिपुङ्गव । प्रयोजनं प्रवेशस्य वनस्यास्य धनुर्धरौ4.2.26।।
273.e: 'O best of monkeys ascertain their purpose by praising them and studying their honest intentions. Gain the confidence of the wielders of bows and if you find them agreeable, enquire the purpose of their entering this forest.

273.sa: शुद्धात्मानौ यदि त्वेतौ जानीहि त्वं प्लवङ्गम। व्याभाषितैर्वा विज्ञेया स्याद्दुष्टाऽदुष्टता तयोः4.2.27।।
273.e: 'O best of monkeys find out whether they are noble in their intentions or evil in their design through your conversation with them.'

273.sa: इत्येवं कपिराजेन सन्दिष्टो मारुतात्मजः। चकार गमने बुद्धिं यत्र तौ रामलक्ष्मणौ4.2.28।।
273.e: Instructed thus by the king of the monkeys, Hanuman, son of the Windgod, decided to meet both Rama and Lakshmana.

273.sa: तथेति सम्पूज्य वचस्तु तस्य तत्कपेस्सुभीमस्य दुरासदस्य च। महानुभावो हनुमान्ययौ तदा स यत्र रामोऽतिबलश्च लक्ष्मणः4.2.29।।
273.e: Hanuman, the venerable, powerful and not easily conquerable monkey, honoured the words of the great Lord of the monkeys, offered salutations and said 'So be it'. And then proceeded towards the mighty Rama and Lakshmana. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये किष्किन्धाकाण्डे द्वितीयस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the second sarga of Kishkindakanda of the Holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by the sage Valmiki.

274.sa: वचो विज्ञाय हनुमान् सुग्रीवस्य महात्मनः। पर्वतादृश्यमूकात्तु पुप्लुवे यत्र राघवौ।।4.3.1।।
274.e: Listening to great Sugriva, Hanuman leaped from mount Rishyamuka on to the location of the Raghavas.

274.sa: कपिरूपं परित्यज्य हनुमान्मारुतात्मजः। भिक्षुरूपं ततो भेजे शठबुद्धितया कपिः4.3.2।।
274.e: Hanuman, son of the Windgod, with an ingenious mind assumed the guise of a mendicant.

274.sa: ततस्स हनुमान्वाचा श्लक्ष्णया सुमनोज्ञया। विनीतवदुपागम्य राघवौ प्रणिपत्य च।।4.3.3।। आबभाषे तदा वीरौ यथावत्प्रशशंस च।
274.e: Approaching the Raghavas in all humility, valiant Hanuman offered them reverential salutations and addressed them in gentle and pleasing words.

274.sa: सम्पूज्य विधिवद्वीरौ हनुमान्मारुतात्मजः। उवाच कामतो वाक्यं मृदु सत्यपराक्रमौ4.3.4।।
274.e: The valiant son of the Windgod, Hanuman offered those heroes whose power came from their sense of truth due respect and spoke to them in all gentleness:

274.sa: राजर्षिदेवप्रतिमौ तापसौ संशितव्रतौ। देशं कथमिमं प्राप्तौ भवन्तौ वरवर्णिनौ4.3.5।। त्रासयन्तौ मृगगणानन्यांश्च वनचारिणः4.3.6।।
274.e: 'You both fair in complexion, resemble royal sages or gods. You appear like ascetics and pursue vows in austerity. How come, you are present here, as if to frighten the animals and other creatures roaming this forest?

274.sa: राजर्षिदेवप्रतिमौ तापसौ संशितव्रतौ। देशं कथमिमं प्राप्तौ भवन्तौ वरवर्णिनौ4.3.5।। त्रासयन्तौ मृगगणानन्यांश्च वनचारिणः4.3.6।।
274.e: 'You both fair in complexion, resemble royal sages or gods. You appear like ascetics and pursue vows in austerity. How come, you are present here, as if to frighten the animals and other creatures roaming this forest?

274.sa: पम्पातीररुहान्वृक्षान् वीक्षमाणौ समन्ततः। इमां नदीं शुभजलां शोभयन्तौ तपस्विनौ4.3.7।। धैर्यवन्तौ सुवर्णाभौ कौ युवां चीरवाससौ। निःश्वसन्तौ वरभुजौ पीडयन्ताविमाः प्रजा:4.3.8।।
274.e: 'Gazing at the trees on the bank of Pampa, you both appear in brilliant complexion as if to enhance the beauty of the auspicious river water. Though young, courageous and with handsome shoulders, you seem to sigh in exhaustion. And though you look like ascetics robed in bark,  you seem to terrify these creatures.

274.sa: पम्पातीररुहान्वृक्षान् वीक्षमाणौ समन्ततः। इमां नदीं शुभजलां शोभयन्तौ तपस्विनौ4.3.7।। धैर्यवन्तौ सुवर्णाभौ कौ युवां चीरवाससौ। निःश्वसन्तौ वरभुजौ पीडयन्ताविमाः प्रजा:4.3.8।।
274.e: 'Gazing at the trees on the bank of Pampa, you both appear in brilliant complexion as if to enhance the beauty of the auspicious river water. Though young, courageous and with handsome shoulders, you seem to sigh in exhaustion. And though you look like ascetics robed in bark,  you seem to terrify these creatures.

274.sa: सिंहविप्रेक्षितौ वीरौ महाबलविक्रमौ। शक्रचापनिभे चापे गृहीत्वा शत्रुसूदनौ4.3.9।। श्रीमन्तौ रूपसम्पन्नौ वृषभश्रेष्ठविक्रमौ। हस्तिहस्तोपमभुजौ द्युतिमन्तौ नरर्षभौ4.3.10।।
274.e: 'Having the gaze  of a lion, both of you are heroic in your stance. As each of you hold a bow resembling the rainbow, you seem to be mighty warriors eager to annihilate the enemies. With the valour of superior bulls and your shoulders resembling elephant's trunks, you look magnificent, handsome and brilliant. (No doubt,) you are the best among the humans.

274.sa: सिंहविप्रेक्षितौ वीरौ महाबलविक्रमौ। शक्रचापनिभे चापे गृहीत्वा शत्रुसूदनौ4.3.9।। श्रीमन्तौ रूपसम्पन्नौ वृषभश्रेष्ठविक्रमौ। हस्तिहस्तोपमभुजौ द्युतिमन्तौ नरर्षभौ4.3.10।।
274.e: 'Having the gaze  of a lion, both of you are heroic in your stance. As each of you hold a bow resembling the rainbow, you seem to be mighty warriors eager to annihilate the enemies. With the valour of superior bulls and your shoulders resembling elephant's trunks, you look magnificent, handsome and brilliant. (No doubt,) you are the best among the humans.

274.sa: प्रभया पर्वतेन्द्रोऽयं युवयोरवभासितः। राज्यार्हावमरप्रख्यौ कथं देशमिहागतौ4.3.11।।
274.e: 'You are young and radiant like the gods. This king of mountains (Rishyamuka) dazzles with your brilliance. Although you deserve to be sovereigns, how is it that you are here (into the forest)?

274.sa: पद्मपत्रेक्षणौ वीरौ जटामण्डलधारिणौ। अन्योन्यसदृशौ वीरौ देवलोकादिवागतौ4.3.12।। यदृच्छयेव सम्प्राप्तौ चन्द्रसूर्यौ वसुन्धराम्। विशालवक्षसौ वीरौ मानुषौ देवरूपिणौ4.3.13।। सिंहस्कन्धौ महोत्साहौ समदाविव गोवृषौ।
274.e: 'Both of you appear alike, with eyes like lotus petals and locks of matted hair. You look like heroes descending from the world of the gods. You look like the Sun and the Moon dropped incidentally on this earth. With shoulders like those of a lion and the majesty of energetic bulls, you broadchested warriors appear like divine beings, though in fact humans.

274.sa: पद्मपत्रेक्षणौ वीरौ जटामण्डलधारिणौ। अन्योन्यसदृशौ वीरौ देवलोकादिवागतौ4.3.12।। यदृच्छयेव सम्प्राप्तौ चन्द्रसूर्यौ वसुन्धराम्। विशालवक्षसौ वीरौ मानुषौ देवरूपिणौ4.3.13।। सिंहस्कन्धौ महोत्साहौ समदाविव गोवृषौ।
274.e: 'Both of you appear alike, with eyes like lotus petals and locks of matted hair. You look like heroes descending from the world of the gods. You look like the Sun and the Moon dropped incidentally on this earth. With shoulders like those of a lion and the majesty of energetic bulls, you broadchested warriors appear like divine beings, though in fact humans.

274.sa: आयताश्च सुवृत्ताश्च बाहवः परिघोपमाः। सर्वभूषणभूषार्हाः किमर्थं न विभूषिताः4.3.14।।
274.e: 'Your long arms and spherelike shoulders appear as strong as iron clubs. Although they deserve to be decked with ornaments, how is it they are unadorned?

274.sa: उभौ योग्यावहं मन्ये रक्षितुं पृथिवीमिमाम्। ससागरवनां कृत्स्नां विन्ध्यमेरुविभूषिताम्4.3.15।।
274.e: 'To me, you both deserve to rule the entire earth encompassed by seas and forests and adorned with mountains like Vindhya and Meru.

274.sa: इमे च धनुषी चित्रे श्लष्णे चित्रानुलेपने। प्रकाशेते यथेन्द्रस्य वज्रे हेमविभूषिते4.3.16।।
274.e: 'Smeared with wonderful unguents, (your) bows look  very attractive. And they glow very much like Indra's golden thunderbolt.

274.sa: सम्पूर्णा निशितैर्बाणै स्तूणाश्च शुभदर्शनाः4.3.17।। जीवितान्तकरैर्घोरै श्श्वसद्भिरिव पन्नगैः।।
274.e: '(Your) quivers also appear beautiful, for they are  fully  filled with sharp and deadly arrows which look like the hissing of dreadful snakes

274.sa: महाप्रमाणौ विस्तीर्णौ तप्तहाटकभूषितौ4.3.18।। खडगावेतौ विराजेते निर्मुक्ताविवपन्नगौ।।
274.e: '(Your) long and broad swords appear very huge in size. Being encrusted with pure gold, they  glitter brilliant like snakes in hyberation.

274.sa: एवं मां परिभाषन्तं कस्माद्वै नाभिभाषथः4.3.19।। सुग्रीवो नाम धर्मात्मा कश्चिद्वानरयूथपः। वीरो विनिकृतो भ्रात्रा जगद्भ्रमति दुःखितः4.3.20।।
274.e: 'Why are you silent  while I am talking? (I am here to apprise ) about a great and righteous warrior Sugriva, the chief of the troop of monkeys, sadly wandering all over the land here, banished by his brother

274.sa: एवं मां परिभाषन्तं कस्माद्वै नाभिभाषथः4.3.19।। सुग्रीवो नाम धर्मात्मा कश्चिद्वानरयूथपः। वीरो विनिकृतो भ्रात्रा जगद्भ्रमति दुःखितः4.3.20।।
274.e: 'Why are you silent  while I am talking? (I am here to apprise ) about a great and righteous warrior Sugriva, the chief of the troop of monkeys, sadly wandering all over the land here, banished by his brother

274.sa: प्राप्तोऽहं प्रेषितस्तेन सुग्रीवेण महात्मना। राज्ञा वानरमुख्यानां हनुमान्नाम वानरः4.3.21।।
274.e: 'I am a monkey called Hanuman. I am here sent by great king Sugriva, the best of monkeys.

274.sa: युवाभ्यां सह धर्मात्मा सुग्रीवस्सख्यमिच्छति। तस्य मां सचिवं वित्तं वानरं पवनात्मजम्4.3.22।। भिक्षुरूपप्रतिच्छन्नं सुग्रीवप्रियकाम्यया। ऋष्यमूकादिह प्राप्तं कामगं कामरूपिणम्4.3.23।।
274.e: 'The righteous Sugriva wishes to make friendship with both of you. For his wellbeing I came here disguised as a mendicant from  Rishyamuka mountain. I am a monkey, son of the Windgod and minister to Sugriva. I can assume any form at my free will and go anywhere I like'.

274.sa: युवाभ्यां सह धर्मात्मा सुग्रीवस्सख्यमिच्छति। तस्य मां सचिवं वित्तं वानरं पवनात्मजम्4.3.22।। भिक्षुरूपप्रतिच्छन्नं सुग्रीवप्रियकाम्यया। ऋष्यमूकादिह प्राप्तं कामगं कामरूपिणम्4.3.23।।
274.e: 'The righteous Sugriva wishes to make friendship with both of you. For his wellbeing I came here disguised as a mendicant from  Rishyamuka mountain. I am a monkey, son of the Windgod and minister to Sugriva. I can assume any form at my free will and go anywhere I like'.

274.sa: एवमुक्त्वा तु हनुमांस्तौ वीरौ रामलक्ष्मणौ। वाक्यज्ञौ वाक्यकुशलः पुनर्नोवाच किञ्चन4.3.24।।
274.e: The eloquent Hanuman, having spoken thus to both Rama and Lakshmana, good at speaking, said no more.

274.sa: एतच्छ्रुत्वा वचन्तस्य रामो लक्ष्मणमब्रवीत्। प्रहृष्टवदनश्श्रीमान्भ्रातरं पार्श्वतः स्थितम्4.3.25।।
274.e: Having heard him, the Illustrious Rama cheerfully said to brother Lakshmana standing nearby:

274.sa: सचिवोऽयं कपीन्द्रस्य सुग्रीवस्य महात्मनः। तमेव काङ्क्षमाणस्य ममान्तिकमुपागतः4.3.26।।
274.e: 'Here is minister to Sugriva, the great chief of monkeys whom I wish to see.

274.sa: तमभ्यभाष सौमित्रे सुग्रीवसचिवं कपिम्। वाक्यज्ञं मधुरैर्वाक्यैस्स्नेहयुक्तमरिन्दम।।4.3.27।।
274.e: 'O Saumitri, conqueror of enemies this monkey, Sugriva's minister, is skilled in friendly communication. Reply to him in words gentle and sweet.

274.sa: नानृग्वेदविनीतस्य नायजुर्वेद्धारिणः। नासामवेदविदुषश्शक्यमेवं विभाषितुम्4.3.28।।
274.e: 'Unless wellversed in Rigveda, Yajurveda and Samaveda, for sure, it is not possible for anyone to articulate so well.

274.sa: नूनं व्याकरणं कृत्स्नमनेन बहुधा श्रुतम्। बहु व्याहरताऽनेन न किञ्चिदपशब्दितम्4.3.29।।
274.e: 'Surely, he seems to have studied well the whole of grammar, for there is not a single mispronunciation in his entire speech.

274.sa: न मुखे नेत्रयोर्वापि ललाटे च भ्रुवोस्तथा। अन्येष्वपि च गात्रेषु दोषस्संविदितः क्वचित्4.3.30।।
274.e: No fault can be found in his face, eyes, forehead, between the eyebrows or any other part of his body (during his expression).

274.sa: अविस्तरमसन्दिग्धमविलम्बितमद्रुतम्। उरस्थं कण्ठगं वाक्यं वर्तते मध्यमे स्वरे4.3.31।।
274.e: His sentences are not too elaborate, not ambiguous, not dragging, not fast, raised in the chest or throat, in a medium tone.

274.sa: संस्कारक्रमसम्पन्नामद्रुतामविलम्बिताम्। उच्चारयति कल्याणीं वाचं हृदयहारिणीम्4.3.32।।
274.e: 'His words are auspicious. They are refined. Neither fast nor slow, his utterances captivate the heart.

274.sa: अनया चित्रया वाचा त्रिस्थानव्यञ्जनस्थया। कस्य नाराध्यते चित्तमुद्यतासेररेरपि4.3.33।।
274.e: 'His colourful words flow from all the three sources: the bottom of his bosom, his throat and his head. Whose mind will not adore them even if one happens to be an enemy holding a sword?

274.sa: एवं विधो यस्य दूतो न भवेत्पार्थिवस्य तु। सिद्ध्यन्ति हि कथं तस्य कार्याणां गतियोऽनघ4.3.34।।
274.e: 'O sinless one, how can a king, whoever he be, not accomplish his goal in the past with such an ambassador?

274.sa: एवं गुणगणैर्युक्ता यस्य स्युः कार्यसाधकाः। तस्य सिध्यन्ति सर्वाऽर्था दूतवाक्यप्रचोदिताः4.3.35।।
274.e: Whoever has such great taskmasters of great qualities as their envoys, can have all their goals accomplished, driven by their diplomatic skills.

274.sa: एवमुक्तस्तु सौमित्रिस्सुग्रीवसचिवं कपिम्। अभ्यभाषत वाक्यज्ञो वाक्यज्ञं पवनात्मजम्4.3.36।।
274.e: Thus instructed, Saumitri who was equally skilled in speach replied to Sugriva's minister, son of the Windgod

274.sa: विदितौ नौ गुणा विद्वंत्सुग्रीवस्य महात्मनः। तमेव चाऽवां मार्गावस्सुग्रीवं प्लवगेश्वरम्4.3.37।।
274.e: 'O learned Hanuman having heard about the virtues of  great Sugriva, lord of the monkeys, we eagerly look forward to meeting him

274.sa: यथा ब्रवीषि हनुमान्सुग्रीववचनादिह। तत्तथा हि करिष्यावो वचनात्तव सत्तम4.3.38।।
274.e: 'O virtuous Hanuman we will do whatever you are saying, for it is the message of Sugriva.

274.sa: तत्तस्य वाक्यं निपुणं निशम्य प्रहृष्टरूपः पवनात्मजः कपिः। मनस्समाधाय जयोपपत्तौ सख्यं तदा कर्तुमियेष ताभ्याम्4.3.39।।
274.e: Pleased with Lakshmana's words spoken in a skilful manner, Hanuman, the monkey son of the Windgod, resolved to make friendship with them. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये किष्किन्धाकाण्डे तृतीयस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the third sarga of Kishkindakanda of the Holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

275.sa: ततः प्रहृष्टौ हनुमान्कृत्यवानिति तद्वचः। श्रुत्वा मधुरसम्भाषं  सुग्रीवं मनसा गतः4.4.1।।
275.e: After listening to the sweet words of Lakshmana, Hanuman, having done what he had to do felt happy and thought of Sugriva.

275.sa: भव्यो राज्यागमस्तस्य सुग्रीवस्य महात्मनः। यदयं कृत्यवान्प्राप्तः कृत्यं चैतदुपागतम्4.4.2।।
275.e: The great Sugriva, thinks Hanuman, who had done his duty is likely to acquire his kingdom, because great Rama who would help in the work of Sugriva has also come.'

275.sa: ततः परमसंहृष्टो हनुमान् प्लवगर्षभः। प्रत्युवाच ततो वाक्यं रामं वाक्यविशारदः4.4.3।।
275.e: Hanuman, the best of the monkeys, learned in conversation, felt extremely happy and enquired from Rama:

275.sa: किमिर्थं त्वं वनं घोरं पम्पाकाननमण्डितम्। आगतस्सानुजो दुर्गं नानाव्याळमृगायुतम्4.4.4।।
275.e: 'Why have you come with your brother to this dreadful, inaccessible forest surrounding Pampa, full of different varieties of serpents and wild animals?'

275.sa: तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा लक्ष्मणो रामचोदितः। आचचक्षे महात्मानं रामं दशरथात्मजम्4.4.5।।
275.e: Having listened to Hanuman, and urged by Rama, Lakshmana told him about the great Rama, son of Dasaratha.

275.sa: राजा दशरथो नाम द्युतिमान्धर्मवत्सलः। चातुर्वर्ण्यं स्वधर्मेण नित्यमेवाभ्यपालयत्4.4.6।।
न द्वेष्टा विद्यते तस्य न च स द्वेष्टि कञ्चन। स च सर्वेषु भूतेषु पितामह इवापरः4.4.7।। अग्निष्टोमादिभिर्यज्ञैरिष्टवानाप्तदक्षिणैः।
275.e: 'He never hated any one nor did any one ever hate him. To all his subjects, he was like another father, the Creator Brahma. And he was generous in giving gifts while performing yajnas (rituals with fire) like Agnistoma.

275.sa: तस्यायं पूर्वजः पुत्रो रामो नाम जनैः श्रुतः।।4.4.8।। शरण्यस्सर्वभूतानां पितुर्निर्देशपारगः।
275.e: 'Here is his eldest son, popularly known as Rama. He is the protector of all beings and never failed his father's instructions.

275.sa: वीरो दशरथस्यायं पुत्राणां गुणवत्तमः।।4.4.9।। राजलक्षणसम्पन्नस्सम्युक्तो राजसम्पदा। राज्याद्भ्रष्टो वने वस्तुं मया सार्धमिहागतः4.4.10।।
वीरो दशरथस्यायं पुत्राणां गुणवत्तमः।।4.4.9।। राजलक्षणसम्पन्नस्सम्युक्तो राजसम्पदा। राज्याद्भ्रष्टो वने वस्तुं मया सार्धमिहागतः4.4.10।।
भार्यया च महातेजास्सीतयाऽनुगतो वशी। दिनक्षये महातेजाः प्रभयेव दिवाकरः4.4.11।।
275.e: 'This glorious Rama was followed by his wife, Sita, like the rays of the effulgent Sun follow him to the end of the day.

275.sa: अहमस्यावरो भ्राता गुणैर्दास्यमुपागतः। कृतज्ञस्य बहुज्ञस्य लक्ष्मणो नाम नामतः4.4.12।।
275.e: 'I am his younger brother, called Lakshmana. I have accepted the service of this learned, virtuous and grateful man.

275.sa: सुखार्हस्य महार्हस्य सर्वभूतहितात्मनः। ऐश्वर्येण च हीनस्य वनवासाश्रितस्य च4.4.13।। रक्षसाऽपहृता भार्या रहिते कामरूपिणा। तच्च न ज्ञायते रक्षः पत्नी येनास्य सा हृता4.4.14।।
275.e: 'This man who should have lived in comfort and in reverence, one who was worthy of all the wellwishers lost his wealth and was banished into the forest. He is now deprived of his wife kidnapped by an unknown demon who could assume any form at will.

275.sa: सुखार्हस्य महार्हस्य सर्वभूतहितात्मनः। ऐश्वर्येण च हीनस्य वनवासाश्रितस्य च4.4.13।। रक्षसाऽपहृता भार्या रहिते कामरूपिणा। तच्च न ज्ञायते रक्षः पत्नी येनास्य सा हृता4.4.14।।
