282.sa: स एव संशयस्तात तव तस्य च यद्बले4.11.90।। सालमेकं तु निर्भिद्या भवेद्व्यक्तिर्बलाबले।
282.e: 'O Dear, therefore, I have my doubt about your relative strength. If you can split a sala tree with a single arrow then can your strength or weakness be demonstrated.

282.sa: कृत्वेदं कार्मुकं सज्यं हस्तिहस्त मिवाततम्4.11.91।। आकर्णपूर्णमायम्य विसृजस्व महाशरम्।
282.e: 'Now string your bow, draw it like the trunk of an elephant up to your ear and release the great arrow.

282.sa: इमं हि सालं सहित स्त्वया शरो न संशयोऽत्रास्ति विदारयिष्यति। अलं विमर्शेन मम प्रियं ध्रुवं कुरुष्व राजात्मज शापितो मया4.11.92।।
282.e: 'It will be enough and my doubt will be cleared. If you can pierce the sala tree with your arrow it will be my pleasure and not a test of your strength.

282.sa: यथा हि तेजस्सु वरस्सदा रवि र्यथा हि शैलो हिमवान्महाद्रिषु। यथा चतुष्पात्सु च केसरी वर स्तथा नरणामसि विक्रमे वरः4.11.93।।
282.e: 'Just as the Sun is the best among the brilliant, the Himalayas among the great mountains, the lion among the quadrupeds, so also you are the best among men of valour.' इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये किष्किन्धाकाण्डे एकादशस्सर्गः।। Thus ends  the eleventh sarga of Kishkindakanda of the Holy Ramayana, the first epic, composed by sage Valmiki.

283.sa: एतच्च वचनं श्रुत्वा सुग्रीवेण सुभाषितम्। प्रत्ययार्थं महातेजा रामो जग्राह कार्मुकम्4.12.1।।
283.e: Having heard Sugriva's pleasing words, the brilliant Rama took up the bow in order to inspire confidence in Sugriva.

283.sa: स गृहीत्वा धनुर्घोरं शरमेकं च मानदः। सालमुद्दिश्य चिक्षेप ज्यास्वनैः पूरयन्दिशः। 4.12.2।।
283.e: Rama, subduer of the enemy's pride, strung his terrific bow, produced the twang that filled all directions, and discharged a single arrow aimed at the sala tree.

283.sa: स विसृष्टो बलवता बाणस्स्वर्णपरिष्कृतः। भित्त्वा सालान् गिरिप्रस्थं सप्त भूमिं विवेश ह4.12.3।।
283.e: Released with great force, Rama's arrow embellished with gold pierced through the seven sala trees and splitting the mountain terrain entered the earth.

283.sa: प्रविष्टश्च मुहूर्तेन धरां भित्त्वा महाजवः। निष्पत्य च पुनस्तूर्णं स्वतूणीं प्रविवेश ह4.12.4।।
283.e: In a moment the arrow emerged from the earth which it pierced and reentered the quiver with great speed.

283.sa: तान्दृष्ट्वा सप्त निर्भिन्नान्सालान्वानरपुङ्गवः। रामस्य शरवेगेन विस्मयं परमं गतः4.12.5।।
283.e: The chief of the monkeys was struck with wonder seeing Rama's arrow piercing through  the seven sala trees so swiftly.

283.sa: स मूर्ध्ना न्यपतदभ्मौ प्रलम्बीकृतभूषणः। सुग्रीवः परमप्रीतो राघवाय कृताञ्जलिः4.12.6।।
283.e: Sugriva was immensely happy and offered obeisance to Rama with folded hands and bowed down and prostrated while his ornaments touched the ground.

283.sa: इदं चोवाच धर्मज्ञं कर्मणा तेन हर्षितः। रामं सर्वास्त्रविदुषां श्रेष्ठं शूरमवस्थितम्4.12.7।।
283.e: Sugriva who stood by, elated to watch the deed of Rama, best among the valiant, proficient in the use of arms of all kinds and knower of dharma, said:

283.sa: सेन्द्रानपि सुरान्सर्वांस्त्वं बाणैः पुरुषर्षभ। समर्थस्समरे हन्तुं किं पुन र्वालिनं प्रभो 4.12.8।।
283.e: 'O bull among men, O lord, you are capable of killing with your arrows even the gods including Indra in the battle, what to speak of Vali.

283.sa: येन सप्तमहासाला गिरिर्भूमिश्च दारिताः। बाणेनैकेन काकुत्स्थ स्थाता ते को रणाग्रतः4.12.9।।
283.e: 'O Rama who can in a battle confront you, capable of splitting seven huge sala trees, the mountain and the earth with a single arrow?

283.sa: अद्य मे विगतश्शोकः प्रीतिरद्य परा मम। सुहृदं त्वां समासाद्य महेन्द्रवरुणोपमम्4.12.10।।
283.e: 'Having found a friend in you comparable to Indra and Varuna, my grief is gone and I am so happy now.

283.sa: तमद्यैव प्रियार्थं मे वैरिणं भ्रातृरूपिणम्। वालिनं जहि काकुत्स्थ मया बद्धोऽयमञ्जलिः4.12.11।।
283.e: 'O Rama, for my pleasure kill Vali who is, to me, an enemy in the guise of a brother. I fold my hands to you.

283.sa: ततो रामः परिष्वज्य सुग्रीवं प्रियदर्शनम्। प्रत्युवाच महाप्राज्ञो लक्ष्मणानुगतं वचः4.12.12।।
283.e: Then wise Rama embraced handsome Sugriva and replied in these words which were agreeable to Lakshmana:

283.sa: अस्माद्गच्छेम किष्किन्धां क्षिप्रं गच्छ त्वमग्रतः। गत्वा चाह्वय सुग्रीव वालिनं भ्रातृगन्धिनम्4.12.13।।
283.e: 'O Sugriva, get ready at once. We will promptly proceed to Kishkinda from here. Go ahead and challenge Vali, your brother only in name, to a combat.'

283.sa: सर्वे ते त्वरितं गत्वा किष्किन्धां वालिनः पुरीम्। वृक्षैरात्मानमावृत्य व्यतिष्ठन्गहने वने4.12.14।।
283.e: Thay all rushed to Kishkinda, the capital of Vali and waited in the thick forest behind the trees.

283.sa: सुग्रीवो व्यनदद्घोरं वालिनोऽऽह्वानकारणात्। गाढं परिहितो वेगान्नादैर्भिन्दन्निवाम्बरम्4.12.15।।
283.e: Sugriva tightened up his waist cloth hurriedly and roared terrifically as though piercing the sky. And screamed  for Vali.

283.sa: तं श्रुत्वा निनदं भ्रातुः क्रुद्धो वाली महाबलः। निश्चक्राम सुसंरब्धो भास्करोऽस्ततटादिव4.12.16।।
283.e: On hearing his brother roaring, powerful Vali was enraged and rushed like the Sun from behind the western shore of the ocean (this simile suggests the downfall of Vali).

283.sa: ततस्सुतुमुलं युद्धं वालिसुग्रीवयोरभूत्। गगने ग्रहयोर्घोरं बुधाङ्गारकयोरिव4.12.17।।
283.e: Then a tumultuous combat took place between Vali and Sugriva who looked like the planets Mercury and Mars.

283.sa: तलैरशनिकल्पैश्च वज्रकल्पैश्च मुष्टिभिः। जघ्नतुस्समरेऽन्योन्यं भ्रातरौ क्रोधमूर्छितौ4.12.18।।
283.e: The brothers, insensate with fury, struck each other like thunder with their palms, soles  and fists in the combat.

283.sa: ततो रामो धनुष्पाणिस्तावुभौ समुदीक्ष्यतु। अन्योन्यसदृशौ वीरावुभौ देवाविवाश्विनौ4.12.19।।
283.e: Bow in hand, Rama watched both the heroes who resembled the twin Aswini Kumaras.

283.sa: यन्नावगच्छत्सुग्रीवं वालिनं वापि राघवः। ततो न कृतवान्बुद्धिं मोक्तुमन्तकरं शरम्4.12.20।।
283.e: Since Rama was not able to distinguish between Vali and Sugriva, he could not decide whether he should discharge his deadly arrow .

283.sa: एतस्मिन्नन्तरे भग्नस्सुग्रीवस्तेन वालिना। अपश्यन्राघवं नाथमृश्यमूकं प्रदुद्रुवे4.12.21।।
283.e: Discomfited  by Vali, and not seeing Rama around, Sugriva ran towards Rishyamuka mountain.

283.sa: क्लान्तो रुधिरसिक्ताङ्गः प्रहारैर्जर्झरीकृतः। वालिनाऽभिद्रुतः क्रोधात्प्रविवेश महावनम्4.12.22।।
283.e: Exhausted, disfigured and body mauled and drenched in blood all over, Sugriva, chased by the infuriated Vali, entered the region of  great sage Matanga.

283.sa: तं प्रविष्टं वनं दृष्ट्वा वाली शापभयार्दितः। मुक्तो ह्यसि त्वमित्युक्त्वा स निवृत्तो महाद्युतिः4.12.23।।
283.e: Effulgent Vali saw Sugriva entering the (prohibited) grove and turned back due to the fear of the curse (of sage Matanga) saying, 'You have escaped'.

283.sa: राघवोऽसि सह भ्रात्रा सह चैव हनूमता। तदेव वनमागच्छत्सुग्रीवो यत्र वानरः4.12.24।।
283.e: Rama together with Lakshmana and Hanuman also arrived at the same gave where  Sugriva was.

283.sa: तं समीक्ष्यागतं रामं सुग्रीवस्सहलक्ष्मणम्। ह्रीमान्दीनमुवाचेदं वसुधामवलोकयन्4.12.25।।
283.e: At the sight of Rama accompanied by Lakshmana, Sugriva felt ashmed and aggrieved, and looking down on the ground, said:

283.sa: आह्वयस्वेति मामुक्त्वा दर्शयित्वा च विक्रमम्। वैरिणा घातयित्वा च किमिदानीं त्वया कृतम्4.12.26।।
283.e: 'You demonstrated your prowess and directed me to challenge Vali and then why did you make the enemy hit me thus?

283.sa: तामेन वेलां वक्तव्यं त्वया राघव तत्त्वतः। वालिनं न निहन्मीति ततो नाहमितो व्रजे4.12.27।।
283.e: 'Had you, in fact, told me that you were not going to kill Vali, I would not have budged from this place.'

283.sa: तस्य चैवं ब्रुवाणस्य सुग्रीवस्य महात्मनः। करुणं दीनया वाचा राघवः पुनरब्रवीत्4.12.28।।
283.e: On hearing the great Sugriva's miserable and moving words, Rama again said:

283.sa: सुग्रीव श्रूयातां तात क्रोधश्च व्यपनीयताम्। कारणं येन बाणोऽयं न मया स विसर्जितः4.12.29।।
283.e: 'O dear Sugriva dispel your anger and listen to me why I had not released the arrow.

283.sa: अलङ्कारेण वेषेण प्रमाणेन गतेन च। त्वं च सुग्रीव वाली च सदृशौ स्थः परस्परम्4.12.30।।
283.e: 'O Sugriva in form, ornaments and movements there is perfect resemblance between you and Vali.

283.sa: स्वरेण वर्चसा चैव प्रेक्षितेन च वानर। विक्रमेण च वाक्यैश्च व्यक्तिं वां नोपलक्षये4.12.31।।
283.e: 'O monkey in your voice, in brightness, in looks, in valour or in words I have marked no difference between you.

283.sa: ततोऽहं रूपसादृश्यान्मोहितो वानरोत्तम। नोत्सृजामि महावेगं शरं शत्रुनिबर्हणम्4.12.32।।
283.e: 'O distinguished monkey you both are so similar in form that I was puzzled and did not release my swift arrow that could have destroyed the enemy.

283.sa: जीवितान्तकरं घोरं सादृश्यात्तु विशङ्कितः। मूलघातो न नौ स्याद्धि द्वयोरपि कृतो मया4.12.33।।
283.e: 'I was doubtful because of your similar appearance. I thought that I should not strike at the very root of the interests of both of us. Therefore, I did not release the terrific and deadly  arrow.

283.sa: त्वयि वीरे विपन्ने हि अज्ञानाल्लाघवान्मया। मौढ्यं च मम बाल्यं च ख्यापितं स्यात्कपीश्वर4.12.34।।
283.e: 'O lord of monkeys I would have betrayed my foolishness and childishness had I exposed you to danger by my ignorance and thoughtlessness.

283.sa: दत्ताभयवधो नाम पातकं महदुच्यते। अहं च लक्ष्मणश्चैव सीता च वरवर्णिनी4.12.35।। त्वदधीना वयं सर्वे वनेऽस्मिन् शरणं भवान्।
283.e: 'It is said that killing a person to whom protection is promised is highly sinful. Lakshmana, darling Sita and me, are under your care and you are our refuge.

283.sa: तस्माद्युध्यस्व भूयस्त्वं मा मा शङ्केश्च वानर4.12.36।। एतन्मुहूर्ते सुग्रीव पश्य वालिनमाहवे। निरस्तमिषुणैकेन वेष्टमानं महीतले4.12.37।।
283.e: 'Therefore, O monkey, go and engage yourself in fight again. Do not suspect me. With this single arrow of mine, in one moment you will see Vali thrown down and rolling on the ground in this combat.

283.sa: तस्माद्युध्यस्व भूयस्त्वं मा मा शङ्केश्च वानर4.12.36।। एतन्मुहूर्ते सुग्रीव पश्य वालिनमाहवे। निरस्तमिषुणैकेन वेष्टमानं महीतले4.12.37।।
283.e: 'Therefore, O monkey, go and engage yourself in fight again. Do not suspect me. With this single arrow of mine, in one moment you will see Vali thrown down and rolling on the ground in this combat.

283.sa: अभिज्ञानं कुरुष्व त्वमात्मनो वानरेश्वर। येन त्वामभिजानीयां द्वन्द्वयुद्धमुपागतम्4.12.38।।
283.e: 'O lord of monkeys while you both are engaged in a duel wear some identification mark by which I can recognise you.

283.sa: गजपुष्पीमिमां फुल्लामुत्पाट्य शुभलक्षणाम्। कुरु लक्ष्मण कण्ठेऽस्य सुग्रीवस्य महात्मनः।।4.12.39।।
283.e: 'O Lakshmana this Gajapushpi  in bloom is auspicious. Pluck and fasten it on great Sugriva's neck.'

283.sa: ततो गिरितटे जातामुत्पाट्य कुसुमाकुलाम्। लक्ष्मणो गजपुष्पीं तां तस्य कण्ठे व्यसर्जयत्4.12.40।।
283.e: Then Lakshmana went to the mountain slope, plucked the (creeper with) gajapuspi blossoms and fastened it on the neck of Sugriva.

283.sa: स तया शुशुभे श्रीमान् लतया कण्ठसक्तया। मालयेव बलाकानां ससन्ध्य इव तोयदः4.12.41।।
283.e: With the creeper round the neck, Sugriva looked like the raincloud at twilight, adorned by a row of cranes like a garland.

283.sa: विभ्राजमानो वपुषा रामवाक्यसमाहितः। जगाम सह रामेण किष्किन्थां वालिपालिताम्4.12.42।।
283.e: Radiant Sugriva intent on carrying out Rama's words again went to Kishkinda ruled by Vali. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये किष्किन्धाकाण्डे द्वादशस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the twelfth sarga of Kishkindakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

284.sa: ऋष्यमूकात्स धर्मात्मा किष्किन्धां लक्ष्मणाग्रजः। जगाम सहसुग्रीवो वालिविक्रमपालिताम्4.13.1।।
284.e: Lakshmana's righteous elder brother left Rishyamuka with Sugriva for Kishkinda protected by Vali's valour.

284.sa: समुद्यम्य महच्चापं रामः काञ्चनभूषितम्। शरांश्चादित्यसङ्काशान्गृहीत्वा रणसाधकान्4.13.2।।
284.e: Getting ready to go, Rama took up his great bow and arrows adorned with gold and potent in war looking (dazzling) like the Sun.

284.sa: अग्रतस्तु ययौ तस्य राघवस्य महात्मनः। सुग्रीवः संहतग्रीवो लक्ष्मणश्च महाबलः4.13.3।।
284.e: The strongnecked Sugriva and mighty Lakshmana walked in front of the highsouled Rama.

284.sa: पृष्ठतो हनुमान्वीरो नलो नीलश्च वानरः। तारश्चैव महातेजा हरियूथपयूथपः4.13.4।।
284.e: Brave and brilliant Hanuman, Nala, Nila, and Tara among the leaders of the monkeys  walked behind.

284.sa: ते वीक्षमाणा वृक्षांश्च पुष्पभारावलम्बिनः। प्रसन्नाम्बुवहाश्चैव सरितस्सागरङ्गमाः4.13.5।।
284.e: They saw (on the way) trees bent down with the load of flowers, and rivers with pure water flowing into the sea.

284.sa: कन्दराणि च शैलांश्च निर्दराणि गुहास्तथा। शिखराणि च मुख्यानि दरीश्च प्रियदर्शनाः4.13.6।।
284.e: (They saw) beautiful valleys, mountains, caves, prominent peaks with deep caverns.

284.sa: वैढूर्यविमलै:पर्णै पद्मैश्चाकोशकुट्मलैः। शोभितांत्सजलान्मार्गे तटाकांश्च व्यलोकयन्4.13.7।।
284.e: Observing on the way delightful lotus buds with leaves like Vaidurya, clear water and full tanks (They moved on).

284.sa: कारण्डैस्सारसैर्हंसैर्वञ्जुलैर्जलकुक्कुटैः। चक्रवाकै स्तथा चान्यैश्शकुनैः रुपनादितान्4.13.8।।
284.e: Ducks, cranes, swans, vanjulas, waterfowls, chakravakas and other birds warbling melodiously.

284.sa: मृदुशष्पाङ्कुराहारान्निर्भयान्वनगोचरान्। चरतस्सर्वतौऽपश्यन् स्थलीषु हरिणान् स्थितान्4.13.9।।
284.e: They observed deer feeding on tender grass on the ground around without fear, some standing and some roaming the forest

284.sa: तटाकवैरिणश्चापि शुक्लदन्तविभूषितान्। घोरानेकचरान्वन्यान्द्विरदान्कूलघातिनः4.13.10।।
284.e: Observing terrific elephants adorned with white tusks wandering alone destroying the tanks, shattering the banks.

284.sa: मत्तान्गिरितटोत्कृष्टान्पर्वतानिव जङ्गमान्। वारणान्वारिदप्रख्यान्महीरेणुसमुक्षितान्4.13.11।।
284.e: (Observing) intoxicated elephants knocking the edges of mountain slopes, elephants resembling (dark) rainbearing clouds, elephants like moving mountains, elephants with dust covered all over the body.

284.sa: वने वनचरांश्चान्यान्खेचरांश्च विहङ्गमान्। पश्यन्तस्त्वरिता जग्मुस्सुग्रीववशवर्तिनः4.13.12।।
284.e: Following Sugriva faithfully, they proceeded swiftly, observing animals of the forest and birds flying in the sky.

284.sa: तेषां तु गच्छतां तत्र त्वरितं रघुनन्दनः। द्रुमषण्डं वनं दृष्ट्वा रामस्सुग्रीवमब्रवीत्4.13.13।।
284.e: While walking fast, looking at the forest full of trees Rama, the delight of the Raghus said to Sugriva:

284.sa: एष मेघ इवाकाशे वृक्षषण्डः प्रकाशते। मेघसङ्घातविपुलः पर्यन्तकदलीवृतः4.13.14।।
284.e: 'This cluster of trees surrounded by plantain groves look splendid like a vast collection of clouds in the sky.

284.sa: किमेतत् ज्ञातुमिच्छामि सखे कौतूहलं हि मे। कौतूहलापनयनं कर्तुमिच्छाम्यहं त्वया4.13.15।।
284.e: 'O friend I wish to know what this is? Could you answer my curiosity?'

284.sa: तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा राघवस्य महात्मनः। गच्छन्नेवाचचक्षेऽथ सुग्रीवस्तन्महद्वनम्4.13.16।।
284.e: On hearing great Rama's words while walking in the extensive forest,  Sugriva started narrating:

284.sa: एतद्राघव विस्तीर्णमाश्रमं श्रमनाशनम्। उद्यानवनसम्पन्नं स्वादुमूलफलोदकम्4.13.17।।
284.e: 'O Raghava this is a hermitage, enchanting with vast gardens and trees bearing sweet fruits, full of tasty roots and water that relieves tiresomeness (of travellers).

284.sa: अत्र सप्तजना नाम मुनय स्संश्रितव्रताः। सप्तैवासन्नधशशीर्षा नियतं जलशायिनः4.13.18।।
सप्तरात्रकृताहारा वायुनाचलवासिनः। दिवं वर्षशतैर्याताः सप्तभिः सकलेबराः4.13.19।।
284.e: 'These seven sages used to live on air and that too once in seven nights. They lived for seven hundred years performing penance with motionlessness and attained heaven along with their bodies.

284.sa: तेषामेवं प्रभावानां द्रुमप्राकारसंवृतम्। आश्रमस्सुदुराधर्ष अपि सेन्द्रैस्सुरासुरैः4.13.20।।
284.e: 'By virtue of the power of their penance, this hermitage surrounded by a row of trees is impenetrable even for demons and gods including Indra.

284.sa: पक्षिणो वर्जयन्त्येतत्तथाऽन्ये वनचारिणः। विशन्ति मोहाद्येऽप्यत्र निवर्तन्ते न ते पुनः4.13.21।।
284.e: 'Birds and wild animals avoid the hermitage and whoever enters there out of ignorance never returns.

284.sa: विभूषणरवास्तत्र श्रूयन्ते सकलाक्षराः। तूर्यगीतस्वनाश्चात्र गन्धो दिव्यश्च राघव4.13.22।।
284.e: 'O Rama, one can hear pleasant sounds of jingling ornaments (of nymphs), of songs and windinstruments here. One can inhale divine fragrance, too.

284.sa: त्रेताग्नयोऽपि दीप्यन्ते दूमो ह्यत्र प्रकाशते। वेष्टयन्निव वृक्षाग्रान्कपोताङ्गारुणो घनः4.13.23।।
284.e: 'The three sacred fires keep burning and the thick smoke they emit resembles the red feet of  pigeons. It shines forth as if enveloping the treetops.

284.sa: एते वृक्षाः प्रकाशन्ते धूमसंसक्तमस्तकाः। मेघजालप्रतिच्छन्ना वैढूर्यगिरयो यथा4.13.24।।
284.e: 'These treetops covered with thick smoke glow like mountains of Vaidurya concealed by a cluster of clouds.

284.sa: कुरु प्रणामं धर्मात्मंस्तेषामुद्दिश्य राघव। लक्ष्मणेव सह भ्रात्रा प्रयन्तस्सयताञ्जलिः4.13.25।।
284.e: 'O rigteous Rama you and your brother Lakshmana humbly offer obeisance to them(sacred hermitage and sages Saptajana) with folded hands and meditate on them.

284.sa: प्रणमन्ति हि ये तेषां मुनीनां भावितात्मनाम्। न तेषामशुभं किञ्चिच्छरीरे राम दृश्यते4.13.26।।
284.e: 'O Rama, nothing inauspicious happens to them who offer obeisance to those highly spiritual sacred sages.'

284.sa: ततो रामस्सह भ्रात्रा लक्ष्मणेन कृताञ्जलिः। समुद्दिश्य महात्मानस्तानृषीनभ्यवादयत्4.13.27।।
284.e: Rama and Lakshmana  offered salutations with folded hands in memory of those great sages, great souls.

284.sa: अभिवाद्य तु धर्मात्मा रामो भ्राता च लक्ष्मणः। सुग्रीवो वानराश्चैव जग्मुसंहृष्टमानसाः4.13.28।।
284.e: Righteous Rama, Lakshmana, Sugriva and all the monkeys offered obeisance and proceeded delighted at heart.

284.sa: ते गत्वा दूरमध्वानं तस्मात्सप्तजनाश्रमात्। ददृशुस्तां दुराधर्षां किष्किन्धां वालिपालिताम्4.13.29।।
284.e: Walking a long distance from the hermitage of the seven seers, they beheld the unassailable Kishkinda ruled by Vali.

284.sa: ततस्तु रामानुजरामवानराः प्रगृह्य शस्त्राण्युदिताग्र्यतेजसः। पुरीं सुरेशात्मजवीर्यपालितां वधाय शत्रोः पुनरागतास्सह4.13.30।।
284.e: Rama and Lakshmana of fierce lustre, and the monkeys took hold of the weapons to kill the enemy and reached the capital ruled by the valour of Vali, son of Indra. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये किष्किन्धाकाण्डे त्रयोदशस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the thirteenth sarga of Kishkindakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

285.sa: सर्वे ते त्वरितं गत्वा किष्किन्धां वालि पालिताम्। वृक्षैरात्मानमावृत्य व्यतिष्ठन् गहने वने4.14.1।।
285.e: They all at once went to Kishkinda ruled by Vali and there waited hiding behind the trees in the dense forest.

285.sa: विचार्य सर्वतो दृष्टिं कानने काननप्रियः। सुग्रीवो विपुलग्रीवः क्रोधमाहारयद्भृशम्4.14.2।।
285.e: Broadnecked Sugriva, a lover of the forest, looked around and flew into a rage.

285.sa: ततस्स निनदं घोरं कृत्वा युद्धाय चाह्वयत्। परिवारैः परिवृतो नादैर्भिन्दन्निवाम्बरम्4.14.3।। गर्जन्निव महामेघो वायुवेगपुरस्सरः।
285.e: Sugriva, surrounded by his companions, raised his voice as if piercing the sky, roaring like a huge thundering cloud, challenging Vali to a duel.

285.sa: अथ बालार्कसदृशो दृप्तसिंहगतिस्तदा4.14.4।। दृष्ट्वा रामं क्रियादक्षं सुग्रीवो वाक्यमब्रवीत्।
285.e: Sugriva, proficient in the performance of any task, one who appeared like the rising Sun and moved like a proud lion, said to Rama:

285.sa: हरिवागुरया व्याप्तां तप्तकाञ्चनतोरणाम्। प्राप्ताः स्म ध्वजयन्त्राढ्यां किष्किन्धां वालिनः पुरीम्।।4.14.5।।
285.e: 'We have arrived at Kishkinda, the capital of Vali, decorated with flags and having a glittering golden archway that can be opened mechanically. Teeming with monkeys, it looks like a snare to catch the enemy.

285.sa: प्रतिज्ञा या त्वया वीर कृता वालिवधे पुरा। सफलां कुरु तां क्षिप्रं लतां काल इवागतः4.14.6।।
285.e: 'O heroic Rama fulfil quickly the vow taken by you earlier to kill Vali in the same way  a creeper bears fruit when the time comes.'

285.sa: एवमुक्तस्तु धर्मात्मा सुग्रीवेण स राघवः। तमेवोवाच वचनं सुग्रीवं शत्रुसूदनः4.14.7।।
285.e: Requested thus by Sugriva, righteous Rama, the destroyer of enemies, replied:.

285.sa: कृताभिज्ञानचिह्नस्त्व मनया गजसाह्वया। लक्ष्मणेन समुत्पाट्य यैषा कण्ठे कृता तव4.14.8।।
285.e: 'Lakshmana has uprooted a creeper of  gaja, and fastened it on your neck by which you can be easily identified.

285.sa: शोभसेऽह्यधिकं वीर लतया कण्ठसक्तया। विपरीत इवाकाशे सूर्यो नक्षत्रमालया4.14.9।।
285.e: 'O hero, you are shining with the creeper fastened to your neck , just as the fullmoon adorned with a cluster of stars shines in the sky.

285.sa: अद्य वालिसमुत्थं ते भयं वैरं च वानर। एकेनाहं प्रमोक्ष्यामि बाणमोक्षेण संयुगे4.14.10।।
285.e: 'O monkey, with the release of a single arrow in the combat, I shall dispel your fear and enmity (hatred) for Vali.

285.sa: मम दर्शय सुग्रीव वैरिणं भ्रातृरूपिणम्। वाली विनिहतो यावद्वने पांसुषु वेष्टते4.14.11।।
285.e: 'O Sugriva show me your enemy,who is in the guise of your brother.He will be killed. He will roll down in the dust of the forest.

285.sa: यदि दृष्टिपथं प्राप्तो जीवन्स विनिवर्तते। ततो दोषेण मा गच्छेत्सद्यो गर्हेच्च मा भवान्4.14.12।।
285.e: 'If Vali appears before me I will not let him go with life.Then you will not blame me and find fault with me.

285.sa: प्रत्यक्षं सप्त ते साला मया बाणेन दारिताः। तेनावेहि बलेनाद्य वालिनं निहतं मया4.14.13।।
285.e: 'You have seen how I have pierced through seven sala trees with a single arrow. You will know how with the same strength I will kill Vali.'

285.sa: अनृतं नोक्तपूर्वं मे वीर कृच्छ्रेऽपि तिष्टता। धर्मलोभपरीतेन न च वक्ष्ये कथञ्चन4.14.14।।
285.e: 'O Sugriva, I have uttered no falsehood before for fear of deviation from righteousness although I was in distress, nor shall I utter any falsehood in any circumstances hereafter.

285.sa: सफलां च करिष्यामि प्रतिज्ञां जहि सम्भ्रमम्। प्रसूतं कलमं क्षेत्रे वर्षेणेव शतक्रतुः4.14.15।।
285.e: 'I shall fulfil my promise just as Indra (who performed a hundred sacrifices) helps production in the cornfield through timely rain. Give up your apprehension.

285.sa: तदाह्वाननिमित्तं त्वं वालिनो हेममालिनः। सुग्रीव कुरु तं शब्दं निष्पतेद्येन वानरः4.14.16।।
285.e: 'O Sugriva give a warcry so that Vali adorned with a golden garland will come out.

285.sa: जितकाशी बलश्लाघी त्वया चाधर्षितः पुरा। निष्पतिष्यत्यसङ्गेन वाली स प्रियसंयुगः4.14.17।।
285.e: 'Vali, who is proud of  his valour,  is strong, fearless and fond of combat, will rush out of the city in response to your challenge.

285.sa: रिपूणां धर्षिण शूरा मर्षयन्ति न संयुगे। जानन्तस्तु स्वकं वीर्यं स्त्रीसमक्षं विशेषतः4.14.18।।
285.e: 'Proud of their own prowess, heroes will not brook the challenge of foes in battle, specially in the presence of women.'

285.sa: स तु रामवचश्श्रुत्वा सुग्रीवो हेमपिङ्गलः। ननर्द क्रूरनादेन विनिर्भिन्दन्निवाम्बरम्4.14.19।।
285.e: On hearing Rama's words, the goldenhued Sugriva roared in a fierce voice as if it would piece  the sky.

285.sa: तस्य शब्देन वित्रस्ता गावो यान्ति हतप्रभाः। राजदोषपरामृष्टाः कुलस्त्रिय इवाकुलाः4.14.20।।
285.e: Alarmed at the yelling of Sugriva, the cows began to run in all directions, like the  women of noble pedigree who, with their brightness lost, run perplexed for failure of the king to protect their chastity.

285.sa: द्रवन्ति च मृगाश्शीघ्रं भग्ना इव रणे हयाः। पतन्ति च खगा भूमौ क्षीणपुण्या इव ग्रहाः4.14.21।।
285.e: The deer were unable to run like wounded horses in a battle. Birds fell down on the ground like planets fall when their merit is exhausted.

285.sa: ततस्सजीमूतगणप्रणादो नादं ह्यमुञ्चत्त्वरया प्रतीतः। सूर्यात्मजश्शौर्यविवृद्धतेजाः सरित्पतिर्वाऽनिलचञ्चलोर्मिः4.14.22।।
285.e: Then Sugriva, son of the Sungod, with his lustre enhanced by his valour moved swiftly. His roar resembled the rumbling of a cluster of thundering clouds. He gave a warcry the tone of which resembled the sounds of waves lashed by high velocity winds in the sea. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये किष्किन्धाकाण्डे चतुर्दशस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the fourteenth sarga of Kishkindakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

286.sa: अथ तस्य निनादं तं सुग्रीवस्य महात्मनः। शुश्रावान्तः पुर गतो वाली भ्रातुरमर्षणः4.15.1।।
286.e: The indignant Vali, who was in the harem, heard the roaring of his venerable brother, Sugriva.

286.sa: श्रुत्वा तु तस्य निनदं सर्वभूतप्रकम्पनम्। मदश्चैकपदे नष्टः क्रोधश्चापतितो महान्4.15.2।।
286.e: The roar (of Sugriva) that frightened all beings gave Vali's vanity a jolt and at once   aroused in him violent rage.

286.sa: स तु रोषपरीताङ्गो वाली सन्ध्याकनकप्रभः। उपरक्त इवादित्यस्सद्यो निष्प्रभतां गतः4.15.3।।
286.e: Overcome with anger, Vali looked pale like the eclipsed Sun with the golden radiance faded from  his face.

286.sa: वाली दंष्ट्राकरालस्तु क्रोधाद्दीप्ताग्निसन्निभः। भात्युत्पतितपद्मस्तु समृणाळ इव ह्रदः4.15.4।।
286.e: Vali, who looked fierce with his teeth and whose eyes shone like a flaming fire through anger looked like a pond with the lotuses and their stalks uprooted.

286.sa: शब्दं दुर्मर्षणं श्रुत्वा निष्पपात ततो हरिः। वेगेन चरणन्यासैर्दारयन्निव मेदिनीम्4.15.5।।
286.e: Unable to tolerate Sugriva's roar, Vali stepped out hurriedly, taking long strides as if breaking the earth.

286.sa: तं तु तारा परिष्वज्य स्नेहाद्दर्शितसौहृदाः। उवाच त्रस्तसम्भ्रान्ता हितोदर्कमिदं वचः4.15.6।।
286.e: Tara, perplexed out of fear, glanced at Vali lovingly, embraced him and gave him wise counsel:

286.sa: साधु क्रोधमिमं वीर नदीवेगमिवागतम्। शयनादुत्थितः काल्यं त्यज भुक्तामिव स्रजम्4.15.7।।
286.e: 'O valiant Vali anger has overtaken you like the flood of a river. It is natural for you to be angry at this time, but shake off your anger just as the wise discard a flower  garland already used up.

286.sa: काल्यमेतेन सङ्ग्रामं करिष्यसि च वानर। वीर ते शत्रुबाहुल्यं फल्गुता वा न विद्यते4.15.8।।
286.e: 'O monkey fight him only tomorrow morning. By this you are not going to prove your weakness or increase your respect for the enemy.

286.sa: सहसा तव निष्क्रामो मम तावन्न रोचते। श्रूयतां चाभिधास्यामि यन्निमित्तं निवार्यसे4.15.9।।
286.e: 'I do not like your rashness. I will explain the reason I am preventing you. Listen:

286.sa: पूर्वमापतितः क्रोधात्स त्वामाह्वयते युधि। निष्पत्य च निरस्तस्ते हन्यमानो दिशो गतः4.15.10।।
286.e: 'Earlier, he (Sugriva) came  and challenged you to a duel. You struck him in anger, and defeated, he fled, running in all directions. Now his challenge rouses my suspicion.

286.sa: त्वया तस्य निरस्तस्य पीडितस्य विशेषतः। इहैत्य पुनराह्वानं शङ्कां जनयतीव मे4.15.11।।
286.e: 'One who is defeated and badly mauled by you is again coming and inviting you to a duel in this manner arouses suspicion in me.

286.sa: दर्पश्च व्यवसायश्च यादृशस्तस्य नर्दतः। निनादश्चापि संरम्भो नैतदल्पं हि कारणम्4.15.12।।
286.e: 'His determination, his insolence, his roaring, his arroganceall this cannot be for a small reason.

286.sa: नासहायमहं मन्ये सुग्रीवं तमिहागतम्। अवष्टब्धसहायश्च यमाश्रित्यैष गर्जति4.15.13।।
286.e: 'Certainly Sugriva has not come here to give a warcry without any external help. The person whose refuge he has sought is not a small one.

286.sa: प्रकृत्या निपुणश्चैव बुद्धिमांश्चैव वानरः। अपरीक्षितवीर्येण सुग्रीवस्सहनैष्यति।।4.15.14।।
286.e: 'Sugriva is clever by nature. He is wise. Without assessing the ability of the ally he will not enter into friendship.

286.sa: पूर्वमेव मया वीर श्रुतं कथयतो वचः। अङ्गदस्य कुमारस्य वक्ष्यामित्वा हितं वचः4.15.15।।
286.e: 'O hero I have heard the news earlier from our son Angada. I will tell you what he had heard and what he has said to me:

286.sa: अङ्गदस्तु कुमारोऽयं वनान्तमुपनिर्गतः। प्रवृत्तिस्तेन कथिता चारै राप्तैर्निवेदिता4.15.16।।
286.e: 'When our son Angada was out into the forest he had collected some reports from the spies which he has transmitted to me.

286.sa: अयोध्याधिपतेः पुत्रौ शूरौ समरदुर्जयौ। इक्ष्वाकूणां कुले जातौ प्रथितौ रामलक्ष्मणौ4.15.17।। सुग्रीवप्रियकामार्थं प्राप्तौ तत्र दुरासदौ।
286.e: 'Rama and Lakshmana, two heroic sons of the king of Ayodhya born of the Ikshvaku race, are invincible in war. They have come there to help Sugriva.

286.sa: तव भ्रातुर्हि विख्यातस्सहायो रणकर्कशः। रामः परबलामर्दी युगान्ताग्निरिवोत्थितः4.15.18।।
286.e: 'Rama, famous for crushing foes in war, like the fire that breaks out at the dissolution of the world, has slain strong enemies like Khara and will help your brother.

286.sa: निवासवृक्षः साधूनामापन्नानां परा गतिः। आर्तानां संश्रयश्चैव यशसश्चैकभाजनम्4.15.19।।
286.e: 'He is like a sheltering tree to the virtuous, an ultimate refuge for the destitutes and a protector of the distressed. He is the sole repository of fame.

286.sa: ज्ञानविज्ञानसम्पन्नो निदेशे निरतः पितुः। धातूनामिव शैलेन्द्रो गुणानामाकरो महान्4.15.20।।
286.e: 'He is endowed with the knowledge of science and scriptures. He stood by his father's command. He is like a mine of virtues just as the lord of the mountain is  a mine of minerals.

286.sa: तत्क्षमं न विरोधस्ते सह तेन महात्मना। दुर्जयेनाप्रमेयेन रामेण रणकर्मसु4.15.21।।
286.e: 'Rama is immeasurable in prowess and unconquerable in war. Therefore, enmity with him is not desirable for you.

286.sa: शूर वक्ष्यामि ते किञ्चिन्न चेच्छाम्यभ्यसूयितुम्। श्रूयतां क्रियतां चैव तव वक्ष्यामि यद्धितम्4.15.22।।
286.e: 'O hero, this I tell you not because I dislike you, but because I wish your welfare. Listen, and do as I say

286.sa: यौवराज्येन सुग्रीवं तूर्णं साध्वभिषेचय। विग्रहं मा कृथा वीर भ्रात्रा राजन्बलीयसा4.15.23।।
286.e: 'O king O hero consecrate your brother Sugriva as prince at once. Do not create enmity with him.

286.sa: अहं हि ते क्षमं मन्ये तेन रामेण सौहृदम्। सुग्रीवेण च सम्प्रीतिं वैरमुत्सृज्य दूरतः4.15.24।।
286.e: 'Leave enmity with Sugriva far behind. Make friendship with Rama. I think it is the right thing for you.

286.sa: लालनीयो हि ते भ्राता यवीयानेष वानरः। तत्र वा सन्निहस्थो वा सर्वथा बन्धुरेव ते4.15.25।।
286.e: 'This monkey is your younger brother and, therefore, deserves your protection. Whether he is here or there, he is your brother.

286.sa: न हि तेन समं बन्धुं भुवि पश्यामि कञ्चन4.15.26।। दानमानादिसत्कारैः कुरुष्व प्रत्यनन्तरम्। वैरमेतत्समुत्सृज्य तव पार्श्वे स तिष्ठतु4.15.27।।
286.e: 'Indeed I do not see any of your relatives comparable to him on earth. Give up enmity with him. Give him wealth. Give him respect. Keep him by your side.

286.sa: न हि तेन समं बन्धुं भुवि पश्यामि कञ्चन4.15.26।। दानमानादिसत्कारैः कुरुष्व प्रत्यनन्तरम्। वैरमेतत्समुत्सृज्य तव पार्श्वे स तिष्ठतु4.15.27।।
286.e: 'Indeed I do not see any of your relatives comparable to him on earth. Give up enmity with him. Give him wealth. Give him respect. Keep him by your side.

286.sa: सुग्रीवो विपुलग्रीवस्तवबन्धुस्सदा मतः। भ्रातृस्सौहृदमालम्ब नान्या गतिरिहास्ति ते4.15.28।।
286.e: 'Extend your brotherly affection to broadnecked Sugriva. He is always your great relation. There is no alternative for you other than this at present.

286.sa: यदि ते मत्प्रियं कार्यं यदि चावैषि मां हिताम्। याच्यमानः प्रयत्नेन साधु वाक्यं कुरुष्व मे4.15.29।।
286.e: 'Pray, do me this favour. Treat me as your wellwisher. Heed my  advice given with care.

286.sa: प्रसीद पथ्यं शृणु जल्पितं हि मे न रोष मेवानुविधातुमर्हसि। क्षमो हि ते कोसलराजसूनुना न विग्रहश्शक्रसमानतेजसा4.15.30।।
286.e: 'Do not lose your temper. Quieten your mind. My advice is beneficial to you. You should not  fight with the prince of Kosala who is comparable to Indra in splendour.It is not proper for you.'

286.sa: तदा हि तारा हितमेव वाक्यं तं वालिनं पथ्यमिदं बभाषे। न रोचते तद्वचनं हि तस्य कालाभिपन्नस्य विनाशकाले4.15.31।।
286.e: Even though Tara gave good counsel to Vali at the hour of destruction, the advice did not find favour with him as he was under the influence of unfavourable time (seized by death). इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये किष्किन्धाकाण्डे पञ्चदशस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the fifteenth sarga of Kishkindakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

287.sa: तामेवं ब्रुवतीं तारां ताराधिपनिभाननाम्। वाली निर्भर्त्सयामास वचनं चेदमब्रवीत्4.16.1।।
287.e: To these words of Tara with her Moonlike face, Vali replied reproachfully:

287.sa: गर्जतोऽस्य च सुसम्भ्रश्च भ्रातुः शत्रोर्विशेषतः। मर्षयिष्याम्यहं केन कारणेन वरानने4.16.2।।
287.e: 'O lady with a charming face why should I tolerate the enemy (Sugriva) who is none other than my own younger brother, especially when he roars excitedly?

287.sa: अधर्षितानां शूराणां समरेष्वनिवर्तिनाम्। धर्षणामर्षणं भीरु मरणादतिरिच्यते4.16.3।।
287.e: O timid lady to swallow insult (without facing the opponent) is worse than death for indomitable heroes (like me) who know no retreat in a battle.

287.sa: सोढुं न च समर्थोऽहं युद्धकामस्य संयुगे। सुग्रीवस्य च सम्रम्भं हीनग्रीवस्य गर्जतः4.16.4।।
287.e: 'When the weaknecked Sugriva roars eager to join a duel it is not right on my part to tolerate his arrogance,much less his warcry.

287.sa: न च कार्यो विषादस्ते राघवं प्रति मत्कृते। धर्मज्ञश्च कृतज्ञश्च कथं पापं करिष्यति4.16.5।।
287.e: 'You need not be concerned about me on account of Rama. How can one who knows dharma and who has a sense of gratitude commit sin?

287.sa: निवर्तस्व सह स्त्रीभिः कथं भूयोऽनुगच्छसि। सौहृदं दर्शितं तारे मयि भक्ति: कृता त्वया4.16.6।।
287.e: 'Go back with all the women of the harem. Why do you follow me again? Your devotion towards me is evident from the sincere concern expressed by you.

287.sa: प्रतियोत्स्याम्यहं गत्वा सुग्रीवं जहि सम्भ्रमम्। दर्पमात्रं विनेष्यामि न च प्राणैर्विमोक्ष्यते4.16.7।।
287.e: 'I shall accept the challenge and fight with Sugriva. Give up your anxiety. I will destroy  his pride, not his life.

287.sa: अहं ह्याजौस्थितस्यास्य करिष्यामि यथेप्सितम्। वृक्षैर्मुष्टिप्रहारैश्च पीडितः प्रतियास्यति4.16.8।।
287.e: 'When he faces me in the battlefield, I will hit him with trees and fists, and he will run back  for life.

287.sa: न मे गर्वितमायस्तं सहिष्यति दुरात्मवान्। कृतं तारे सहांयत्वं सौहृदं दर्शितं मयि4.16.9।।
287.e: 'That evilminded Sugriva cannot bear my mighty, hard blows. Tara you could shower your affection on me and extend help (in passing secret information obtained through Angada)

287.sa: शापिताऽपि मम प्राणैर्निवर्तस्व जयेन च। अहं जित्वा निवर्तिष्ये तमहं भ्रातरं रणे4.16.10।।
287.e: 'I make a vow even on my life and my victory. Pray return with the retinue. I will be back only after winning the encounter with my brother.

287.sa: तं तु तारा परिष्वज्य वालिनं प्रियवादिनी। चकार रुदती मन्दं दक्षिणा सा प्रदक्षिणम्4.16.11।।
287.e: Pleasing in her words, Tara then embraced Vali and sobbing, circumambulated Vali in compliance (to his advice).

287.sa: ततः स्वस्त्ययनं कृत्वा मन्त्रविद्विजयैषिणी। अन्तःपुरं सह स्त्रीभिः प्रविष्टा शोकमोहिता4.16.12।।
287.e: The wise counsellor, Tara bade him farewell, wishing him victory and then, overwhelmed with sorrow, entered the inner apartment followed by the womenfolk.

287.sa: प्रविष्टायां तु तारायां सह स्त्रीभिस्स्वमालयम्। नगरान्निर्ययौ क्रुद्धो महासर्प इव श्वसन्4.16.13।।
287.e: After Tara and other women returned to their abode, Vali departed from the city,  hissing  like a huge angry cobra.

287.sa: स निश्श्वस्य महातेजा वाली परमरोषणः। सर्वतश्चारयन् दृष्टिं शत्रुदर्शनकाङ्क्षया4.16.14।।
287.e: The mighty Vali, breathing heavily, looked around to find where his enemy was.

287.sa: स ददर्श ततश्श्रीमान् सुग्रीवं हेमपिङ्गलम्। सुसंवीतमवष्टब्धं दीप्यमानमिवानलम्4.16.15।।
287.e: There Vali saw Sugriva in lustrous, red gold complexion standing ready for a combat steady like glowing fire.

287.sa: स तं दृष्ट्वा महावीर्यं सुग्रीवं पर्यवस्थितम्। गाढं परिदधे वासो वाली परमरोषण:4.16.16।।
287.e: On seeing the great hero Sugriva standing firmly, the enraged Vali tied his upper cloth (around his loin) tightly.

287.sa: स वाली गाढसंवीतो मुष्टिमुद्यम्य वीर्यवान्। सुग्रीवमेवाभिमुखो ययौ योद्धुं कृतक्षणः4.16.17।।
287.e: Vali tied up his cloth tightly, raised his fist and advanced towards Sugriva, ready for the encounter.

287.sa: श्लिष्टं मुष्टिं समुद्यम्य संरब्धतरमागतः। सुग्रीवोऽपि समुद्दिश्य वालिनं हेममालिनम्4.16.18।।
287.e: Sugriva also lifted his fist firmly and advanced more impatiently towards Vali adorned with a golden necklace.

287.sa: तं वाली क्रोधताम्राक्षस्सुग्रीवं रणपण्डितम्। आपतन्तं महावेगमिदं वचनमब्रवीत्4.16.19।।
287.e: While Sugriva, expert in combat, advanced swiftly to pounce upon (his enemy), Vali whose eyes turned red in anger said:

287.sa: एष मुष्टिर्मयाबद्धो गाढस्सन्निहिताङ्गुलिः। मया वेगविमुक्तस्ते प्राणानादाय यास्यति4.16.20।।
एवमुक्तस्तु सुग्रीवः क्रुद्धो वालिनमब्रवीत्। तवैव चा हरन्प्राणान्मुष्टिः पततु मूर्धनि4.16.21।।
287.e: This infuriated Sugriva who, looking at Vali, said 'This fist of mine will draw your life out, hitting your forehead'.

287.sa: ताडितस्तेन सङ्कृद्धस्समभिक्रम्य वेगितः। अभवच्छोणितोद्गारी सोत्पीड इव पर्वतः4.16.22।।
287.e: Struck by Vali, enraged Sugriva encountered Vali more aggresively. His body drenched in blood seemed a mountain with rivulets of blood flowing.

287.sa: सुग्रीवेण तु निस्सङ्गं सालमुत्पाट्य तेजसा। गात्रेष्वभिहतो वाली वज्रेणेव महागिरिः4.16.23।।
287.e: With all his vigour, Sugriva uprooted a sala tree, pulled it out and struck Vali on the body, like a thunderbolt striking a huge mountain.

287.sa: स तु वाली प्रचलितस्सालताडनविह्वलः। गुरुभारसमाक्रान्तो नौ सार्थ इव सागरे4.16.24।।
287.e: Struck by the blows of the sala tree, Vali also lost his balance like the heavily loaded ship of a trader shaken up in the ocean.

287.sa: तौ भीमबलविक्रान्तौ सुपर्णसमवेगिनौ। प्रवृद्धौ घोरवपुषौ चन्द्रसूर्याविवाम्बरे। परस्परममित्रघ्नौ च्छिद्रान्वेषणतत्परौ4.16.25।।
287.e: Both of them endowed with terrible strength, fierce in appearance, and each seeking the weak points of the other advanced, as fast as Garuda, striking at the enemy. Their fight grew more and more fierce like the fight between Sun and Moon in the sky.

287.sa: ततोऽवर्धत वाली तु बलवीर्यसमन्वितः। सूर्यपुत्रो महावीर्यस्सुग्रीवः परिहीयते4.16.26।।
287.e: In a short while Vali, endowed with great strength, gained the upper hand and Sugriva, son of the Sungod, was losing ground .

287.sa: वालिना भग्नदर्पस्तु सुग्रीवो मन्दविक्रमः। वालिनं प्रति सामर्षो दर्शयामास लाघवम्4.16.27।।
287.e: With his strength waning and pride crushed, Sugriva, anguished, exhibited shrewdness.

287.sa: वृक्षैः स्सशाखै स्सशिखैर्वज्रकोटिनिभैर्नखैः4.16.28।। मुष्टिभिर्जानुभिः पद्भिर्बाहुभिश्च पुनः पुनः। तयोर्युद्धमभूद्घोरं वृत्रवासवयोरिव4.16.29।।
287.e: Both like Vritra and Indra fought, hitting each other again and again with trees full of branches and tops, with their hard nails akin to thunderbolts and with their fists, knees, feet, etc.

287.sa: वृक्षैः स्सशाखै स्सशिखैर्वज्रकोटिनिभैर्नखैः4.16.28।। मुष्टिभिर्जानुभिः पद्भिर्बाहुभिश्च पुनः पुनः। तयोर्युद्धमभूद्घोरं वृत्रवासवयोरिव4.16.29।।
287.e: Both like Vritra and Indra fought, hitting each other again and again with trees full of branches and tops, with their hard nails akin to thunderbolts and with their fists, knees, feet, etc.

287.sa: तौ शोणिताक्तौ युध्येतां वानरौ वनचारिणौ। मेघाविव महाशब्दै स्तर्जमानौ परस्परम्4.16.30।।
287.e: The monkeys, wanderers in the forest, both with blood stains fiercely clashed pointing at each other, roaring with dreadful sounds like two clouds.

287.sa: हीयमानमथोऽपश्यत्सुग्रीवं वानरेश्वरम्। वीक्षमाणं दिशश्चैव राघवस्स मुहुर्मुहुः4.16.31।।
287.e: Raghava perceived that the monkey king Sugriva whose strength was waning was looking again and again in all directions (seeking help).

287.sa: ततो रामो महातेजा आर्तं दृष्ट्वा हरीश्वरम्। शरं च वीक्षते वीरो वालिनो वधकारणात् 4.16.32।।
287.e: Finding the king of the monkeys in distress, the heroic, brilliant Rama looked for an  arrow in order to kill Vali.

287.sa: ततो धनुषि सन्धाय शरमाशीविषोपमम्। पुरयामास तच्चापं कालचक्रमिवान्तकः4.16.33।।
287.e: Rama then fixed an arrow which resembled a venomous snake, on to his bow looking like the very deathwheel of Yama and stretched it fully.

287.sa: तस्य ज्यातलघोषेण त्रस्ताः पत्ररथेश्वराः। प्रदुद्रुवुर्मृगाश्चैव युगान्त इव मोहिताः4.16.34।।
287.e: As if scared by the twang of the bowstring, winged and feathered birds and animals ran frightened in different directions.

287.sa: मुक्तस्तु वज्रनिर्घोष: प्रदीप्ताशनिसन्निभः। राघवेण महाबाणो वालिवक्षसि पातितः4.16.35।।
287.e: As Rama shot the mighty arrow, it went like a blazing lightning with a thunderous sound and pierced into the chest of Vali.

287.sa: ततस्तेन महातेजा वीयौटत्सिक्तः कपीश्वरः। वेगेनाभिहतो वाली निपपात महीतले4.16.36।।
287.e: Then the powerful monkey king Vali, who was proud of his might, fell down on earth, struck by the fast flying arrow.

287.sa: इन्द्रध्वज इवोद्धूतः पौर्णमास्यां महीतले। आश्वयुक्समये मासि गतश्रीको विचेतनः4.16.37।।
287.e: Vali fell lustreless on the ground. He was thrown down unconscious like the banner (hoisted in honour) of Indra on the fullmoon day of Aswayuja month.

287.sa: नरोत्तमः कालयुगान्तकोपमं शरोत्तमं काञ्चनरूप्यभुषितम्। ससर्ज दीप्तं तममित्रमर्दनं सधूममग्निं मुखतो यथा हरः4.16.38।।
287.e: The arrow of Rama, distinguished among men, adorned with silver and gold, which could crush the enemy shone like fire and smoke emitted from the mouth of Rudra at the time of dissolution (at the end of the aeon).

288.sa: ततश्शरेणाभिहतो रामेण रणकर्कशः। पपात सहसा वाली निकृत्त इव पादपः4.17.1।।
288.e: A tyrant in war, Vali struck by4.54.24 Rama's arrow, collapsed instantaneously like a tree felled down.

288.sa: स भूमौ न्यस्तसर्वाङ्गस्तप्तकाञ्चनभूषणः। अपतद्देवराजस्य मुक्तरश्मिरिव ध्वजः4.17.2।।
288.e: Adorned with shining gold ornaments,Vali fell down with all his limbs touching the ground like Indra's flag when its ropes are loosened.

288.sa: तस्मिन्निपतिते भूमौ वानराणां गणेश्वरे। नष्टचन्द्रमिव व्योम न व्यराजत भूतलम्4.17.3।।
288.e: When the lord of the monkey troops fell down, it was as though the earth lost its brightness like the sky loses its brightness devoid of the Moon.

288.sa: भूमौ निपतितस्यापि तस्य देहं महात्मनः। न श्रीर्जहाति न प्राणा न तेजो न पराक्रमः4.17.4।।
288.e: Even though the highsouled Vali's body had fallen on the ground, its  splendour, glow, life and valour had not left it.

288.sa: शक्रदत्ता वरा माला काञ्चनी वज्रभूषिता। दधार हरिमुख्यस्य प्राणांस्तेज्शियं च सा4.17.5।।
288.e: As the most beautiful golden necklace, studded with diamonds, given by Indra was there on him, the life, brightness and splendour of Vali's body remained.

288.sa: स तया मालया वीरो हेमया हरियूथपः। सन्ध्यानुगतपर्यन्तः पयोधर इवाभवत्4.17.6।।
288.e: Vali, the chief hero of the monkeys, with his golden necklace appeared like the raincloud hallowed by the glowing twilight.

288.sa: तस्य माला च देहश्च मर्मघाती च यश्शरः। त्रिधेव रचिता लक्ष्मीः पतितस्यापि शोभते4.17.7।।
288.e: Even though he had fallen down, the effulgence of his necklace on his body, and the arrow pierced into his vital parts remained.

288.sa: तदस्त्रं तस्य वीरस्य स्वर्गमार्गप्रभावनम्। रामबाणासनक्षिप्तमावहत्परमां गतिम्4.17.8।।
288.e: Rama's arrow released paved the way to heaven which was that hero's supreme destination.

288.sa: तं तदा पतितं सङ्ख्ये गतार्चिषमिवानलम्। बहुमान्य च तं वीर वीक्षमाणं शनैरिव।4.17.9।। ययातिमिव पुण्यान्ते देवलोकादिहच्युतम्। आदित्यमिव कालेन युगान्ते भुवि पातितम्।4.17.10।। महेन्द्रमिव दुर्धर्षंमुपेन्द्रमिव दुस्सहम्। महेन्द्रपुत्रं पतितं वालिनं हेममालिनम्।।4.17.11।। सिंहोरस्कं महाबाहुं दीप्तास्यं हरिलोचनम्। लक्ष्मणानुगतो रामो ददर्शोपससर्प च।।4.17.12।।
288.e: Rama followed by Lakshmana slowly approached the longarmed, lionchested, brightfaced, tawnyeyed Vali, and admiringly observed this unchallengeable son of Indra, unassailable like Indra himself. Adorned with a golden necklace, he had fallen on the ground like fire without flame, like king Yayati descended on the earth from the celestial realm on the exhaustion of his merits, or like the Sun cast down on the earth at the end of the aeon.

288.sa: तं तदा पतितं सङ्ख्ये गतार्चिषमिवानलम्। बहुमान्य च तं वीर वीक्षमाणं शनैरिव।4.17.9।। ययातिमिव पुण्यान्ते देवलोकादिहच्युतम्। आदित्यमिव कालेन युगान्ते भुवि पातितम्।4.17.10।। महेन्द्रमिव दुर्धर्षंमुपेन्द्रमिव दुस्सहम्। महेन्द्रपुत्रं पतितं वालिनं हेममालिनम्।।4.17.11।। सिंहोरस्कं महाबाहुं दीप्तास्यं हरिलोचनम्। लक्ष्मणानुगतो रामो ददर्शोपससर्प च।।4.17.12।।
288.e: Rama followed by Lakshmana slowly approached the longarmed, lionchested, brightfaced, tawnyeyed Vali, and admiringly observed this unchallengeable son of Indra, unassailable like Indra himself. Adorned with a golden necklace, he had fallen on the ground like fire without flame, like king Yayati descended on the earth from the celestial realm on the exhaustion of his merits, or like the Sun cast down on the earth at the end of the aeon.

288.sa: तं तदा पतितं सङ्ख्ये गतार्चिषमिवानलम्। बहुमान्य च तं वीर वीक्षमाणं शनैरिव।4.17.9।। ययातिमिव पुण्यान्ते देवलोकादिहच्युतम्। आदित्यमिव कालेन युगान्ते भुवि पातितम्।4.17.10।। महेन्द्रमिव दुर्धर्षंमुपेन्द्रमिव दुस्सहम्। महेन्द्रपुत्रं पतितं वालिनं हेममालिनम्।।4.17.11।। सिंहोरस्कं महाबाहुं दीप्तास्यं हरिलोचनम्। लक्ष्मणानुगतो रामो ददर्शोपससर्प च।।4.17.12।।

Adorned with a golden necklace, he had fallen on the ground like fire without flame, like king Yayati descended on the earth from the celestial realm on the exhaustion of his merits, or like the Sun cast down on the earth at the end of the aeon.

288.sa: तं तदा पतितं सङ्ख्ये गतार्चिषमिवानलम्। बहुमान्य च तं वीर वीक्षमाणं शनैरिव।4.17.9।। ययातिमिव पुण्यान्ते देवलोकादिहच्युतम्। आदित्यमिव कालेन युगान्ते भुवि पातितम्।4.17.10।। महेन्द्रमिव दुर्धर्षंमुपेन्द्रमिव दुस्सहम्। महेन्द्रपुत्रं पतितं वालिनं हेममालिनम्।।4.17.11।। सिंहोरस्कं महाबाहुं दीप्तास्यं हरिलोचनम्। लक्ष्मणानुगतो रामो ददर्शोपससर्प च।।4.17.12।।
288.e: Rama followed by Lakshmana slowly approached the longarmed, lionchested, brightfaced, tawnyeyed Vali, and admiringly observed this unchallengeable son of Indra, unassailable like Indra himself. Adorned with a golden necklace, he had fallen on the ground like fire without flame, like king Yayati descended on the earth from the celestial realm on the exhaustion of his merits, or like the Sun cast down on the earth at the end of the aeon.

288.sa: तं दृष्ट्वा राघवं वाली लक्ष्मणं च महाबलम्। अब्रवीत्प्रश्रितं वाक्यं परुषं धर्मसंहितम्4.17.13।। त्वं नराधिपतेः पुत्रः प्रथितः प्रियदर्शनः कुलीनस्सत्त्वसम्पन्न स्तेजस्वी चरितव्रतः।।4.17.14।। पराङ्मुखवधं कृत्वा कोऽत्र प्राप्तस्त्वया गुणः। यदहं युद्धसंरब्धश्शरेणोरसि ताडित:4.17.15।।
288.e: On seeing powerful Rama and Lakshmana approaching,Vali spoke with pride and rigteousness to Rama, 'You are a prince, born of a noble family, son of a renowned king. You are famous, brilliant, handsome and follower of good practices.Having hit me when I was engaged otherwise in an encounter what merit have you gained?'

288.sa: तं दृष्ट्वा राघवं वाली लक्ष्मणं च महाबलम्। अब्रवीत्प्रश्रितं वाक्यं परुषं धर्मसंहितम्4.17.13।। त्वं नराधिपतेः पुत्रः प्रथितः प्रियदर्शनः कुलीनस्सत्त्वसम्पन्न स्तेजस्वी चरितव्रतः।।4.17.14।। पराङ्मुखवधं कृत्वा कोऽत्र प्राप्तस्त्वया गुणः। यदहं युद्धसंरब्धश्शरेणोरसि ताडित:4.17.15।।
288.e: On seeing powerful Rama and Lakshmana approaching,Vali spoke with pride and rigteousness to Rama, 'You are a prince, born of a noble family, son of a renowned king. You are famous, brilliant, handsome and follower of good practices.Having hit me when I was engaged otherwise in an encounter what merit have you gained?'

288.sa: तं दृष्ट्वा राघवं वाली लक्ष्मणं च महाबलम्। अब्रवीत्प्रश्रितं वाक्यं परुषं धर्मसंहितम्4.17.13।। त्वं नराधिपतेः पुत्रः प्रथितः प्रियदर्शनः कुलीनस्सत्त्वसम्पन्न स्तेजस्वी चरितव्रतः।।4.17.14।। पराङ्मुखवधं कृत्वा कोऽत्र प्राप्तस्त्वया गुणः। यदहं युद्धसंरब्धश्शरेणोरसि ताडित:4.17.15।।
288.e: On seeing powerful Rama and Lakshmana approaching,Vali spoke with pride and rigteousness to Rama, 'You are a prince, born of a noble family, son of a renowned king. You are famous, brilliant, handsome and follower of good practices.Having hit me when I was engaged otherwise in an encounter what merit have you gained?'

288.sa: रामः करुणवेदी च प्रजानां च हिते रतः। सानुक्रोशो जितोत्साहस्समयज्ञो दृढव्रतः।।4.17.16।। इति ते सर्वभूतानि कथयन्ति यशो भुवि।।4.17.17।।
रामः करुणवेदी च प्रजानां च हिते रतः। सानुक्रोशो जितोत्साहस्समयज्ञो दृढव्रतः।।4.17.16।। इति ते सर्वभूतानि कथयन्ति यशो भुवि।।4.17.17।।
दमश्शमः क्षमा धर्मो धृतिस्सत्यं पराक्रमः। पार्थिवानां गुणा राजन्दण्डश्चाप्यपराधिषु4.17.18।।
288.e: 'O king selfcontrol (of organs of action and sense organs), righteousness, steadfastness, truthfulness, valiance and capacity to punish the offenders are virtues  of a king.

288.sa: तान्गुणान्सम्प्रधार्याहमग्र्यं चाभिजनं तव। तारया प्रतिषिद्धोऽपि सुग्रीवेण समागतः4.17.19।।
288.e: 'Believing that you are a repository of all these virtues are in you, and respecting your noble lineage I engaged in a duel with Sugriva even though I was forewarned (by Tara).

288.sa: न मामन्येन सम्रब्धं प्रमत्तं योद्धु मर्हसि। इति मे बुद्धिरुत्पन्ना बभूवादर्शने तव4.17.20।।
न त्वां विनिहतात्मानं धर्मध्वजमधार्मिकम्। जाने पापसमाचारं तृणैः कूपमिवावृतम्4.17.21।।
288.e: 'I did not know that you have killed your soul (by acting against your conscience), that you are sinful in conduct and unrighteous under the show of virtues like a well, its mouth covered with grass.

288.sa: सतां वेषधरं पापं प्रच्छन्नमिव पावकम्। नाहं त्वामभिजानामि धर्मच्छद्माभिसंवृतम्4.17.22।।
288.e: 'You are a sinful man covered with the mask of piety thus resembling a hidden fire. I failed to recognise that righteousness is a mere pretext for you.

288.sa: विषये वा पुरे वा ते यदा पापं करोम्यहम्। न च त्वामवजाने च कस्मात्त्वं हंस्यकिल्बिषम्4.17.23।। फलमूलाशनं नित्यं वानरं वनगोचरम्। मामिहाप्रतियुध्यन्तमन्येन च समागतम्4.17.24।।
288.e: 'I did no harm to your affairs or to your city. I did not insult you. Why did you choose to kill me, a monkey roaming in the forest and living on fruits and roots? I was not fighting you. Why did you come and strike a person like me?

288.sa: विषये वा पुरे वा ते यदा पापं करोम्यहम्। न च त्वामवजाने च कस्मात्त्वं हंस्यकिल्बिषम्4.17.23।। फलमूलाशनं नित्यं वानरं वनगोचरम्। मामिहाप्रतियुध्यन्तमन्येन च समागतम्4.17.24।।
288.e: 'I did no harm to your affairs or to your city. I did not insult you. Why did you choose to kill me, a monkey roaming in the forest and living on fruits and roots? I was not fighting you. Why did you come and strike a person like me?

288.sa: त्वं नराधिपतेः पुत्रः प्रतीतः प्रियदर्शनः। लिङ्गमप्यस्ति ते राजनन्दृश्यते धर्मसंहितम्4.17.25।।
288.e: 'O prince, you are son to a king, handsome and famous. Even signs of righteousness are discernible in you.

288.sa: कः क्षत्रियकुले जात्शृतवान्नष्टसंशयः। धर्मलिङ्गप्रतिच्छन्न क्रूरं कर्म समाचरेत्4.17.26।।
288.e: 'Who, born in a kshatriya family, versed in the Vedas and free from doubt will commit such a cruel act under the guise of righteousness?

288.sa: राम राजकुले जातो धर्मवानिति विश्रुतः।।4.17.27।। अभव्यो भव्यरूपेण किमर्थं परिधावसि।
288.e: 'You are born in a royal family. You are wellknown. You are proficient in dharma. Yet you are unworthy  of your race and robe.

288.sa: साम दानं क्षमा धर्मस्सत्यं धृतिपराक्रमौ। पार्थिवानां गुणा राजन् दण्डश्चाप्यपराधिषु4.17.28।।
288.e: 'Conciliation, generosity, forbearance, righteousness, truthfulness, steadfastness in valour and punishing offenders are the hallmarks of rulers.

288.sa: वयं वनचरा राम मृगा मूलफलाशना:। एषा प्रकृतिरस्माकं पुरुषस्त्वं नरेश्वरः4.17.29।।
288.e: 'O Rama we are mere animals wandering in the forest and living on roots and fruits. This is our nature. (But) you are a lord of men.

288.sa: भूमिर्हिरण्यं रूप्यं च विग्रहे कारणानि च। अत्र कस्ते वने लोभो मदीयेषु फलेषु वा4.17.30।।
288.e: 'We fight for land or gold or silver. What did you fight me for, for what I have or for the fruits of the forest?

288.sa: नयश्च विनयश्चोभौ निग्रहानुग्रहावपि4.17.31।। राजवृत्तिरसङ्कीर्णा न नृपाः कामवृत्तयः।
288.e: 'Submissiveness and modesty are the attributes of good rulers and should not be mixed up with benevolence and selfrestraint. Kings ought not to act (as they like) impulsively.

288.sa: त्वं तु कामप्रधानश्च कोपनश्चानवस्थितः4.17.32।। राजवृत्तेश्च सङ्कीणश्शरासनपरायणः।
288.e: 'Fulfilling your own desire is important for you. You are wrathful and unstable with royal course of conduct. Your business is with your bow and arrows.

288.sa: न तेऽस्त्यपचितिर्धर्मे नार्थे बुद्धिरवस्थिता4.17.33।। इन्द्रियैः कामवृत्तस्सन्कृष्यसे मनुजेश्वर।
288.e: 'O lord of men you have no faith in righteousness, no steadfastness in the acquisition of wealth. You have no control over the senses. You are overcome by delusion.

288.sa: हत्वा बाणेन काकुत्स्थ मामिहानपराधिनम्4.17.34।। किं वक्ष्यसि सतां मध्ये कर्म कृत्वा जुगुप्सितम्।
288.e: 'O scion of the Kakutsthas Having killed me here with your arrow even though I have done you no harm, you have perpetrated an abominable act. How will you defend yourself in the midst of holy men after commiting such a sinful act?

288.sa: राजहा ब्रह्महा गोघ्नश्चोरः प्राणिवधे रतः4.17.35।। नास्तिकः परिवेत्ता च सर्वे निरयगामिनः।
288.e: 'One who kills a king, a brahmin or a cow, a thief or one who delights in destruction of life an atheist or one who marries before his elder  they all go to hell.

288.sa: सूचकश्च कदर्यश्च मित्रघ्नो गुरुतल्पगः4.17.36।। लोकं पापात्मनामेते गच्छन्ते नात्र संशयः।
अधार्यं चर्म मे सद्भी रोमाण्यस्थि च वर्जितम्। अभक्ष्याणि च मांसानि त्वद्विधैर्धर्मचारिभिः4.17.37।।
288.e: 'My skin is not fit to be worn by the virtuous, my hair and bones are also prohibited from any use. My flesh is also not at all fit to be eaten by righteous people like you

288.sa: पञ्च पञ्च नखा भक्ष्या ब्रह्मक्षत्रेण राघव4.17.38।। शल्यक श्श्वाविधो गोधा शशः कूर्मश्च पञ्चमः।
288.e: 'O Rama brahmins and kshatriyas are permitted to eat only the five nailed animals the porcupine, the hedgehog, the alligator, the rabbit and the tortoise.

288.sa: चर्म चास्थि च मे राजन् नस्पृशन्ति मनीषिणः4.17.39।। अभक्ष्याणि च मांसानि सोऽहं पञ्चनखो हतः।
288.e: 'O king the learned do not even touch my skin or bone. They do not eat my flesh. While it is so, you have unnecessarily killed me, a fivenailed animal.

288.sa: तारया वाक्यमुक्तोऽहं सत्यं सर्वज्ञया हितम्4.17.40।। तदतिक्रम्य मोहेन कालस्य वशमागतः।
288.e: 'Tara knew everything. Her words were correct. They were meant for my wellbeing. However, due to my ignorance (or arrogance), I did not heed her words and fell under the sway of the lord of death

288.sa: त्वया नाथेन काकुत्स्थ न सनाथा वसुन्धरा। प्रमदा शीलसम्पन्ना धूर्तेन पतिना यथा4.17.41।।
288.e: 'O Kakutstha just as a wife endowed with good character cannot be protected by a wicked husband, you cannot be a protector of this earth.

288.sa: शठो नैकृतिकः क्षुद्रो मिथ्याप्रश्रितमानसः। कथं दशरथेन त्वं जातः पापो महात्मना4.17.42।।
288.e: 'You are treacherous, dishonest, mean, guised with false humility and a sinner to the core. How were you born to that highsouled Dasaratha?

288.sa: छिन्नचारित्रकक्ष्येण सतां धर्मातिवर्तिना। त्यक्तधर्माङ्कुशेनाहं निहतो रामहस्तिना4.17.43।।
288.e: 'Breaking through the chains of good character, trespassing the moral code of conduct of the sages, discharging the sharp arrow of righteousness, the elephantine (arrogant) Rama killed me.

288.sa: अशुभं चाप्ययुक्तं च सतां चैव विगर्हितम्। वक्ष्यसे चेदृशं कृत्वा सद्भिस्सह समागतः4.17.44।।
288.e: 'You have committed an inauspicious, improper act, despised by the virtuous. What will you speak when you are questioned by noble men for committing such an act?

288.sa: उदासीनेषु योऽस्मासु विक्रमऽस्ते प्रकाशितः। अपकारिषु ते राजन्नहि पश्यामि विक्रमम्4.17.45।।
288.e: 'O king you have exhibited your valour against one who has done you no harm. Why have you not shown such valour on those who have offended you?

288.sa: दृश्यमानस्तु युद्ध्येथा मया यदि नृपात्मज। अद्य वैवस्वतं देवं पश्येस्त्वं निहतो मया4.17.46।।
288.e: 'O prince had  you fought me face to face you would have seen Vaivasvata, the lord of death today (you would have been killed by me).

288.sa: त्वयाऽदृश्येन तु रणे निहतोऽहं दुरासदः। प्रसुप्तः पन्नगेनेव नरः पानवशं गतः4.17.47।।
288.e: bitten to death by a snake while fast asleep.

288.sa: मामेव यदि पूर्वं त्वमेतदर्थमचोदयः4.17.48।। मैथिलीमहमेकाह्ना तव चानीतवान्भवेत्। सुग्रीवप्रियकामेन यदहं निहतस्त्वया। कण्ठे बद्ध्वा प्रदद्यां ते निहतं रावणं रणे4.17.49।।
288.e: 'Had you sought my help earlier(before you met Sugriva), I would have restored Sita to you within a single day. I have been killed by you to oblige Sugriva. I would have handed over Ravana by the neck after killing him in the battle.

288.sa: मामेव यदि पूर्वं त्वमेतदर्थमचोदयः4.17.48।। मैथिलीमहमेकाह्ना तव चानीतवान्भवेत्। सुग्रीवप्रियकामेन यदहं निहतस्त्वया। कण्ठे बद्ध्वा प्रदद्यां ते निहतं रावणं रणे4.17.49।।
288.e: 'Had you sought my help earlier(before you met Sugriva), I would have restored Sita to you within a single day. I have been killed by you to oblige Sugriva. I would have handed over Ravana by the neck after killing him in the battle.

288.sa: न्यस्तां सागरतोये वा पाताले वापि मैथिलीम्। आनयेयं तवादेशाच्छ्वेतामश्वतरीमिव4.17.50।।
288.e: 'Even if she were hidden in the waters of the ocean or in the underworld, I would have brought her by your order like Sweta to Aswatari or Hayagriva. (Hayagriva, an incarnation of Visnu brought Vedas stolen by demons, Madhu and Kaitabha from Patala or the netherworld)

288.sa: युक्तं यत्प्राप्नुयाद्राज्यं सुग्रीवस्स्वर्गते मयि। अयुक्तं यदधर्मेण त्वयाऽहं निहतो रणे4.17.51।।
288.e: 'Sugriva inheriting the kingdom after my departure to heaven is proper. But your killing me this way in the combat by unjustifiable means is not.

288.sa: काममेवं विधो लोकः कालेन विनियुज्यते। क्षमं चेद्भवता प्राप्तमुत्तरं साधु चिन्त्यताम्4.17.52।।
288.e: 'Indeed, in the world people meet with death when the time comes. Hiding yourself (from me) you have achieved it. Is it proper for you? You may think over and give your reply.'

289.sa: इत्युक्तः प्रश्रितं वाक्यं धर्मार्थसहितं हितम्। परुषं वालिना रामो निहतेन विचेतसा4.18.1।।
289.e: To these harsh words though seemingly wellmeaning, courteous and righteous, Vali who had been mortally wounded and confused in mind, Rama replied:

289.sa: तं निष्प्रभमिवादित्यं मुक्ततोयमिवाम्बुदम्। उक्तवाक्यं हरिश्रेष्ठमुपशान्तमिवानलम्4.18.2।। धर्मार्थगुणसम्पन्नं हरीश्वरमनुत्तमम्। अधिक्षिप्तस्तदा रामः पश्चाद्वालिनमब्रवीत्4.18.3।।
289.e: To righteous Vali,the best of the monkeys, the lord of the monkeys, who looked like the Sun shorn of his brilliance or a raindrained cloud or a fire that had been extinguished. Rama, under the scanner, said in reply:

289.sa: तं निष्प्रभमिवादित्यं मुक्ततोयमिवाम्बुदम्। उक्तवाक्यं हरिश्रेष्ठमुपशान्तमिवानलम्4.18.2।। धर्मार्थगुणसम्पन्नं हरीश्वरमनुत्तमम्। अधिक्षिप्तस्तदा रामः पश्चाद्वालिनमब्रवीत्4.18.3।।
289.e: To righteous Vali,the best of the monkeys, the lord of the monkeys, who looked like the Sun shorn of his brilliance or a raindrained cloud or a fire that had been extinguished. Rama, under the scanner, said in reply:

289.sa: धर्ममर्थं च कामं च समयं चापि लौकिकम्। अविज्ञाय कथं बाल्यान्मामिहाद्य विगर्हसे4.18.4।।
289.e: 'Without correct knowledge of dharma, artha, kama and worldly ways, how do you reproach me bitterly now in total ignorance?

289.sa: अपृष्ट्वा बुद्धिसम्पन्नान्वृद्धानाचार्यसम्मतान्। सौम्य वानरचापल्यात्किं मावक्तुमिहेच्छसि4.18.5।।
289.e: 'O gentle Vali why do you speak with monkeyish frivolousness, without consulting the elders and teachers endowed with intelligence?

289.sa: इक्ष्वाकूणामियं भूमिस्सशैलवनकानना। मृगपक्षिमनुष्याणां निग्रहप्रग्रहावपि4.18.6।।
289.e: 'This earth including mountains, groves and forests, animals, birds and humans belongs to the Ikshvaku kings.The right of purnishment and reward also vests with them.

289.sa: तां पालयति धर्मात्मा भरतस्सत्यवागृजुः। धर्मकामार्थतत्त्वज्ञो निग्रहानुग्रहे रतः4.18.7।।
289.e: 'Bharata, righteous, truthful, upright, knower of dharma, artha and kama and dispenser of punishment and rewards, rules this earth.

289.sa: नयश्च विनयश्चोभौ यस्मिन्सत्यं च सुस्थितम्। विक्रमश्च यथा दृष्टस्स राजा देशकालवित्4.18.8।।
289.e: 'Bharata in whom justice and discipline, truth and courage along with the knowledge of time and place for action are firmly rooted is king (of this earth).

289.sa: तस्य धर्मकृतादेशा वयमन्ये च पार्थिवाः। चरामो वसुधां कृत्स्नां धर्मसन्तानमिच्छवः4.18.9।।
289.e: 'Following his command, in confirmity with dharma we and the other kings also move all over the  entire world desirous of promoting dharma.

289.sa: तस्मिन्नृपतिशार्दूले भरते धर्मवत्सले। पालयत्यखिलां भूमिं कश्चरेद्धर्मनिग्रहम्4.18.10।।
289.e: 'Who can stray from the path of dharma when the whole world is ruled by Bharata, a tiger among kings, and a lover of dharma?

289.sa: ते वयं धर्मविभ्रष्टं स्वधर्मे परमे स्थिताः। भरताज्ञां पुरस्कृत्य निगृह्णीमो यथाविधि4.18.11।।
289.e: 'By the command of Bharata ,all of us are devoted to our duty of upholding dharma and virtue and duly punish those who deviate from the path of dharma.

289.sa: त्वं तु संक्लिष्टधर्मा च कर्मणा च विगर्हितः। कामतन्त्रप्रधानश्च न स्थितो राजवर्त्मनि4.18.12।।
289.e: 'You have violated dharma. You stand condemned for your actions. Passion is your priority. You have strayed from the right path of kings.

289.sa: ज्येष्ठो भ्राता पिता चैव यश्च विद्यां प्रयच्छति। त्रयस्ते पितरो ज्ञेया धर्म्ये च पथि वर्तिनः4.18.13।।
यवीयानात्मनः पुत्रशशिष्यश्चापि गुणोदितः। पुत्रवत्ते त्रयश्चिन्त्या धर्मश्चेदत्रकारणम्4.18.14।।
सूक्ष्मः परमदुरजेयस्सतां धर्मः प्लवङ्गम। हृदिस्थस्सर्वभूतानामात्मा वेद शुभाशुभम्4.18.15।।
289.e: 'O monkey dharma is very subtle. It is extremely difficult to understand. Installed in the hearts of all living beings the self knows good and evil (soul is the witness of good and evil).

289.sa: चपलश्चपलैस्सार्धं वानरैरकृतात्मभिः। जात्यन्ध इव जात्यन्धैर्मन्त्रयन् प्रेक्षसे नु किम्4.18.16।।
289.e: 'You are fickle by nature. Your consultants are frivolous, pettyminded monkeys. It is like one born blind suppporting another blind by birth. What do you know (about dharma)?

289.sa: अहं तु व्यक्ततामस्य वचनस्य ब्रवीमि ते। न हि मां केवलं रोषात्त्वं विगर्हितुमर्हसि4.18.17।।
289.e: 'I shall explain to you clearly (the reason for striking you down). It is not proper for you to despise me with mere anger and malice.

289.sa: तदेतत्कारणं पश्य यदर्थं त्वं मया हतः। भ्रातुर्वर्तसि भार्यायां त्यक्त्वा धर्मं सनातनम्4.18.18।।
289.e: 'Now know the reason why I struck you down. Having abandoned the eternal  law, you are living with your younger brother's wife.

289.sa: अस्य त्वं धरमाणस्य सुग्रीवस्य महात्मनः। रुमायां वर्तसे कामात्स्नुषायां पापकर्मकृत्4.18.19।।
289.e: 'You are a sinner, since you live with Ruma, who is your virtual daughterinlaw, when the great self Sugriva is alive. (A younger brother is like a son and his wife, a daughterinlaw).

289.sa: तद्व्यतीतस्य ते धर्मात्कामवृत्तस्य वानर। भ्रातृभार्यावमर्शेऽस्मिन्दण्डोऽयं प्रतिपादितः4.18.20।।
289.e: 'O monkey since you have violated morality by sinning against your brother's wife this punishment is justified.

289.sa: न हि धर्मविरुद्धस्य लोकवृत्तादपेयुषः। दण्डादन्यत्र पश्यामि निग्रहं हरियूथप4.18.21।
289.e: 'O lord of monkeys I do not see any other way of controlling a person excepting punishing the one who has acted against dharma and swerved from the accepted code of conduct.

289.sa: न हि ते मर्षये पापं क्षत्रियोऽहं कुलोद्भवः। औरसीं भगिनीं वापि भार्यां वाप्यनुजस्य यः4.18.22।। प्रचरेत नरः कामात्तस्य दण्डो वधः स्मृतः।
289.e: 'I am a kshatriya born of a good family. I will not pardon you for your sin. Whosoever transgresses dharma against his own daughter, sister or brother's wife out of lust should be killed according to smriti.

289.sa: भरतस्तु महीपालो वयं त्वादेशवर्तिनः4.18.23।। त्वं तु धर्मादतिक्रान्तः कथं शक्यं उपेक्षितुम्।
289.e: 'Bharata is a king and we follow his command. How can you, who have strayed from dharma, go unpunished?

289.sa: गुरूर्धर्मव्यतिक्रान्तं प्राज्ञो धर्मेण पालयन्4.18.24।। भरतः कामवृत्तानां निग्रहे पर्यवस्थितः।
289.e: 'Wise Bharata being a respectable king rules by dharma. By the command of Bharata, we are bent upon punishing those who have strayed from dharma  by being addicted to sensual pleasures.

289.sa: वयं तु भरतादेश विधिं कृत्वा हरीश्वर। त्वद्विधान्भिन्नमर्यादान्नियन्तुपर्यवस्थिताः4.18.25।।
289.e: 'O Vali we have to follow Bharata's command and are bent upon punishing those wicked people who deviate from the bounds of dharma.

289.sa: सुग्रीवेण च मे सख्यं लक्ष्मणेन यथा तथा। दारराज्यनिमित्तं च निःश्रेयसि रत स्स मे4.18.26।। प्रतिज्ञा च मया दत्ता तदा वानरसन्निधौ। प्रतिज्ञा च कथं शक्या मद्विधेनानवेक्षितुम्4.18.27।।
289.e: 'My friendship with Sugriva is as strong as that with Lakshmana. Its motive is the recovery of his wife and sovereignty. I have  promised this to him in the presence of monkeys. How can a pledge remain unhonoured by a person like me? How is it possible?

289.sa: सुग्रीवेण च मे सख्यं लक्ष्मणेन यथा तथा। दारराज्यनिमित्तं च निःश्रेयसि रत स्स मे4.18.26।। प्रतिज्ञा च मया दत्ता तदा वानरसन्निधौ। प्रतिज्ञा च कथं शक्या मद्विधेनानवेक्षितुम्4.18.27।।
289.e: 'My friendship with Sugriva is as strong as that with Lakshmana. Its motive is the recovery of his wife and sovereignty. I have  promised this to him in the presence of monkeys. How can a pledge remain unhonoured by a person like me? How is it possible?

289.sa: तदेभिः कारणैस्सर्वैर्महद्भिर्धर्मसंहितैः4.18.28।। शासनं तप यद्युक्तं तद्भवाननुमन्यताम्।
289.e: 'Knowing all these reasons(many violations of dharma), it is proper for you as a king to approve of the punishment accorded to you in consonance with dharma.

289.sa: सर्वथा धर्म इत्येव द्रष्टव्यस्तव निग्रहः4.18.29।। वयस्यस्योपकर्तव्यं धर्ममेवानुपश्यतः।
289.e: 'Punishment given to you should be viewed as a right course of action in all respects. This is the duty of a trustworthy friend who follows dharma.

289.sa: शक्यं त्वयाऽपि तत्कार्यं धर्ममेवानुपश्यता4.18.30।। श्रूयते मनुना गीतौ श्लोकौ चारित्रवत्सलौ। गृहीतौ धर्मकुशलैस्तत्तथा चरितं हरे4.18.31।।
289.e: 'You should also have acted in that manner considering dharma. Now listen to what Manu said, in two verses that hold good traditions dear which are accepted by men wellversed in dharma. O monkey the action taken by me is in conformity with this.

289.sa: शक्यं त्वयाऽपि तत्कार्यं धर्ममेवानुपश्यता4.18.30।। श्रूयते मनुना गीतौ श्लोकौ चारित्रवत्सलौ। गृहीतौ धर्मकुशलैस्तत्तथा चरितं हरे4.18.31।।
289.e: 'You should also have acted in that manner considering dharma. Now listen to what Manu said, in two verses that hold good traditions dear which are accepted by men wellversed in dharma. O monkey the action taken by me is in conformity with this.

289.sa: राजभिर्धृतदण्डास्तु कृत्वा पापानि मानवाः। निर्मलास्स्वर्गमायान्ति सन्तस्सुकृतिनो यथा4.18.32।।
289.e: 'Men who have perpetrated sins should be subjected to punishment by kings so that they become stainless and attain heaven like pious men who have performed good deeds.

289.sa: शासनाद्वाऽपिमोक्षाद्वा स्तेनः स्तेयाद्विमुच्यते। राजात्वशासन्पापस्य तदवाप्नोति किल्बिषम्4.18.33।।
आर्येण मम मान्धात्रा व्यसनं घोरमीप्सितम्। श्रमणेन कृते पापे यथा पापं कृतं त्वया4.18.34।।
289.e: 'In the past a similar sin was perpetrated by Sramana, a revered soul (mendicant) and Mandhata, a noble king of my race inflicted terrible punishment on him.

289.sa: अन्यैरपि कृतं पापं प्रमत्तैर्वसुधाधिपैः। प्रायश्चित्तं च कुर्वन्ति तेन तच्छाम्यते रजः4.18.35।।
289.e: 'Vicious deeds have been committed by others when the kings were not watchful. Kings punish such sinners when they are vigilant. Otherwise they have to atone for their negligence.

289.sa: तदलं परितापेन धर्मतः परिकल्पितः। वधो वानरशार्दूल न वयं स्ववशे स्थिता:।।4.18.36।।
289.e: 'O tiger among monkeys do not regret. Your death has the sanction of dharma. We are under the control of sastras. We are committed to them. We do not have the freedom to act independently.

289.sa: शृणु चाप्यपरं भूयः कारणं हरिपुङ्गव। यच्छ्रुत्वा हेतुमद्वीर न मन्युं कर्तुमर्हसि4.18.37।।
289.e: 'O hero O best of monkeys listen to me. I will give you one more reason. On hearing it, I hope you would not be angry with me.

289.sa: न मे तत्र मनस्तापो न मन्युर्हरिपुङ्गव। वागुराभिश्च पाशैश्च कूटैश्च विविधैर्नराः4.18.38।। प्रतिच्छन्नाश्च दृश्याश्च गृह्णन्ति सुबहून्मृगान्।
289.e: 'O best of monkeys I have no mental agony nor do I regret in this case. Hidden from view or out in the open, people catch animals by means of snares or ropes or through other tricks.

289.sa: प्रधावितान्वा वित्रस्तान्विस्रब्धांश्चापि निष्ठितान्4.18.39।। प्रमत्तानप्रमत्तान्वा नरा मांसार्थिनो भृशम्। विध्यन्ति विमुखांश्चापि न च दोषोऽत्र विद्यते4.18.40।।
289.e: 'People seeking animal flesh for food kill animals alarmed or unalarmed, animals that run away or animals that stand still. They kill animals whether they are alert or not and no blemish is attached.

289.sa: प्रधावितान्वा वित्रस्तान्विस्रब्धांश्चापि निष्ठितान्4.18.39।। प्रमत्तानप्रमत्तान्वा नरा मांसार्थिनो भृशम्। विध्यन्ति विमुखांश्चापि न च दोषोऽत्र विद्यते4.18.40।।
289.e: 'People seeking animal flesh for food kill animals alarmed or unalarmed, animals that run away or animals that stand still. They kill animals whether they are alert or not and no blemish is attached.

289.sa: यान्ति राजर्षयश्चात्र मृगयां धर्मकोविदाः। तस्मात्त्वं निहतो युद्धे मया बाणेन वानर4.18.41।। अयुध्यन्प्रतियुध्यन्वा यस्माच्छाखामृगो ह्यसि।
289.e: 'O monkey even royal saints wellversed in dharma go for hunting. I struck you down with an arrow whether you were fighting with Sugriva or not, since you are a monkey. (You can be hit whether you are fighting face to face or not).

289.sa: दुर्लभस्य च धर्मस्य जीवितस्य शुभस्य च4.18.42।। राजानो वानरश्रेष्ठ प्रदातारो न संशयः।
289.e: 'O best of monkeys kings are donors of dharma, life and auspiciousness to people which is difficult to acquire. There is no doubt about it.

289.sa: तान्न हिंस्यान्न चाक्रोशेन्नाक्षिपेन्नाप्रियं वदेत्4.18.43।। देवा मानुषरूपेण चरन्त्येते महीतले।
289.e: 'One should not insult kings, nor shout at them, nor disregard them nor speak unpleasant words to them. They are gods in human form moving on this earth.

289.sa: त्वं तु धर्ममविज्ञाय केवलं रोषमास्थितः4.18.44।। प्रदूषयसि मां धर्मे पितृपैतामहे स्थितम्।
289.e: 'Seized with improper anger, you are reproaching one who is devoted to dharma, without knowing that I follow the code of conduct that has been passed on by my fathers and forefathers.'

289.sa: एवमुक्तस्तु रामेण वाली प्रव्यथितो भृशम्4.18.45।। न दोषं राघवे दध्यौ धर्मेऽधिगतनिश्चयः।
289.e: Vali was very much pained to hear Rama. He became free from confusion regarding dharma and no longer found fault with Rama.

289.sa: प्रत्युवाच ततो रामं प्राञ्जलिर्वानरेश्वरः।।4.18.46।। यत्त्वमात्थ नरश्रेष्ठ तदेवं नात्र संशयः।
289.e: Thereafter Vali offered obeisance with folded palms to Rama, saying, 'O best among men whatever you have spoken is undoubtedly true.'

289.sa: प्रतिवक्तुं प्रकृष्टे हि नापकृष्टस्तु शक्नुयात्4.18.47।। यदयुक्तं मया पूर्वं प्रमादाद्वाक्यमप्रियम्। तत्रापि खलु मे दोषं कर्तुं नार्हसि राघव।
तदयुक्तं मया पूर्वं प्रमादादुक्तमप्रियम् । तत्रापि खलु मे दोषं कर्तुं नार्हसि राघव ।। 4.18.48 ।।
289.e: In Progress

289.sa: त्वं हि दृष्टार्थतत्त्वज्ञ: प्रजानां च हिते रतः। कार्यकारणसिद्धौ च प्रसन्ना बुद्धिरव्यया4.18.49।।
289.e: 'You are a wise man given to truth and righteousness.You remain devoted to people's wellbeing. As you know for certain about cause and effect your intellect is sound and words pleasant.

289.sa: मामप्यगतधर्माणं व्यतिक्रान्तपुरस्कृतम्। धर्मसंहितया वाचा धर्मज्ञ परिपालय4.18.50।।
289.e: 'O knower of dharma, I did not follow dharma in the past. I have trangressed the bounds of dharma. Say, you have pardoned me, protect me in a righteous manner.

289.sa: न त्वात्मानमहं शोचे न तारां न च बान्धवान्। यथा पुत्रं गुणज्येष्ठमङ्गदं कनकाङ्गदम् 4.18.51।।
289.e: 'I neither grieve for myself nor for Tara nor for my kinsmen. But I do for my son Angada adorned with golden armlets. He is embellished with all virtues.

289.sa: स ममादर्शनाद्दीनो बाल्यात्प्रभृति लालितः। तटाक इव पीताम्बुरुपशोषं गमिष्यति4.18.52।।
289.e: 'I loved him very much from his childhood. He will grow depressed in my absence. He will become like a pond whose waters have been dried up.

289.sa: बालश्चाकृतबुद्धिश्च एकपुत्रश्च मे प्रियः। तारेयो राम भवता रक्षणीयो महाबलः4.18.53।।
289.e: 'O Rama he is my only son through Tara and dear to me. He is young,innocent but strong.He  deserves to be protected by you.

289.sa: सुग्रीवे चाङ्गदे चैव विधत्स्व मतिमुत्तमाम्। त्वं हि शास्ता च गोप्ता च कार्याकार्यविधौ स्थितः4.18.54।।
289.e: 'Shower equal affection from your heart on Sugriva and Angada. You are their protector and punisher also. You know what should and should not be done.

289.sa: या ते नरपते वृत्तिर्भरते लक्ष्मणे च या। सुग्रीवे चाङ्गदे राजंस्तां त्वमाधातुमिहासि4.18.55।।
289.e: 'O lord of men may you have the same kind of affection for Sugriva and Angada as you have for Bharata and Lakshmana.

289.sa: मद्दोषकृतदोषां तां यथा तारां तपस्विनीम्। सुग्रीवो नावमन्येत तथाऽवस्थातुमर्हसि4.18.56।।
289.e: 'I hope Tara will not be made to suffer because of my offence. Make Sugriva not to run wretched Tara down.

289.sa: त्वया ह्यनुगृहीतेन राज्यं शक्यमुपासितुम्4.18.57।। त्वद्वशे वर्तमानेन तव चित्तानुवर्तिना। शक्यं दिवं चार्जयितुं वसुधां चापि शासितुम्4.18.58।।
289.e: 'It is possible for a person favoured by you to rule the kingdom.It is possible for one who is under your control and acts according to your will to rule the entire world and earn heaven.

289.sa: त्वया ह्यनुगृहीतेन राज्यं शक्यमुपासितुम्4.18.57।। त्वद्वशे वर्तमानेन तव चित्तानुवर्तिना। शक्यं दिवं चार्जयितुं वसुधां चापि शासितुम्4.18.58।।
289.e: 'It is possible for a person favoured by you to rule the kingdom.It is possible for one who is under your control and acts according to your will to rule the entire world and earn heaven.

289.sa: त्वत्तोऽहं वधमाकाङ्क्षन्वार्यमाणोऽपि तारया। सुग्रीवेण सह भ्रात्रा द्वन्द्वयुद्धमुपागतः4.18.59।। इत्युक्त्वा सन्नतो रामं विरराम हरीश्वरः।
289.e: 'Even though I was prevented by Tara, I came for a duel with Sugriva since I wished to die in your hands.' Having spoken thus to Rama, Vali fell silent.

289.sa: स तमाश्वासयद्रामो वालिनं व्यक्तदर्शनम्4.18.60।। सामसम्पन्नया वाचा धर्मतत्त्वार्थयुक्तया।
289.e: Now Vali was able to see clearly. Rama consoled him with words of peace and tranquillity, truth and righteousness.

289.sa: न सन्तापस्त्वया कार्य एतदर्थं प्लवङ्गम4.18.61।। न वयं भवता चिन्त्या नाप्यात्मा हरिसत्तम। वयं भवद्विशेषेण धर्मतः कृतनिश्चयाः4.18.62।।
289.e: 'O best of monkeys, abandon all your anxiety on this score. Bother not about us or about yourself. Whatever has happened, has happened in consonance with dharma.

289.sa: न सन्तापस्त्वया कार्य एतदर्थं प्लवङ्गम4.18.61।। न वयं भवता चिन्त्या नाप्यात्मा हरिसत्तम। वयं भवद्विशेषेण धर्मतः कृतनिश्चयाः4.18.62।।
289.e: 'O best of monkeys, abandon all your anxiety on this score. Bother not about us or about yourself. Whatever has happened, has happened in consonance with dharma.

289.sa: दण्ड्ये यः पातयेद्दण्डं दण्ड्यो यश्चापि दण्ड्यते। कार्यकारणसिद्धार्था वुभौ तौ नावसीदतः4.18.63।।
289.e: 'The sinner and the punisher, whoever gives punishment and whoever receives it, are both regulated by the law of cause and effect. So do not despair.

289.sa: तद्भवान्दण्डसंयोगादस्माद्विगतकल्मषः। गतस्स्वां प्रकृतिं धर्म्यं धर्मदृष्टेन वर्त्मना4.18.64।।
289.e: 'You have been purged of your sin through punishment from the point of view of righteousness. You have regained your spiritual nature on the path of dharma.

289.sa: त्यज शोकं च मोहं च भयं च हृदये स्थितम्। त्वया विधानं हर्यग्र्य न शक्यमतिवर्तितुम्4.18.65।।
289.e: 'O best of monkeys remove sorrow from your heart, delusion and fear. It is not possible for you to transgress fate.

289.sa: यथा त्वय्यङ्गदो नित्यं वर्तते वानरेश्वर। तथा वर्तेत सुग्रीवे मयि चापि न संशयः4.18.66।।
289.e: 'O lord of monkeys Angada will remain with Sugriva and with me as he used to live with you. Rest assured.'

289.sa: स तस्य वाक्यं मधुरं महात्मन स्समाहितं धर्मपथानुवर्तिनः। निशम्य रामस्य रणावमर्दिनो वचस्सुयुक्तं निजगाद वानरः4.18.67।।
289.e: Having listened to the sweet, wellcomposed words of great Rama, a crusher of the enemy in war ,follower of righteous path, Vali replied in appropriate manner:

289.sa: शराभितप्तेन विचेतसा मया प्रदूषितस्त्वं यदजानता प्रभो। इदं महेन्द्रोपम भीमविक्रम प्रसादितस्त्वं क्षम मे नरेश्वर4.18.68।।
289.e: 'Pray, O mighty prince, hero of immense valour, pardon me for the words of blame I unwittingly hurled at you. I said all that in excruciating pain caused by your mighty arrow and in confusion of what is right and what is wrong.' इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये किष्किन्धाकाण्डे अष्टादशस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the eighteenth sarga of Kishkindakanda of the Holy Ramayana, the first epic, composed by sage Valmiki.

290.sa: स वानरमहाराजश्शयानश्शरविक्षतः। प्रत्युक्तो हेतुमद्वाक्यैर्नोत्तरं प्रत्यपद्यत4.19.1।।
290.e: The king of monkeys lying on the ground struck by the arrow did not offer to reply after listening to Rama's appropriate answers (to his objections).

290.sa: अश्मभिः प्रविभिन्नाङ्गः पादपैराहतो भृशम्। रामबाणेन चाक्रान्तो जीवितान्ते मुमोह सः4.19.2।।
290.e: Severely battered by stones, hit by trees and pierced by Rama's arrow, Vali lost consciousness as the end of his life was nearing.

290.sa: तं भार्या बाणमोक्षेण रामदत्तेन संयुगे। हतं प्लवगशार्दूलं तारा शुश्राव वालिनम्4.19.3।।
290.e: Tara, wife of Vali, heard that her husband, tiger among monkeys, was killed in the battle by the arrow discharged by Rama.

290.sa: सा सपुत्राप्रियं श्रुत्वा वधं भर्तुस्सुदारुणम्। निष्पपात भृशं तस्माद्विविधा गिरिगह्वरात्4.19.4।।
290.e: Hearing the terrible, unhappy news of her husband's death, Tara anxiously rushed along with her son out of the mountain cave.

290.sa: ये त्वङ्गदपरीवारा वानरा भीमविक्रमाः। ते सकार्मुकमालोक्य रामं त्रस्ताः प्रदुद्रुवुः4.19.5।।
290.e: Alarmed at the sight of Rama holding the bow, the terribly courageous monkeys who followed Angada as his bodyguards ran in different directions.

290.sa: सा ददर्श ततस्त्रस्तान्हरीनापततो भृशम्। यूथादिव परिभ्रष्टान्मृगान्निहतयूथपान्4.19.6।।
290.e: Tara saw the terrorstricken monkeys running helterskelter, like the herd of deer whose leader who had strayed had been killed.

290.sa: तानुवाच समासाद्य दुःखितान्दुखिता सती। रामवित्रासितान्सर्वाननुबद्धानिवेषुभिः4.19.7।।
290.e: Sorrowful Tara, the wife of Vali, duly approaching the monkeys stricken with grief and running as if chased by the arrows of Rama at their back, said to them:

290.sa: वानराः राजसिंहस्य यस्य यूयं पुरस्सराः। तं विहाय सुसन्त्रस्ताः कस्माद्द्रवथ दुर्गताः4.19.8।।
290.e: 'O monkeys deserting the lion among kings,whose servants you are ? What should you  be frightened for ? Why run away in distress?

290.sa: राज्यहेतोस्स चेद्भ्राता भ्रात्रा रौद्रेण पातितः। रामेण प्रहितैरौद्रैर्मार्गणैर्दूरपातिभिः4.19.9।।
290.e: 'If the (elder) brother is struck down by his (younger) brother in anger for the sake of kingship using farreaching arrows discharged by Rama, why are you running?'

290.sa: कपिपत्न्या वचश्श्रुत्वा कपयः कामरूपिणः। प्राप्तकालमविक्लिष्टमूचुर्वचनमङ्गनाम्4.19.10।।
290.e: On hearing Tara, the wife of Vali, the monkeys who could assume any form at their will replied with clear words appropriate to the occasion:

290.sa: जीवपुत्रे निवर्तस्व पुत्रं रक्षस्व चाङ्गदम्। अन्तको रामरूपेण हत्वा नयति वालिनम्4.19.11।।
290.e: 'O mother, your son is still alive. Go back and protect your son Angada. Lord of death in the form of Rama has come and killed Vali and is carrying him away.

290.sa: क्षिप्तान् वृक्षान्समाविध्य विपुलाश्च शिलास्तथा। वाली वज्रसमैर्बाणै रामेण विनिपातितः4.19.12।।
290.e: 'Rama smashed the trees and stones Vali hurled at him and then struck him down with thunderboltlike arrows.

290.sa: अभिद्रुतमिदं सर्वं विद्रुतं प्रसृतं बलम्। अस्मिन् प्लवगशार्दूले हते शक्रसमप्रभे4.19.13।।
290.e: 'When Vali who was equal to Indra in strength, a tiger among monkeys, was killed, the army of monkeys got terrified and ran away here and there, scattered in different directions.

290.sa: रक्ष्यतां नगरद्वारमङ्गदश्चाभिषिच्यताम्। पदस्थं वालिनः पुत्रं भजिष्यन्ति प्लवङ्गमाः4.19.14।।
290.e: 'Let the gate of the city be shut and Vali's son be consecrated as king. All the monkeys will serve him when he assumes power.

290.sa: अथवाऽरुचितं स्थानमिह ते रुचिरानने। आविशन्ति हि दुर्गाणि क्षिप्रमन्यानि वानराः4.19.15।।
290.e: 'O lovely Tara, this very day other monkeys will soon occupy our citadels.

290.sa: अभार्याश्च सभार्याश्च सन्त्यत्र वनचारिणः। लुब्धेभ्यो विप्रयुक्तेभ्यस्तेभ्यो नस्तुमुलं भयम्4.19.16।।
290.e: 'There are monkeys wandering in the forest (sent away by Vali). Some of them have made others' wives their own and some have been separated from their wives. They are a great cause of fear.'

290.sa: अल्पान्तरगतानां तु श्रुत्वा वचनमङ्गना। आत्मनः प्रतिरूपं सा बभाषे चारुहासिनी4.19.17।।
